52	class Collateral:
53	    """D-30, plan time and apply time.
54	
55	    The same `protected` set answers both, which is the point: a package classified manual at
56	    plan time and a package the apply-time guard refuses to lose must be the same package, or
57	    the review asked about something other than what the guard enforces.
58	    """
59	
60	    def __init__(
61	        self,
62	        *,
63	        target: RemoteExecutor,
64	        machines: Machines,
65	        target_manual_set: frozenset[str],
66	        origins: OriginClassifier,
67	    ) -> None:
68	        self._target = target
69	        self._machines = machines
70	        # The target's `apt-mark showmanual` set: the single source of the auto-versus-manual
71	        # split (D-30). A collateral package the simulation would remove or downgrade is
72	        # manual (the user chose it -> a review item) if it is in this set, auto (apt's own
73	        # dependency -> proceed silently) if it is not. Consulted at plan time by `classify`
74	        # and at apply time by the converge guards, which must agree.
75	        self._target_manual_set = target_manual_set
76	        self._origins = origins
77	        # Package names of every manual-collateral item the user let go ahead, computed from
78	        # the collateral group's decisions. The apply-time guard lets a removal/downgrade of
79	        # one of these through; every other manual collateral stays refused (D-30 — the last
80	        # line of defence behind plan-time classification).
81	        self._approved: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
82	        # Each collateral item's `item_id` -> the install/remove item_ids whose OWN
83	        # transaction reproduces it (`for_direction` narrows the batch down to them).
84	        # Used to translate a `skip` decision on a collateral item into `SKIP_ONCE` on exactly
85	        # those, so a declined collateral leaves them unapproved rather than failing them at
86	        # the apply-time guard — and cancels nothing else.
87	        self._trigger_ids: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {}
88	
89	    @property
90	    def approved(self) -> frozenset[str]:
91	        return self._approved

93	    def protected(self) -> frozenset[str]:
94	        """Packages a collateral removal/downgrade must not silently touch: the TARGET's
95	        `apt-mark showmanual` set alone (ADR-020 D-40).
96	
97	        The source's manual set is deliberately NOT unioned in, and the case that gives up
98	        is knowingly accepted rather than overlooked: a package the user installed by hand
99	        on the source, which arrives on the target as an automatic dependency, can now be
100	        removed as collateral without a prompt. If the target's apt installed it
101	        automatically, the target's apt owns it, and reclaiming it as a user choice on the
102	        strength of the OTHER machine's bookkeeping is a guess. The narrower set is also
103	        the set apt itself consults, so "manually installed" means the same thing to
104	        pc-switcher and to apt on the machine being changed.
105	
106	        The machine-specific decision list is still not consulted (D-30, accepted
107	        limitation, unchanged).
108	        """
109	        return self._target_manual_set

111	    async def plan_time(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
112	        """One BATCHED simulation per direction — the whole install candidate set, the whole
113	        removal candidate set — not one per package (D-30).
114	
115	        Each simulation's would-remove/would-downgrade collateral is split by `classify`
116	        against the target's manual set: auto collateral produces nothing (apt's own
117	        business, D-30), manual collateral becomes a review item.
118	
119	        The install rehearsal covers only the candidates the target's apt can resolve TODAY
120	        (`OriginClassifier.target_resolvable`); see there for what that costs and what still
121	        covers it.
122	        """
123	        # APT_PACKAGE only: a hold item (`apt:hold:`) shares the INSTALL/REMOVE actions
124	        # but is dpkg selection state, not an apt-get transaction, so it drives no
125	        # collateral simulation and its id is not a package id (#208).
126	        pkg = [d for d in diffs if d.item_class == ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE]
127	        install_diffs = [d for d in pkg if d.action == DiffAction.INSTALL]
128	        install_names = [package_name(d.item_id) for d in install_diffs]
129	        remove_names = [package_name(d.item_id) for d in pkg if d.action == DiffAction.REMOVE]
130	        # Every package this run already asks about, resolvable or not: one of them turning up
131	        # in another's transaction is a decision the user is taking anyway, not collateral.
132	        reviewed_names = frozenset(install_names) | frozenset(remove_names)
133	        rehearsed = [package_name(d.item_id) for d in install_diffs if self._origins.target_resolvable(d.item_id)]
134	
135	        # A removal candidate is by definition installed on the target, so apt can always
136	        # resolve it and that set is never narrowed.
137	        collateral: list[ItemDiff] = []
138	        if rehearsed:
139	            collateral.extend(await self.for_direction(rehearsed, reviewed_names, install_args, verb="Installing"))
140	        if remove_names:
141	            collateral.extend(await self.for_direction(remove_names, reviewed_names, remove_args, verb="Removing"))
142	        return collateral
143	
144	    async def for_direction(
145	        self,
146	        candidates: Sequence[str],
147	        reviewed_names: frozenset[str],
148	        args_for: Callable[[Sequence[str]], str],
149	        *,
150	        verb: str,
151	    ) -> list[ItemDiff]:
152	        """One direction's collateral: the batched rehearsal, then — only if it found
153	        manual collateral — the narrowing that says WHICH candidates cause each item.
154	
155	        Attribution matters because `skip` cancels the candidates recorded against the item:
156	        blaming the whole batch would make one collateral question cancel every package in it,
157	        including packages whose own transaction never touches the collateral. The batch alone
158	        cannot say — apt reports the transaction, not its causes — so each candidate is
159	        rehearsed on its own and blamed for the collateral its own transaction reproduces.
160	
161	        The cost is one extra `apt-get --dry-run` per candidate, paid ONLY by a run whose
162	        batch found manual collateral, and never by the common clean run. A single candidate
163	        is its own answer and is not rehearsed twice.
164	
165	        Collateral that no single candidate reproduces is jointly caused (apt removes what
166	        depends on `a | b` only once BOTH go) and is attributed to the whole batch — the
167	        conservative answer, and the only true one.
168	        """
169	        preview = await simulate_apt_transaction(self._target, args_for(candidates), login_shell=False)
170	        found = await self.classify(preview, reviewed_names)
171	        if not found:
172	            return []
173	
174	        triggers = {item.package: frozenset(candidates) for item in found}
175	        if len(candidates) > 1:
176	            narrowed: dict[str, set[str]] = {item.package: set() for item in found}
177	            for candidate in candidates:
178	                alone = await simulate_apt_transaction(self._target, args_for([candidate]), login_shell=False)
179	                for item in await self.classify(alone, reviewed_names):
180	                    if item.package in narrowed:
181	                        narrowed[item.package].add(candidate)
182	            triggers = {name: frozenset(blamed) or frozenset(candidates) for name, blamed in narrowed.items()}
183	
184	        return [
185	            self._item(
186	                item,
187	                build_trigger_phrase(triggers[item.package], candidates),
188	                verb,
189	                frozenset(f"{APT_PACKAGE_ID_PREFIX}{trigger}" for trigger in triggers[item.package]),
190	            )
191	            for item in found
192	        ]
193	
194	    async def classify(self, preview: AptTransactionPreview, reviewed_names: frozenset[str]) -> list[CollateralEffect]:
195	        """Partition a simulation's would-remove/would-downgrade packages by origin
196	        (D-30): a package in the TARGET's manual set becomes a manual-collateral review
197	        item (ADR-020 D-40); one outside it is auto-installed — apt's own dependency — and
198	        produces nothing, not even a report line the user cannot act on.
199	
200	        A downgrade is detected exactly as before: an `install_versions` entry with a
201	        non-`None` old version and `compare_deb_versions(target, new, old) < 0`.
202	
203	        Returns `CollateralEffect`s rather than `ItemDiff`s because the caller must
204	        attribute them before any of it can be phrased: only the caller knows which
205	        candidates to put in front of the effect.
206	        """
207	        protected = self.protected()
208	        collateral: list[CollateralEffect] = []
209	
210	        for pkg in preview.removals:
211	            if pkg in reviewed_names or pkg not in protected:
212	                continue
213	            collateral.append(CollateralEffect(pkg, "remove", f"remove {pkg}", f"{pkg} is removed as well"))
214	
215	        for pkg, (old_version, new_version) in preview.install_versions.items():
216	            if pkg in reviewed_names or old_version is None or pkg not in protected:
217	                continue
218	            if await compare_deb_versions(self._target, new_version, old_version) < 0:
219	                collateral.append(
220	                    CollateralEffect(
221	                        pkg,
222	                        "downgrade",
223	                        f"downgrade {pkg} from {old_version} to {new_version}",
224	                        f"{pkg} is downgraded from {old_version} to {new_version} as well",
225	                    )
226	                )
227	
228	        return collateral
229	
230	    def _item(self, effect: CollateralEffect, trigger: str, verb: str, trigger_ids: frozenset[str]) -> ItemDiff:
231	        """Build one manual-collateral `ItemDiff` and record the candidates it gates.
232	
233	        The screen's two answers are phrased HERE because this is the only layer that knows
234	        what causes the collateral: the act answer reads "install sl on nomad, so fortunes
235	        is removed as well", and the next item's cause may be a removal instead. `verb` is
236	        the direction of the change under review ("Installing"/"Removing"), not what happens
237	        to the collateral package.
238	        """
239	        target = self._machines.target
240	        causing = "install" if verb == "Installing" else "remove"
241	        diff = collateral_diff(
242	            effect.package,
243	            f"{verb} {trigger} on {target} would {effect.phrase}",
244	            act_word=effect.act_word,
245	            answer_hints=(
246	                f"{causing} {trigger} {'on' if causing == 'install' else 'from'} {target}, so {effect.sentence}",
247	                f"keep {effect.package} on {target}; {trigger} will not be "
248	                f"{'installed' if causing == 'install' else 'removed'}; will be asked again next sync",
249	            ),
250	        )
251	        self._trigger_ids[diff.item_id] = trigger_ids
252	        return diff
253	
254	    def approved_removals(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]) -> frozenset[str]:
255	        """Package names of every `REMOVE`-action diff this run's decisions approved.
256	
257	        The removal guard's rule is "removes nothing the user did not approve", not
258	        "removes nothing else" — removing a package legitimately removes things that
259	        depend on it, so the guard needs to know the full approved-removal set, not
260	        just the one item currently converging.
261	        """
262	        return frozenset(
263	            package_name(diff.item_id)
264	            for diff in diffs
265	            if diff.item_class == ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE
266	            and diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE
267	            and decisions.get(diff.item_id) == Decision.APPLY
268	        )
269	
270	    def resolve(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> ReviewOutcome:
271	        """Translate the manual-collateral group's decisions (D-30) into the guard's
272	        approved set and the triggering installs' decisions.
273	
274	        For each collateral item (`apt:collateral:<pkg>`): an `APPLY` (go ahead)
275	        marks `<pkg>` approved, so the install/remove guards let its removal
276	        or downgrade through; a `SKIP_ONCE` (skip) is propagated to the packages whose own
277	        transaction causes that collateral (`for_direction`'s attribution), so each is cleanly
278	        left unapproved rather than attempted and refused at the guard. Abort never reaches
279	        here — it raised `SyncAbortedByUser` inside the review.
280	
281	        Only an `APPLY` is overridden. A trigger the user already declined needs no
282	        cancelling, and overriding a `SKIP_ALWAYS` would silently discard the "never offer
283	        again on this machine" mark it carries: `_record_permanent_skips` reads this same
284	        decisions map, so the mark would never be written and the user would be asked again
285	        next run having been told otherwise.
286	
287	        Returns the outcome with any triggering decisions overridden; leaves the
288	        decisions map untouched when there is no collateral to resolve.
289	        """
290	        approved: set[str] = set()
291	        overrides: dict[str, Decision] = {}
292	        for diff in diffs:
293	            if not is_collateral_diff(diff):
294	                continue
295	            decision = outcome.decisions.get(diff.item_id)
296	            if decision == Decision.APPLY:
297	                approved.add(collateral_name(diff.item_id))
298	            elif decision == Decision.SKIP_ONCE:
299	                for trigger_id in self._trigger_ids.get(diff.item_id, frozenset()):
300	                    if outcome.decisions.get(trigger_id) == Decision.APPLY:
301	                        overrides[trigger_id] = Decision.SKIP_ONCE
302	
303	        self._approved = frozenset(approved)
304	        if not overrides:
305	            return outcome
306	        return ReviewOutcome(
307	            decisions={**outcome.decisions, **overrides},
308	            was_interactive=outcome.was_interactive,
309	            snippets=outcome.snippets,
310	            unresolved=outcome.unresolved,
311	        )

1	"""How this job talks to apt: the argument strings it builds, the output it parses, and
2	what "apt did not answer" means for each.
3	
4	The arguments are built here and nowhere else so the plan-time rehearsal, the apply-time
5	rehearsal and the real command cannot drift apart and rehearse a transaction other than the
6	one that runs. The parsers are here for the same reason the arguments are: a shape apt
7	prints is one fact, and two readers of it would disagree eventually.
8	"""

10	from __future__ import annotations
11

22	# Binaries this job runs under sudo, quoted back to the user when the passwordless-sudo
23	# check fails. A lower bound on what must be permitted, not an exact scope (ADR-013).
24	# The source is only ever read, so it needs just the /etc/apt digest capture and the
25	# conflict-review `cat` of a file the two machines disagree about.
26	SOURCE_SUDO_COMMANDS = ("/usr/bin/find", "/usr/bin/sha256sum", "/usr/bin/test", "/usr/bin/cat")
27	TARGET_SUDO_COMMANDS = (
28	    "/usr/bin/apt-get",
29	    "/usr/bin/apt-mark",
30	    "/usr/bin/find",
31	    "/usr/bin/sha256sum",
32	    "/usr/bin/test",
33	    "/usr/bin/cat",

35	    "/usr/bin/cp",

37	    "/usr/bin/fuser",

40	# Matches one `apt-get --dry-run` transaction line: `Inst <name> [<old>] (<new> ...)` for an
41	# install/upgrade (the `[<old>]` bracket only appears when a version is already
42	# installed), or `Remv <name> [<old>]` for a removal. Parsed by leading verb token and
43	# named groups rather than fixed column positions — the rest of an apt-get --dry-run line's
44	# shape varies with the package and its dependency resolution.
45	_TRANSACTION_LINE_RE = re.compile(
46	    r"^(?P<verb>Inst|Remv)\s+(?P<name>\S+)"
47	    r"(?:\s+\[(?P<old_version>[^\]]+)\])?"
48	    r"(?:\s+\((?P<new_version>[^\s)]+)\)?)?"
49	)
50

52	def lines(output: str) -> list[str]:
53	    """Non-blank, stripped lines — the shape every `apt-mark`/`find` list command in
54	    this job produces."""
55	    return [line.strip() for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]

58	def require_apt_answer(command: str, result: CommandResult, host: Host, *, blocks: int | None = None) -> None:
59	    """`require_answer` with apt's own evidence for what "did not answer" means (ADR-022).
60	
61	    Two conditions, and no others, mean apt did not answer:
62	
63	    * a NON-ZERO EXIT. Measured in a stock `ubuntu:24.04`: `apt-cache policy` exits 0 for a
64	      name it has never heard of, and 100 when it cannot read the sources at all. So a
65	      non-zero exit is never a statement about a package.
66	    * `blocks == 0` where the caller knows at least one block was owed. apt prints exactly
67	      one block per name it knows (measured on the development machine: 152 blocks for a
68	      152-name `apt-mark showmanual` set), so no blocks at all over names apt must know
69	      means the output is not apt's answer. Callers therefore pass `blocks` only where a
70	      block is genuinely owed: a name installed on the machine being asked, or one this run
71	      has already established the machine has a candidate for. A caller asking about names
72	      the machine may legitimately never have heard of passes nothing.
73	    """
74	    require_answer(command, result, host, answers=blocks, answer_noun="package block")

77	def install_args(names: Sequence[str]) -> str:
78	    """The apt-get arguments for installing `names`, shared by the plan-time rehearsal, the
79	    apply-time rehearsal and the real command, so no pair of them can drift apart and
80	    rehearse a transaction other than the one that runs."""
81	    return f"install --assume-yes --no-install-recommends {' '.join(shlex.quote(name) for name in names)}"
82	
83	
84	def remove_args(names: Sequence[str]) -> str:
85	    """`install_args`' counterpart for the removal direction."""
86	    return f"remove --assume-yes {' '.join(shlex.quote(name) for name in names)}"

89	def policy_command(names: Sequence[str]) -> str:
90	    """One batched `apt-cache policy` over `names` — never one call per package, and never
91	    one call per question the output answers."""
92	    return f"apt-cache policy {' '.join(shlex.quote(name) for name in names)}"

95	async def compare_deb_versions(executor: Executor, left: str, right: str) -> int:
96	    """Compare two Debian package version strings, `sorted`-comparator convention.
97	
98	    Returns negative when `left` < `right`, zero when equal, positive when `left` >
99	    `right`. Not hand-rolled: Debian version ordering has epoch, tilde and revision
100	    tie-breaking rules that are neither lexicographic nor PEP 440 — only dpkg's own
101	    comparator correctly ranks an epoch-bearing version like `2:1.0` above `10.0`
102	    (RESEARCH Don't Hand-Roll). Shells out through `executor` (never assumes a local
103	    `dpkg`, since the target's version may need comparing against its own dpkg) with
104	    `shlex.quote` on both operands (ASVS V5, T-02-01). Short-circuits to equal for
105	    byte-identical strings so the common "nothing changed" case costs no subprocess.
106	    """
107	    if left == right:
108	        return 0
109	
110	    quoted_left = shlex.quote(left)
111	    quoted_right = shlex.quote(right)
112	
113	    lt_result = await executor.run_command(f"dpkg --compare-versions {quoted_left} lt {quoted_right}")
114	    if lt_result.success:
115	        return -1
116	
117	    gt_result = await executor.run_command(f"dpkg --compare-versions {quoted_left} gt {quoted_right}")
118	    if gt_result.success:
119	        return 1
120	
121	    return 0
122	
123	
124	@dataclass(frozen=True)
125	class AptTransactionPreview:
126	    """The parsed result of `apt-get --dry-run <args>` — what apt says it WOULD do.
127	
128	    `apt-get --dry-run` is the only honest answer to "what will this command do": apt resolves
129	    dependencies and conflicts at run time, so the package the user ticked and the
130	    transaction apt actually runs are not necessarily the same thing.
131	
132	    `install_versions` maps a package apt would `Inst` to `(currently_installed_version
133	    | None, candidate_version)` — the currently-installed version is `None` for a fresh
134	    install (no `[...]` bracket in the line), present for an upgrade/downgrade. This is
135	    what the downgrade guard compares via `compare_deb_versions` rather than assuming
136	    every `Inst` line is a new install.
137	    """
138	
139	    installs: tuple[str, ...]
140	    removals: tuple[str, ...]
141	    raw: str
142	    install_versions: Mapping[str, tuple[str | None, str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
143	
144	
145	async def simulate_apt_transaction(
146	    executor: RemoteExecutor, apt_args: str, *, login_shell: bool | None = False
147	) -> AptTransactionPreview:
148	    """Run `apt-get --dry-run <apt_args>` on `executor` and parse its Inst/Remv action lines.
149	
150	    No `sudo` is needed: simulation is read-only. Raises `ConvergeItemFailed` if the
151	    simulation itself fails: a failed `apt-get --dry-run` typically prints no Inst/Remv
152	    lines, which would otherwise parse as an indistinguishable-from-clean empty preview and
153	    let both call sites proceed with a real command whose simulation was never actually
154	    trustworthy (WR-01) — refuse rather than silently degrade.
155	
156	    `ConvergeItemFailed` and not `ProbeFailed`, which is the deliberate boundary of ADR-022
157	    D-01: apt gives this command ONE failure code for both categories. Measured in a stock
158	    `ubuntu:24.04`, a name apt cannot locate exits 100 with `E: Unable to locate package`,
159	    which is byte-for-byte the exit code a held dpkg lock produces, and no rewrite of the
160	    command's SYNTAX separates them — apt offers no second code and no second mode.
161	
162	    Apply time simulates one approved install or removal, where apt's refusal is a fact
163	    about that request (ADR-020 D-27). Plan time removes the ambiguity from its ARGUMENTS
164	    instead: it rehearses only names the target's `apt-cache policy` gave a candidate for
165	    (`origins.OriginClassifier.target_resolvable`), so "unable to locate" is not among the
166	    failures it can meet. What remains there — a lock, a broken apt, an unresolvable
167	    candidate set — has no per-item loop to be reported against, so it aborts the plan, which
168	    is correct: a rehearsal that did not happen must not read as a clean one.
169	    """
170	    result = await executor.run_command(f"apt-get --dry-run {apt_args}", login_shell=login_shell)
171	    if not result.success:
172	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(f"apt-get --dry-run {apt_args} failed: {result.stderr.strip()}")
173	    installs: list[str] = []
174	    removals: list[str] = []
175	    install_versions: dict[str, tuple[str | None, str]] = {}
176	    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
177	        match = _TRANSACTION_LINE_RE.match(line)
178	        if match is None:
179	            continue
180	        verb, name = match.group("verb"), match.group("name")
181	        if verb == "Inst":
182	            installs.append(name)
183	            new_version = match.group("new_version")
184	            if new_version is not None:
185	                install_versions[name] = (match.group("old_version"), new_version)
186	        elif verb == "Remv":
187	            removals.append(name)
188	    return AptTransactionPreview(
189	        installs=tuple(installs), removals=tuple(removals), raw=result.stdout, install_versions=install_versions
190	    )

49	@dataclass(frozen=True)
50	class FilenameDiff:
51	    """Filename-level classification of two `{filename: digest}` maps — the shared
52	    basis every one of the `/etc/apt/*` directories is compared with.
53	    """
54	
55	    missing: frozenset[str]

60	def diff_filenames(source_digests: Mapping[str, str], target_digests: Mapping[str, str]) -> FilenameDiff:
61	    source_names = frozenset(source_digests)
62	    target_names = frozenset(target_digests)
63	    changed = frozenset(name for name in source_names & target_names if source_digests[name] != target_digests[name])
64	    return FilenameDiff(missing=source_names - target_names, extra=target_names - source_names, changed=changed)

67	def diff_apt_packages(
68	    source_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
69	    target_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
70	    origin_plan: Mapping[str, OriginPlan],
71	    machines: Machines,
72	    source_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
73	    target_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
74	) -> list[ItemDiff]:
75	    """One diff per item id present on either side, source-then-target order,
76	    followed by the `apt:hold:` membership diffs (#208, D5/D8 — holds emitted AFTER
77	    package diffs so install lands before its hold once the diffs converge).
78	
79	    A HELD package (target hold set) has its install/upgrade action SUPPRESSED (a held
80	    package is never proposed for install/version change) but produces NO package-level
81	    report — the hold travels as its own `apt:hold:` item, so a held package is never
82	    double-reported. A PINNED package gets no echo of any kind: a pin's only job is
83	    deciding which origin wins, which D-35 checks against the target's real post-refresh
84	    state instead of guessing at it here. Otherwise:
85	
86	    - missing-on-target -> `MISSING_ON_TARGET`/`INSTALL` when the source's origin either
87	      already serves the target or can be made to (`OriginPlan.outcome`), else
88	      `REPO_UNAVAILABLE`/`REPORT_ONLY`. This is ADR-020 D-34: the package a target could
89	      satisfy from a DIFFERENT vendor is still an install, but one that carries the source's
90	      repository with it, and the review line names where it will come from.
91	    - extra-on-target -> `EXTRA_ON_TARGET`/`REMOVE`.
92	    - present on both, from vendors that do not overlap -> `ORIGIN_MISMATCH`/`REPORT_ONLY`,
93	      checked BEFORE the version comparison: two vendors' copies of one name have no common
94	      version scale, so "source has X, target has Y" would report a difference of degree
95	      where the real difference is of origin.
96	    - present on both with differing versions -> `VERSION_MISMATCH`/`REPORT_ONLY` (D-04:
97	      reported, never force-downgraded).
98	    - present on both, same vendor, same version -> no diff at all.
99	
100	    Hold membership (D2): source-held & target-not -> `AptHoldItem` INSTALL (hold);
101	    target-held & source-not -> REMOVE (unhold); held on both or neither -> no diff.
102	    """
103	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
104	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
105	
106	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
107	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
108	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
109	
110	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
111	    for item_id in seen:
112	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
113	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
114	
115	        if target_item is not None and target_item.name in target_hold_names:
116	            # Held on the target: suppress its install/version action entirely (a held
117	            # package must never be proposed for install/upgrade). No package-level
118	            # report — the `apt:hold:` item below carries the hold fact.
119	            continue
120	        elif source_item is not None and target_item is None:
121	            origins = origin_plan.get(item_id, OriginPlan())
122	            if origins.outcome() is OriginOutcome.UNREPLICABLE:
123	                diffs.append(
124	                    ItemDiff(
125	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
126	                        diff_class=DiffClass.REPO_UNAVAILABLE,
127	                        action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
128	                        item_id=item_id,
129	                        label=source_item.label(),
130	                        detail=build_repo_unavailable_detail(
131	                            source_item.name,
132	                            sorted(origins.source_origins),
133	                            origins.unavailable_cause(machines),
134	                            machines,
135	                        ),
136	                    )
137	                )
138	            else:
139	                diffs.append(
140	                    ItemDiff(
141	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
142	                        diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET,
143	                        action=DiffAction.INSTALL,
144	                        item_id=item_id,
145	                        label=source_item.label(),
146	                        detail=build_origin_detail(origins.vendor_source_origins),
147	                    )
148	                )
149	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
150	            diffs.append(
151	                ItemDiff(
152	                    item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
153	                    diff_class=DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
154	                    action=DiffAction.REMOVE,
155	                    item_id=item_id,
156	                    label=target_item.label(),
157	                    detail=None,
158	                )
159	            )
160	        elif is_origin_mismatch(origin_plan.get(item_id, OriginPlan())):
161	            origins = origin_plan[item_id]
162	            diffs.append(
163	                ItemDiff(
164	                    item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
165	                    diff_class=DiffClass.ORIGIN_MISMATCH,
166	                    action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
167	                    item_id=item_id,
168	                    label=target_item.label() if target_item is not None else item_id,
169	                    detail=build_origin_mismatch_detail(
170	                        origins.vendor_source_origins, origins.vendor_target_origins, machines
171	                    ),
172	                )
173	            )
174	        elif source_item is not None and target_item is not None and source_item.version != target_item.version:
175	            diffs.append(
176	                ItemDiff(
177	                    item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
178	                    diff_class=DiffClass.VERSION_MISMATCH,
179	                    action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
180	                    item_id=item_id,
181	                    label=target_item.label(),
182	                    detail=build_version_mismatch_detail(source_item.version, target_item.version, machines),
183	                )
184	            )
185	        # else: present on both, one vendor, equal versions, not held -> no diff.
186	
187	    # Hold membership diffs (#208, D2/D8): emitted AFTER every package diff so a
188	    # package install lands before its hold when both are approved.
189	    diffs.extend(diff_apt_holds(source_hold_names, target_hold_names))
190	    return diffs

193	def diff_apt_holds(source_hold_names: frozenset[str], target_hold_names: frozenset[str]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
194	    """`apt:hold:` membership diffs (#208, D2): source-held & target-not -> INSTALL
195	    (hold); target-held & source-not -> REMOVE (unhold); held on both or on neither
196	    -> no diff. `sorted` for a stable, deterministic review order.
197	    """
198	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
199	    for name in sorted(source_hold_names | target_hold_names):
200	        in_source = name in source_hold_names
201	        in_target = name in target_hold_names
202	        if in_source == in_target:
203	            continue
204	        hold_item = AptHoldItem(name=name)
205	        diffs.append(
206	            ItemDiff(
207	                item_class=ItemClass.APT_HOLD,
208	                diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET if in_source else DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
209	                action=DiffAction.INSTALL if in_source else DiffAction.REMOVE,
210	                item_id=hold_item.item_id,
211	                label=hold_item.label(),
212	                detail=None,
213	            )
214	        )
215	    return diffs

236	async def diff_apt_pins(
237	    target_run: Run,
238	    source_digests: Mapping[str, str],
239	    target_digests: Mapping[str, str],
240	) -> tuple[list[ItemDiff], dict[str, str]]:
241	    """Pin-file diffs — the REMOVAL direction only — plus each offered file's content.
242	
243	    A pin the source has is written to the target when missing and overwritten when
244	    different, with no review line at all (ADR-020 D-36): a pin is what makes an origin win,
245	    in the same sense a signing key is what makes a repository trusted, and neither is
246	    something an approved package leaves the user a basis to judge. A pin naming an origin
247	    the target does not have is inert, so the always-sync rule cannot get the derivation
248	    wrong and costs nothing.
249	
250	    Deleting one is different, and that is why this direction survives: a pin the target has
251	    and the source does not is holding some origin above another on a machine the source
252	    knows nothing about, so removing it can flip which vendor supplies a package at the
253	    target's next upgrade — a consequence no approved package implies.
254	
255	    Which is exactly why the file's CONTENT is read here and returned alongside the diffs,
256	    keyed by filename: `99-vendor.pref` names no origin, no priority and no package, so a
257	    review row carrying only that filename asks the user to approve a change to which vendor
258	    supplies their software while showing them nothing about it. One `sudo cat` per file
259	    OFFERED for deletion — never per pin file that exists — and only on a run that found
260	    one. It is a read (`read_file_content`, ADR-022-guarded): silence there fails the job
261	    rather than showing an empty pin the user would approve deleting.
262	
263	    The content is deliberately not parsed. Pin syntax is small enough to read, and a
264	    rendered summary of it would be this module claiming to know which stanza wins.
265	    """
266	    names = diff_filenames(source_digests, target_digests)
267	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
268	    contents: dict[str, str] = {}
269	    for filename in sorted(names.extra):
270	        contents[filename] = await read_file_content(target_run, f"{APT_PREFERENCES_DIR}/{filename}", Host.TARGET)
271	        diffs.append(
272	            file_diff(
273	                AptPinItem(filename=filename, digest=target_digests[filename]),
274	                DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
275	                DiffAction.REMOVE,
276	            )
277	        )
278	    return diffs, contents

296	        detail = build_version_mismatch_detail(source_digests[filename], target_digests[filename], machines)
297	        diffs.append(file_diff(item, DiffClass.VERSION_MISMATCH, DiffAction.CHANGE, detail=detail))

301	async def diff_apt_sources(
302	    target_run: Run,
303	    source_digests: Mapping[str, str],
304	    target_digests: Mapping[str, str],
305	    machines: Machines,
306	    removal_details: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
307	) -> list[ItemDiff]:
308	    """Source-file diffs — the REMOVAL direction only (ADR-020 D-37).
309	
310	    Adding a repository is not a question. A source file lands on the target because a
311	    package approved on the review comes from it, so "package ticked, its repository
312	    unticked" is unrepresentable: the repository has no tick. Overwriting one that
313	    differs on the two machines is derived for the same reason. Both directions are
314	    built in `derived.DerivedWrites` instead, from the packages that need them.
315	
316	    Removal survives because nothing derives it: a repository the source no longer has
317	    is not implied by any approved package, and deleting it strands whatever the target
318	    still installs from it. `removal_details` carries the C26 impact text for a file
319	    whose deletion would strand machine-specific packages, keyed by filename —
320	    disclosure, not refusal, since removing a repository whose packages are also going
321	    is legitimate.
322	
323	    The URLs the file declares are named ahead of that impact text, because they are what
324	    the decision is actually about: a filename is somebody's naming convention, while
325	    `https://cli.github.com/packages` is the thing the machine would stop getting software
326	    from. They cost nothing — the file is already read here for its format, and
327	    `parse_source_file` returns the URIs from the same parse.
328	
329	    The distribution's own files are excluded outright (D-38): they are written and
330	    updated but never removed, so a target that has `ubuntu.sources` and a source that
331	    somehow does not must not turn into an offer to delete the target's archive.
332	    """
333	    details = removal_details or {}
334	    names = diff_filenames(source_digests, target_digests)
335	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
336	
337	    for filename in sorted(names.extra - DISTRO_SOURCE_FILENAMES):
338	        content = await read_file_content(target_run, f"{APT_SOURCES_DIR}/{filename}", Host.TARGET)
339	        fmt, _refs, uris = parse_source_file(filename, content)
340	        item = AptSourceItem(filename=filename, digest=target_digests[filename], fmt=fmt)
341	        diffs.append(
342	            ItemDiff(
343	                item_class=ItemClass.APT_SOURCE,
344	                diff_class=DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
345	                action=DiffAction.REMOVE,
346	                item_id=item.item_id,
347	                label=item.label(),
348	                detail=build_repo_removal_detail(uris, details.get(filename), machines),
349	            )
350	        )
351	
352	    return diffs

1	"""Where a package actually comes from, and whether the target can be given the same place
2	(ADR-020 D-34), plus the read-back that makes it a guarantee rather than a prediction (D-35).
3	
4	Two different jobs, deliberately in one module because they are two halves of one claim.
5	The classification decides which repository work to derive and what the review says; the
6	verification decides what may actually be installed, and only it sees the state the
7	derivation produced. Splitting them would let one drift from the other, which is exactly
8	the failure D-35 exists to catch.
9	"""

29	class OriginOutcome(StrEnum):
30	    """What the origin facts say can be done about one package missing on the target.
31	
32	    Three outcomes, not ADR-020 D-34's four: its classes 2 and 3 (the target has a candidate
33	    from the wrong vendor / the target has no candidate at all) differ only in what they
34	    look like, never in what happens — both install the package and both derive the source's
35	    repository first — so collapsing them keeps the diff from branching on a distinction
36	    that has no consequence.
37	    """
38	
39	    SAME_ORIGIN = "same_origin"
40	    """Class 1. Ordinary install, zero repository work — the target already offers the
41	    package from a place the source uses, or there is no origin fact to hold it to."""
42	
43	    REPLICABLE = "replicable"
44	    """Classes 2 and 3. Install, with the source's repository files derived from it."""
45	
46	    UNREPLICABLE = "unreplicable"
47	    """Class 4. `REPO_UNAVAILABLE`/`REPORT_ONLY` — the origin is declared by no writable
48	    file on the source, so the package can only be reported."""
49	
50	
51	@dataclass(frozen=True)
52	class OriginPlan:
53	    """Every origin fact one source package's classification turns on (ADR-020 D-34).
54	
55	    Assembled per package from facts about BOTH machines, because the question "can the
56	    target end up with this package from the same place the source has it?" is not
57	    answerable from either machine alone.
58	    """
59	
60	    source_origins: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
61	    """Origin URIs of the package's INSTALLED version on the source. Empty means apt named
62	    none for it, or printed no block at all — never evidence of anything (`df48cd07`)."""
63	
64	    source_files: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
65	    """The source's repository files declaring any of `source_origins`. Computed only for a
66	    package missing on the target, which is the only case that could make one travel."""
67	
68	    target_candidate_origins: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
69	    """Origin URIs of the version the TARGET would install. Empty means no repository on
70	    the target offers the name."""
71	
72	    target_candidate_known: bool = False
73	    """Whether apt printed a block for the name on the target AT ALL. Silence is not the
74	    same answer as `Candidate: (none)` and must never be read as one (`df48cd07`): the
75	    first is a question apt did not answer, including the case where the whole command
76	    failed; only the second is apt saying it will install nothing."""
77	
78	    vendor_source_origins: tuple[str, ...] = ()
79	    """`source_origins` minus the SOURCE's distribution origins, sorted. What the review
80	    names (ruling 9), and the left-hand side of the origin comparison (§2.6)."""
81	
82	    vendor_target_origins: tuple[str, ...] = ()
83	    """The package's INSTALLED origins on the target minus the TARGET's distribution
84	    origins, sorted. Filtered against the target's own distribution files so two machines
85	    on different Ubuntu mirrors do not read as two vendors."""
86	
87	    unwritable: str | None = None
88	    """Why no file serving `source_origins` can be written on the target, or `None` when at
89	    least one can. A file whose `Signed-By:` resolves to no key on the source is a
90	    repository apt would refuse on the target, so it cannot deliver the origin."""
91	
92	    def outcome(self) -> OriginOutcome:
93	        """Which of ADR-020 D-34's outcomes this package falls into.
94	
95	        The ladder is ordered by what it takes to be sure: a target candidate from an origin
96	        the source uses settles the question outright, and only after that does it matter
97	        whether the origin could be replicated at all.
98	        """
99	        if not self.source_origins:
100	            # apt named no repository origin for the source's installed version, or printed
101	            # no block for it at all. Absence is never evidence (`df48cd07`): with no origin
102	            # to replicate there is nothing to compare, so the question degrades to the
103	            # presence one this job asked before origins existed — and on that question the
104	            # target's silence still condemns nothing, only an explicit `Candidate: (none)`
105	            # does. A run whose policy call failed proposes the install and lets the install
106	            # report its own failure, rather than reporting a repository problem it never
107	            # established.
108	            refused = self.target_candidate_known and not self.target_candidate_origins
109	            return OriginOutcome.UNREPLICABLE if refused else OriginOutcome.SAME_ORIGIN
110	        if self.source_origins & self.target_candidate_origins:
111	            return OriginOutcome.SAME_ORIGIN
112	        if self.source_files and self.unwritable is None:
113	            return OriginOutcome.REPLICABLE
114	        return OriginOutcome.UNREPLICABLE
115	
116	    @property
117	    def derived_files(self) -> frozenset[str]:
118	        """The source repository files approving this package would make travel (ruling 4).
119	
120	        Empty for `SAME_ORIGIN`: the target already offers the package from a place the
121	        source uses, so nothing about `/etc/apt` has to change for the install to be
122	        faithful. Empty for `UNREPLICABLE` too — that package is reported, not installed,
123	        and deriving a repository for a report-only item would break ruling 4's "derived
124	        from the packages approved from it".
125	        """
126	        return self.source_files if self.outcome() is OriginOutcome.REPLICABLE else frozenset()
127	
128	    def unavailable_cause(self, machines: Machines) -> str:
129	        """Why the source's origin cannot be provided on the target — the second half of a
130	        `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` detail, after the origin itself.
131	        """
132	        if self.unwritable is not None:
133	            return self.unwritable
134	        if not self.source_origins:
135	            return f"apt on {machines.source} names no repository origin for it"
136	        return f"no repository file on {machines.source} declares it"
137

139	def is_origin_mismatch(plan: OriginPlan) -> bool:
140	    """Whether a package present on BOTH machines came from two different vendors (§2.6).
141	
142	    Both sides must name a vendor and the two sets must not overlap. A side with no vendor
143	    origin at all is served by the distribution, and the distribution is not a vendor — that
144	    suppression is the whole reason this can be asked of every package without two machines
145	    on different Ubuntu mirrors reporting every one of them as mismatched.
146	    """
147	    return (
148	        bool(plan.vendor_source_origins)
149	        and bool(plan.vendor_target_origins)
150	        and not (frozenset(plan.vendor_source_origins) & frozenset(plan.vendor_target_origins))
151	    )

154	class OriginClassifier:
155	    """D-34's classification over two machines' captured facts, and D-35's read-back."""
156	
157	    def __init__(
158	        self,
159	        *,
160	        machines: Machines,
161	        source_refs: SourceFileRefs,
162	        target_refs: SourceFileRefs,
163	        source_keys: KeyDigests,
164	    ) -> None:
165	        self._machines = machines
166	        self._source_refs = source_refs
167	        self._target_refs = target_refs
168	        self._source_keys = source_keys
169	        # One `OriginPlan` per source package item id, rebuilt whenever the package diff
170	        # is. It is what the diff classifies from and what the derived `/etc/apt` write set
171	        # is read out of, so it must describe the same run the accepted plan describes.
172	        self._plans: Mapping[str, OriginPlan] = {}
173	        # `{package name: refusal message}` for every approved install whose candidate on
174	        # the REAL post-`apt-get update` target comes from none of the source's origins
175	        # (D-35). `None` until the one batched verification runs; `{}` once it has run and
176	        # found nothing to refuse, which is what distinguishes "not yet checked" from
177	        # "checked, all clear" and keeps the call to exactly one per run.
178	        self._refusals: dict[str, str] | None = None
179	
180	    @property
181	    def plans(self) -> Mapping[str, OriginPlan]:
182	        return self._plans
183	
184	    def plan_for(self, item_id: str) -> OriginPlan:
185	        return self._plans.get(item_id, OriginPlan())
186	
187	    def classify(
188	        self,
189	        source_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
190	        target_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
191	        policy: TargetPolicy,
192	        source_origins: Mapping[str, frozenset[str]],
193	    ) -> Mapping[str, OriginPlan]:
194	        """One `OriginPlan` per source package, from facts already captured this run.
195	
196	        Distribution origins are resolved per machine (D-35) from that machine's own
197	        distribution source files, so a source on one Ubuntu mirror and a target on another
198	        agree that both are the distribution rather than two vendors.
199	        """
200	        source_distribution = self._source_refs.distribution_origins()
201	        target_distribution = self._target_refs.distribution_origins()
202	        on_target = {item.item_id for item in target_items}
203	
204	        plans: dict[str, OriginPlan] = {}
205	        for item in source_items:
206	            origins = source_origins.get(item.name, frozenset())
207	            # Only a package the target lacks can make a repository file travel, so the
208	            # file lookup is skipped for one present on both.
209	            files = self._source_refs.files_serving(origins) if item.item_id not in on_target else frozenset()
210	            target_installed = policy.installed_origins.get(item.name, frozenset())
211	            plans[item.item_id] = OriginPlan(
212	                source_origins=origins,
213	                source_files=files,
214	                target_candidate_origins=policy.candidate_origins.get(item.name, frozenset()),
215	                target_candidate_known=item.name in policy.candidate_origins,
216	                vendor_source_origins=tuple(sorted(origins - source_distribution)),
217	                vendor_target_origins=tuple(sorted(target_installed - target_distribution)),
218	                unwritable=self.unwritable_reason(files),
219	            )
220	        self._plans = plans
221	        return plans
222	
223	    def unwritable_reason(self, source_files: frozenset[str]) -> str | None:
224	        """Why none of `source_files` can be written on the target, or `None` when at least
225	        one can.
226	
227	        ONE writable file is enough: the origin only has to be declared once for the target
228	        to install from it, so a package served by both a sound repository file and a broken
229	        one is still replicable. The reported reason is the first broken file's, sorted, so
230	        the review text does not depend on dict order.
231	        """
232	        reasons: list[str] = []
233	        for filename in sorted(source_files):
234	            dangling = dangling_ref(self._source_refs.refs_of(filename), self._source_keys.filenames)
235	            if dangling is None:
236	                return None
237	            reasons.append(build_dangling_keyring_detail(filename, dangling, self._machines))
238	        return reasons[0] if reasons else None
239	
240	    def target_resolvable(self, item_id: str) -> bool:
241	        """Whether the target's apt named a version it would install for this package, from
242	        the batched `apt-cache policy` this run already ran (`AptProbe.collect_target_policy`).
243	
244	        The plan-time simulation's admission test, and a D-30 ruling rather than a detail. An
245	        ADR-020 D-34 class-3 install — the repository that supplies it is derived from the
246	        package's own approval and written during converge — is a name the target's apt
247	        cannot locate yet, and `apt-get --dry-run` refuses the WHOLE batch on it with the
248	        exit code a held dpkg lock also produces. Including such a name therefore does not
249	        weaken that one package's protection, it removes the protection from every other
250	        package in the run and aborts `plan()` before the user sees anything. The evidence
251	        used is the policy read, never the simulation's exit code, which cannot separate the
252	        two causes (ADR-022 D-01).
253	
254	        What is given up, deliberately: an excluded package gets NO plan-time collateral
255	        classification, because apt cannot say what it would remove for a package it cannot
256	        resolve — the facts the three-way go-ahead/keep/stop question needs do not
257	        exist yet. What still covers it is the per-item simulation the install converger runs
258	        after the `/etc/apt` unit has landed and `apt-get update` has run, so apt CAN
259	        resolve it there: unapproved manual collateral fails that one item (D-27) instead of
260	        being installed over. The residual cost is that the user is told afterwards rather
261	        than asked beforehand, and only for packages whose repository this run adds.
262	
263	        A package whose origin can never be replicated needs no rule here: it is
264	        `REPO_UNAVAILABLE`/`REPORT_ONLY`, so it is never an install candidate at all.
265	        """
266	        return bool(self.plan_for(item_id).target_candidate_origins)
267	
268	    async def refusal(
269	        self,
270	        name: str,
271	        *,
272	        diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff],
273	        decisions: Mapping[str, Decision],
274	        target: RemoteExecutor,
275	    ) -> str | None:
276	        """Why this approved install may not run, or `None` when its origin checks out
277	        (ADR-020 D-35) — the hard guarantee behind origin replication.
278	
279	        Plan-time classification decides what `/etc/apt` work to derive; only this decides
280	        what may be installed, because only it sees the state that derivation actually
281	        produced: a repository whose write failed, a pin that never landed, a vendor version
282	        the archive's epoch still outranks. It is therefore the check that makes "the target
283	        silently installs a different vendor's package" unreachable even when everything
284	        upstream of it is wrong.
285	
286	        ONE batched `apt-cache policy` for the whole approved set, computed on first use and
287	        cached — the answer cannot change between two installs of one run, and a per-package
288	        call would cost a full policy query per install. Reached from the install converger
289	        rather than from `apply()` so it is by construction after this run's single
290	        `apt-get update` (whichever of the two refresh paths issued it) and before the first
291	        install, which is the window in which the answer is about the converged target.
292	
293	        Packages whose source origins are all distribution origins never enter the set
294	        (D-35's exemption): two machines on different Ubuntu mirrors are not two vendors.
295	
296	        A name an ANSWERED probe printed no block for is refused like any other mismatch.
297	        That is deliberately stricter than the plan-time rule, where apt's silence condemns
298	        nothing (`df48cd07`): there, silence leaves the install to report its own failure;
299	        here the install IS the thing being guarded, and a guarantee that could not be
300	        evaluated has not been met. A probe that did not answer at all is a different thing
301	        and does not reach this refusal — `require_apt_answer` fails the run once instead,
302	        because "the environment broke" is not a finding about any package's origin.
303	        """
304	        if self._refusals is None:
305	            self._refusals = await self._verify(diffs, decisions, target)
306	        return self._refusals.get(name)
307	
308	    async def _verify(
309	        self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], decisions: Mapping[str, Decision], target: RemoteExecutor
310	    ) -> dict[str, str]:
311	        held_to: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {}
312	        for diff in diffs:
313	            if diff.item_class is not ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE or diff.action is not DiffAction.INSTALL:
314	                continue
315	            if decisions.get(diff.item_id) != Decision.APPLY:
316	                continue
317	            plan = self._plans.get(diff.item_id)
318	            # `vendor_source_origins` is `source_origins` minus the SOURCE's own distribution
319	            # files, so an empty tuple is exactly D-35's exemption. The intersection below is
320	            # against the FULL set: a package the source has from both a vendor and the
321	            # archive is faithfully replicated by either.
322	            if plan is None or not plan.vendor_source_origins:
323	                continue
324	            held_to[package_name(diff.item_id)] = plan.source_origins
325	
326	        if not held_to:
327	            return {}
328	
329	        command = policy_command(sorted(held_to))
330	        result = await target.run_command(command, login_shell=False)
331	        candidates = candidate_origins_by_package(result.stdout)
332	        # Every name here is an approved install with a vendor origin, so plan-time
333	        # classification already found either a target candidate (class 2) or a source
334	        # repository this run has since written (class 3) — apt owes a block for each.
335	        require_apt_answer(command, result, Host.TARGET, blocks=len(candidates))
336	        return {
337	            name: build_origin_refusal_detail(
338	                name, sorted(origins), sorted(candidates.get(name, frozenset())), self._machines
339	            )
340	            for name, origins in sorted(held_to.items())
341	            if not (candidates.get(name, frozenset()) & origins)
342	        }

1	"""Which `/etc/apt` files travel without a review line of their own, and who pays when one
2	fails to land (ADR-020 D-37/D-38/D-39).
3	
4	Three buckets, in the order they are written, and each is a different answer to "why does
5	this file travel":
6	
7	- every `/etc/apt/preferences.d` file the source has. A pin decides which origin wins, which
8	  is exactly what origin replication turns on; one naming an origin the target lacks is inert,
9	  so always-sync costs nothing and cannot get a derivation wrong.
10	- the distribution's own source files. The user wants both machines pointed at the same
11	  archive, and these are the files that say where it is.
12	- the repository files serving the approved installs, from each package's own `OriginPlan`
13	  (ruling 4). Nothing else makes a repository travel: one that feeds no package this run
14	  syncs stays where it is.
15	
16	A derived write has no item, so it cannot fail as one. It is recorded against its destination
17	and charged to every approved package whose origin depended on it (D-39) — the refusal lands
18	on the thing the user actually decided about, naming the file.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
24	
25	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.items import (
26	    APT_PREFERENCES_DIR,
27	    APT_SOURCES_DIR,
28	    APT_SOURCES_LIST,
29	    CONFLICT_ID_PREFIX,
30	    DISTRO_SOURCE_FILENAMES,
31	    source_file_destination,
32	)
33	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.origins import OriginClassifier
34	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.probe import OriginFacts, RepoFacts
35	from pcswitcher.jobs.packages.items import DiffAction, ItemClass, ItemDiff
36	from pcswitcher.jobs.packages.review import Decision
37	
38	
39	class DerivedWrites:
40	    """The `/etc/apt` write set the accepted decisions imply, and its failure bookkeeping."""
41	
42	    def __init__(
43	        self,
44	        *,
45	        source_origin_facts: OriginFacts,
46	        target_origin_facts: OriginFacts,
47	        source_repo_facts: RepoFacts,
48	        target_repo_facts: RepoFacts,
49	        origins: OriginClassifier,
50	    ) -> None:
51	        self._source_origin = source_origin_facts
52	        self._target_origin = target_origin_facts
53	        self._source_repo = source_repo_facts
54	        self._target_repo = target_repo_facts
55	        self._origins = origins
56	        self._pin_writes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
57	        self._distro_writes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
58	        self._repo_writes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
59	        # `{absolute destination: why it failed}`. A derived write fails no item of its own —
60	        # there is no item — so it is recorded here and charged to every approved package
61	        # that needed the file (D-39). A rollback puts EVERY derived write in here, matching
62	        # what it already does to the reviewed half of the group.
63	        self._failed: dict[str, str] = {}
64	        # `{package item_id: the derived destinations that package needs}`, the inverse
65	        # lookup D-39's attribution runs at install time.
66	        self._package_dests: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {}
67	
68	    @property
69	    def pin_writes(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
70	        return self._pin_writes
71	
72	    @property
73	    def distro_writes(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
74	        return self._distro_writes
75	
76	    @property
77	    def repo_writes(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
78	        return self._repo_writes
79	
80	    @property
81	    def failed(self) -> Mapping[str, str]:
82	        """`{destination: why it failed}` — read by the install refusal, and the one place a
83	        derived write's outcome is observable at all, since it has no item to fail."""
84	        return self._failed
85	
86	    def all_writes(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
87	        """Every derived destination, in the order the repository unit writes them: pins
88	        before sources (so a pin is in place the moment its origin becomes fetchable), the
89	        distribution's files before the vendors'."""
90	        return (*self._pin_writes, *self._distro_writes, *self._repo_writes)
91	
92	    def build(
93	        self,
94	        diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff],
95	        decisions: Mapping[str, Decision],
96	        *,
97	        conflicts: Mapping[str, object],
98	        withheld_esm: frozenset[str],
99	    ) -> None:
100	        """Turn the accepted decisions into the `/etc/apt` files this run writes WITHOUT a
101	        review line (ADR-020 D-37/D-38) — the counterpart to the reviewed half the repository
102	        unit carries.
103	
104	        Only files the target lacks or holds different bytes for are listed — an identical
105	        file needs no write and can therefore fail nothing. `_package_dests` records which
106	        packages each write serves, because a derived write has no item of its own to fail
107	        (D-39) and must charge its failure to the packages that needed it.
108	        """
109	        self._failed = {}
110	        self._package_dests = {}
111	
112	        def differs(source_digests: Mapping[str, str], target_digests: Mapping[str, str], filename: str) -> bool:
113	            return target_digests.get(filename) != source_digests[filename]
114	
115	        self._pin_writes = tuple(
116	            f"{APT_PREFERENCES_DIR}/{filename}"
117	            for filename in sorted(self._source_repo.pin_digests)
118	            if differs(self._source_repo.pin_digests, self._target_repo.pin_digests, filename)
119	        )
120	
121	        # A conflict the user declined is a file this run may NOT write (ruling 6). It is
122	        # seeded as a failed derived write rather than merely dropped, because a package
123	        # whose origin depended on it cannot be delivered and installing it anyway would put
124	        # the wrong vendor's software on the target — the one outcome D-34 exists to prevent.
125	        skipped = {
126	            source_file_destination(filename): (
127	                "the user chose to keep the target's version of this file for now (ADR-020 D-37)"
128	            )
129	            for filename in conflicts
130	            if decisions.get(f"{CONFLICT_ID_PREFIX}{filename}") != Decision.APPLY
131	        }
132	        self._failed = dict(skipped)
133	
134	        distro: list[str] = [
135	            f"{APT_SOURCES_DIR}/{filename}"
136	            for filename in sorted(
137	                (DISTRO_SOURCE_FILENAMES - withheld_esm) & frozenset(self._source_origin.source_digests)
138	            )
139	            if differs(self._source_origin.source_digests, self._target_origin.source_digests, filename)
140	        ]
141	        if (
142	            self._source_origin.sources_list_digest is not None
143	            and self._source_origin.sources_list_digest != self._target_origin.sources_list_digest
144	        ):
145	            distro.append(APT_SOURCES_LIST)
146	        self._distro_writes = tuple(dest for dest in distro if dest not in skipped)
147	
148	        repo: set[str] = {
149	            source_file_destination(filename)
150	            for filename in conflicts
151	            if decisions.get(f"{CONFLICT_ID_PREFIX}{filename}") == Decision.APPLY
152	        }
153	        for diff in diffs:
154	            if diff.item_class is not ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE or diff.action is not DiffAction.INSTALL:
155	                continue
156	            if decisions.get(diff.item_id) != Decision.APPLY:
157	                continue
158	            origin_plan = self._origins.plans.get(diff.item_id)
159	            if origin_plan is None:
160	                continue
161	            # The attribution set keeps a skipped conflict; the write list does not. That
162	            # asymmetry IS D-39's rule: the package still depended on the file.
163	            needed = {
164	                source_file_destination(filename)
165	                for filename in origin_plan.derived_files
166	                if self._target_origin.source_digests.get(filename) != self._source_origin.source_digests.get(filename)
167	            }
168	            if needed:
169	                repo.update(needed)
170	                self._package_dests[diff.item_id] = frozenset(needed)
171	        self._repo_writes = tuple(sorted(repo - frozenset(distro) - frozenset(skipped)))
172	
173	    def record_failure(self, dest: str, reason: str) -> None:
174	        self._failed[dest] = reason
175	
176	    def fail_all(self, message: str) -> None:
177	        """Mark every derived write failed — the rollback path (D-39).
178	
179	        The derived half needs the same treatment for the same reason a rollback fails items
180	        whose own write succeeded: what landed on the target is the pre-run state, so every
181	        package whose origin depended on one of those files must fail rather than install from
182	        wherever apt would now serve it.
183	        """
184	        for dest in self.all_writes():
185	            self._failed[dest] = message
186	
187	    def install_refusal(self, item_id: str, name: str) -> str | None:
188	        """Why this approved install may not run because a file it needed never landed
189	        (D-39), or `None` when every derived file it depends on is in place.
190	
191	        The attribution a derived write cannot make for itself: it has no item, so its
192	        failure has to be charged to the packages whose origin depended on it. Naming the
193	        file and the reason is what keeps "the install failed" from reading as an apt
194	        problem when it is a `/etc/apt` write problem.
195	        """
196	        for dest in sorted(self._package_dests.get(item_id, frozenset())):
197	            reason = self._failed.get(dest)
198	            if reason is not None:
199	                return f"install of {name} refused: {dest} was not written ({reason})"
200	        return None

2	
3	Writing the source's `ubuntu-esm-*` sources to a target with no Ubuntu Pro attachment is not
4	harmless: `esm.ubuntu.com` serves its INDEX publicly, so `apt-get update` succeeds and the ESM
5	suites win candidate selection, and the failure surfaces much later as a 401 on the `.deb` of
6	the target's next install of an ESM-covered package — a failure nobody traces back to a sync.
7	pc-switcher cannot attach the target itself, so it asks.
8	
9	Only the parsed `attached` boolean ever leaves this module: `pro status --format json` also
10	names the subscriber's account, so nothing else may be logged, shown or put in a
11	`JobSkipped` reason (D-38, and `PKG-FR-ESM-PRIVACY` is honoured by construction here rather
12	than by filtering downstream).
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import json
18	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
19	
20	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.items import ESM_SOURCE_FILENAMES
21	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.messages import build_esm_gate_message
22	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.probe import AptProbe
23	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.reporting import Log
24	from pcswitcher.jobs.context import JobContext
25	from pcswitcher.jobs.packages.items import Machines
26	from pcswitcher.models import Host, JobSkipped, LogLevel
27	
28	# `pro status --format json` exits 0 for an unprivileged user and reports a top-level
29	# `attached` boolean. Its payload ALSO names the subscriber's account, so only the parsed
30	# boolean may ever be logged, shown or put in a `JobSkipped` reason.
31	PRO_STATUS_COMMAND = "pro status --format json"
32	
33	
34	class EsmGate:
35	    """Ask before ESM sources travel to an unattached target, and remember what was withheld."""
36	
37	    def __init__(
38	        self,
39	        *,
40	        probe: AptProbe,
41	        machines: Machines,
42	        job_name: str,
43	        manager_id: str,
44	        log: Log,
45	    ) -> None:
46	        self._probe = probe
47	        self._machines = machines
48	        self._job_name = job_name
49	        self._manager_id = manager_id
50	        self._log = log
51	        # ESM sources the gate held back. Only ever non-empty under `--dry-run`: a real
52	        # unattached run raises `JobSkipped` instead of writing a subset (D-38).
53	        self._withheld: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
54	
55	    @property
56	    def withheld(self) -> frozenset[str]:
57	        return self._withheld
58	
59	    def pending(self, source_digests: Mapping[str, str], target_digests: Mapping[str, str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
60	        """The `ubuntu-esm-*` filenames this run's always-sync bucket would put on the
61	        target: present on the source, and absent or different there.
62	
63	        Same predicate the derived-write set applies to the whole distribution bucket,
64	        so the gate can never ask about a file the run would not have written.
65	        """
66	        return tuple(
67	            filename
68	            for filename in sorted(ESM_SOURCE_FILENAMES & frozenset(source_digests))
69	            if source_digests[filename] != target_digests.get(filename)
70	        )
71	
72	    def withhold(self, esm_files: Sequence[str]) -> None:
73	        """Record what a dry run would not have written, so the preview cannot claim writes no
74	        real run would make."""
75	        self._withheld = frozenset(esm_files)
76	
77	    async def attached(self) -> bool:
78	        """Whether the target reports an Ubuntu Pro attachment.
79	
80	        Every failure mode — no `pro` binary, a non-zero exit, output that will not parse —
81	        answers False, which is the recoverable one: False asks a question the user can
82	        answer, True writes files that break the target's next install.
83	
84	        The payload also carries the subscriber's account, so nothing but the parsed
85	        boolean leaves this method (D-38).
86	        """
87	        result = await self._probe.target_pro_attached(PRO_STATUS_COMMAND)
88	        if not result.success:
89	            return False
90	        try:
91	            payload = json.loads(result.stdout)
92	        except ValueError:
93	            return False
94	        return isinstance(payload, dict) and payload.get("attached") is True
95	
96	    async def allow(self, esm_files: Sequence[str], *, context: JobContext) -> bool:
97	        """Ask before putting `ubuntu-esm-*` sources on a target that is not Pro-attached
98	        (D-38), and return whether they may travel.
99	
100	        `context` is passed per call rather than held: the orchestrator injects the reviewer
101	        into `JobContext` after the job is constructed, and a `JobContext` is a frozen
102	        dataclass replaced wholesale when that happens — a gate holding the one it was built
103	        with would ask a reviewer that is no longer the run's.
104	
105	        Two real outcomes: True, the target is attached (possibly after the user attached it
106	        and this re-probed), so the files travel with the rest of the always-sync bucket;
107	        or `JobSkipped`, because the user chose to skip or nobody was there to answer. False
108	        is reachable only under `--dry-run`, where neither answer writes anything.
109	
110	        Skipping the whole job rather than withholding the two files is the user's ruling
111	        and the only coherent partial outcome: `/etc/apt/preferences.d` always-syncs with no
112	        derivation predicate, so the source's ESM pins land on the target whether or not the
113	        sources they name do, leaving a candidate selection that matches neither machine.
114	        Skipping leaves `/etc/apt` exactly as it was.
115	
116	        The re-check loop is deliberately unbounded — the user's ruling: re-probing is free,
117	        and the exit is choosing to skip.
118	        """
119	        if await self.attached():
120	            return True
121	
122	        named = ", ".join(esm_files)
123	        if context.dry_run:
124	            self._log(
125	                Host.TARGET,
126	                LogLevel.WARNING,
127	                f"[dry-run] {self._machines.target} reports no Ubuntu Pro attachment, so {named} would not be "
128	                f"written: a real run would skip {self._job_name} entirely and leave every other job running.",
129	            )
130	            return False
131	
132	        assert context.reviewer is not None, (
133	            f"{self._manager_id} sync has no reviewer; the orchestrator must inject one "
134	            "through JobContext.reviewer before plan()."
135	        )
136	        target = self._machines.target
137	        message = build_esm_gate_message(esm_files, self._machines, self._job_name)
138	        while True:
139	            answer = await context.reviewer.ask_gate(
140	                title=f"{target} needs an Ubuntu Pro attachment",
141	                message=message,
142	                proceed_label=f"I have attached {target} — check again and continue",
143	                stop_label=f"Skip {self._job_name} this run (every other job still runs)",
144	            )
145	            if answer is None:
146	                raise JobSkipped(
147	                    self._job_name,
148	                    f"the source carries {named} and the target reports no Ubuntu Pro attachment; "
149	                    "no TTY was available to ask whether to attach it or skip",
150	                )
151	            if not answer:
152	                raise JobSkipped(
153	                    self._job_name,
154	                    f"the source carries {named}, the target reports no Ubuntu Pro attachment, "
155	                    "and the user chose to skip rather than attach it",
156	                )
157	            if await self.attached():
158	                return True
159	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.WARNING, f"{target} still reports no Ubuntu Pro attachment.")

1	"""The `/etc/apt` unit: back up everything it will touch, write in apt's required order, run
2	ONE `apt-get update`, and roll the whole thing back if that refresh fails (T-02-34).
3	
4	Never partially, because a failed metadata refresh with some files written and others not
5	would leave `/etc/apt` in a configuration nobody reviewed.
6	
7	The unit is a MIX (ADR-020 D-39): reviewed items — repository and pin removals, apt config in
8	all three directions — and derived writes, which have no item and so no per-item outcome. A
9	derived write that fails is recorded against its destination and charged to the packages that
10	needed it; a rollback marks every derived write failed, exactly as it marks every reviewed one.
11	
12	Write order is apt's own (§3.3): keys, then pins and apt config, then the distribution's
13	sources, then the derived vendor repositories, then the approved removals, then unused-key
14	collection, then the single refresh.
15	
16	The base `apply()` loop calls `converge()` once per approved diff, so rather than doing each
17	item's work in ITS OWN call — which would make this transactionality impossible to express
18	without the base loop knowing about units — the FIRST repository-group (or metadata-refresh)
19	diff `converge()` sees triggers `ensure_converged`, which does the WHOLE unit's work right
20	then. Every subsequent call is a cache lookup against the per-item outcome that eager run
21	recorded, including outcomes for diffs `converge()` has not been called for yet, and outcomes
22	for diffs a rollback retroactively marks as failed even though their own write succeeded.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
28	from pathlib import Path
29	from uuid import uuid4
30	
31	from pcswitcher.executor import RemoteExecutor
32	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.derived import DerivedWrites
33	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.files import TargetFiles, backup_path_for, staged_name_for
34	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.items import (
35	    METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID,
36	    REMOVAL_CLASS_ORDER,
37	    REPO_GROUP_CLASSES,
