49	class EtcApt:
50	    """The repository unit, converged exactly once per run."""
51	
52	    def __init__(
53	        self,
54	        *,
55	        target: RemoteExecutor,
56	        files: TargetFiles,
57	        keyrings: Keyrings,
58	        derived: DerivedWrites,
59	        refresh: MetadataRefresh,
60	        log: Log,
61	    ) -> None:
62	        self._target = target
63	        self._files = files
64	        self._keyrings = keyrings
65	        self._derived = derived
66	        self._refresh = refresh
67	        self._log = log
68	        # Lazily computed the first time `converge()` sees a repository-group item
69	        # (pin/config/source, or the synthetic metadata-refresh marker): maps each such diff's
70	        # item_id to (succeeded, message). Populated all at once so the required
71	        # key-before-source write order and the transactional backup/rollback happen exactly
72	        # once per run, regardless of which order the base `apply()` loop's per-diff
73	        # `converge()` calls visit them in.
74	        self._outcome: dict[str, tuple[bool, str]] | None = None
75	
76	    async def converge_item(
77	        self, diff: ItemDiff, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]
78	    ) -> CommandResult:
79	        await self.ensure_converged(diffs, decisions)
80	        assert self._outcome is not None
81	        succeeded, message = self._outcome[diff.item_id]
82	        if succeeded:
83	            return CommandResult(exit_code=0, stdout=message, stderr="")
84	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(message)
85	
86	    @staticmethod
87	    def approved_diffs(diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
88	        """Every repository-group (pin/config/source) diff this run's decisions approved,
89	        in `plan.diffs` order — already pin/config-before-source (`plan()`'s sort).
90	        Excludes the synthetic metadata-refresh marker itself, which is tracked separately
91	        since it names no `/etc/apt` file to back up or write.
92	        """
93	        return [
94	            diff
95	            for diff in diffs
96	            if diff.item_class in REPO_GROUP_CLASSES
97	            and diff.item_id != METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID
98	            and diff.action in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.REMOVE, DiffAction.CHANGE)
99	            and decisions.get(diff.item_id) == Decision.APPLY
100	        ]
101	
102	    async def ensure_converged(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]) -> None:
103	        """Do the unit's entire convergence exactly once per run.
104	
105	        Idempotent: a no-op on every call after the first (`self._outcome` is `None` only until
106	        this method's first completion). Never called under dry-run — the base `apply()` loop
107	        never calls `converge()` at all when `self.context.dry_run` is set, so this method's own
108	        logic can assume real commands are safe to issue.
109	        """
110	        if self._outcome is not None:
111	            return
112	
113	        group_diffs = self.approved_diffs(diffs, decisions)
114	        derived_writes = self._derived.all_writes()
115	        marker_present = decisions.get(METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID) == Decision.APPLY
116	
117	        # Every keyring write this run owes, decided from the decisions and derivations the
118	        # run already made — never from a decision about a key, which does not exist.
119	        written = frozenset(Path(dest).name for dest in (*self._derived.distro_writes, *self._derived.repo_writes))
120	        keyring_writes = self._keyrings.writes(self._keyrings.surviving_refs(diffs, decisions, written))
121	        # "Remove keys after removing sources" is literal: with no source deletion in this
122	        # run nothing can have become unused, so the collection pass does not run at all.
123	        collect_unused = any(
124	            diff.item_class == ItemClass.APT_SOURCE and diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE for diff in group_diffs
125	        )
126	
127	        if not group_diffs and not keyring_writes and not derived_writes:
128	            self._outcome = (
129	                {METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID: (True, "no repository changes to refresh for")} if marker_present else {}
130	            )
131	            return
132	
133	        # Populated incrementally (not built up in a local dict and assigned at the
134	        # end) so a later diff in THIS SAME unit can consult an earlier diff's real
135	        # outcome while the unit is still being written.
136	        self._outcome = {}
137	
138	        staging_dir = await self._files.staging_dir()
139	        backup_dir = f"{staging_dir}/backup-{uuid4().hex}"
140	
141	        existed_before: dict[str, bool] = {}
142	        try:
143	            for _local, dest in keyring_writes:
144	                existed_before[dest] = await self._files.backup(dest, backup_dir)
145	            for dest in derived_writes:
146	                existed_before[dest] = await self._files.backup(dest, backup_dir)
147	            for diff in group_diffs:
148	                dest = repo_item_destination(diff)
149	                existed_before[dest] = await self._files.backup(dest, backup_dir)
150	        except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
151	            # A backup failure aborts the whole unit before any write happens (T-02-34
152	            # never partially applies), but `self._outcome` must still end up populated for
153	            # every group item (D-27) — otherwise the idempotency guard at the top of this
154	            # method treats the unit as "already handled" on the next `converge()` call, and
155	            # `converge_item`'s `self._outcome[diff.item_id]` raises a bare `KeyError` for
156	            # every item after the first, escaping the per-item `ConvergeItemFailed` handler
157	            # and crashing the whole job instead of failing one item.
158	            self._record_failure(group_diffs, marker_present, f"repository group backup failed: {exc}")
159	            return
160	
161	        # Keys FIRST, before any source file is written: a repository whose keyring has
162	        # not landed is a repository apt refuses on every subsequent operation, which
163	        # `Keyrings.gap` turns into a refusal to write that source at all.
164	        await self._keyrings.provision(keyring_writes, staging_dir)
165	
166	        await self._write_files(group_diffs, staging_dir)
167	
168	        # Keys LAST, after every source write and deletion: what a keyring is worth is a
169	        # reference count over the target's REAL source files, and only now is that count
170	        # taken against the state the run actually produced.
171	        if collect_unused:
172	            await self._keyrings.remove_unused(backup_dir, existed_before)
173	
174	        update_result = await self._target.run_command(
175	            "sudo apt-get update",
176	            login_shell=False,
177	            mutates="refresh apt package lists against the newly written repository configuration",
178	        )
179	        if update_result.success:
180	            # This IS the run's single metadata refresh: flag it so the install path's
181	            # `MetadataRefresh.ensure` is a no-op and never issues a second `apt-get update`.
182	            self._refresh.mark_done()
183	            await self._files.discard_backup(
184	                backup_dir, mutates="discard the repository-group backup after a successful refresh"
185	            )
186	            if marker_present:
187	                self._outcome[METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID] = (True, "apt-get update succeeded")
188	            return
189	
190	        # Rollback (T-02-34): restore every file that existed before, delete every file
191	        # the unit created, discard the backup directory, then re-probe apt so the
192	        # failure summary can tell the user whether the target recovered rather than
193	        # leaving them to guess.
194	        recovery = await self._rollback(existed_before, backup_dir)
195	        self._log(
196	            Host.TARGET,
197	            LogLevel.ERROR,
198	            f"apt-get update failed after repository group writes; rolled back ({recovery}): "
199	            f"{update_result.stderr.strip()}",
200	            stderr=update_result.stderr,
201	        )
202	
203	        # Every group item is recorded as a failure (D-27) — even ones whose own write
204	        # just succeeded above — because the rollback undid it: what actually landed on
205	        # the target is the pre-run state, not what this run intended.
206	        self._record_failure(
207	            group_diffs,
208	            marker_present,
209	            f"repository group rolled back after apt-get update failure ({recovery}): {update_result.stderr.strip()}",
210	        )
211	
212	    async def _rollback(self, existed_before: dict[str, bool], backup_dir: str) -> str:
213	        """Undo the unit's writes and re-probe apt; return a short phrase describing how the
214	        target ended up, for the caller's failure summary (T-02-34).
215	
216	        One command per file, each result inspected. A single `;`-joined command would
217	        present the `--confirm-each-command` gate one all-or-nothing prompt, but it
218	        collapses N exit codes into one and makes "which file failed to restore"
219	        unanswerable — and a failing rollback step is exactly when the user needs that
220	        file named. Every step is attempted regardless of earlier failures, so one
221	        unwritable destination cannot strand the remaining files in their post-run state.
222	        """
223	        rollback_failures: list[str] = []
224	        for dest, existed in existed_before.items():
225	            if existed:
226	                action = f"restore {dest} from {backup_path_for(backup_dir, dest)}"
227	                result = await self._files.restore(dest, backup_dir)
228	            else:
229	                action = f"delete {dest}, which this run created"
230	                result = await self._files.delete(dest, mutates=f"ROLLBACK: delete {dest}, which this run created")
231	            if not result.success:
232	                rollback_failures.append(f"could not {action}: {result.stderr.strip()}")
233	                self._log(
234	                    Host.TARGET,
235	                    LogLevel.WARNING,
236	                    f"Rollback step failed — could not {action}: {result.stderr.strip()}",
237	                    stderr=result.stderr,
238	                )
239	
240	        if rollback_failures:
241	            # The backup directory is deliberately NOT discarded: a failed restore means it
242	            # holds the only remaining copy of that file's pre-run content, so deleting it
243	            # would destroy exactly what manual recovery depends on. Name the path — the
244	            # user has to finish this by hand.
245	            self._log(
246	                Host.TARGET,
247	                LogLevel.WARNING,
248	                f"Repository-group rollback incomplete; the backup is kept at {backup_dir} on the target "
249	                f"so the affected file(s) can be restored by hand: {'; '.join(rollback_failures)}",
250	            )
251	        else:
252	            await self._files.discard_backup(
253	                backup_dir, mutates="ROLLBACK: discard the repository-group backup directory"
254	            )
255	
256	        reprobe = await self._target.run_command(
257	            "sudo apt-get update",
258	            login_shell=False,
259	            mutates="ROLLBACK: re-probe apt against the restored repository configuration",
260	        )
261	        if reprobe.success:
262	            # After rollback `/etc/apt` is the pre-run configuration and this reprobe refreshed
263	            # metadata for it; package installs that still run against that config (D-27 —
264	            # a repo-group rollback does not cancel package items) then need no further
265	            # `apt-get update`. If the reprobe itself failed, the flag stays unset and the
266	            # install path's own refresh attempt will surface the still-broken apt.
267	            self._refresh.mark_done()
268	
269	        if rollback_failures:
270	            # Takes precedence over the reprobe's verdict: an incomplete rollback leaves
271	            # /etc/apt as neither the pre-run nor the post-run configuration, which a green
272	            # `apt-get update` would otherwise mask.
273	            return (
274	                f"ROLLBACK INCOMPLETE, {len(rollback_failures)} file(s) left unrestored "
275	                f"(backup kept at {backup_dir}): {'; '.join(rollback_failures)}"
276	            )
277	        return "target apt recovered after rollback" if reprobe.success else "target apt still broken after rollback"
278	
279	    def _record_failure(self, group_diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], marker_present: bool, message: str) -> None:
280	        """Mark every `group_diffs` item (and the metadata-refresh marker, if present)
281	        as failed with `message`, and every DERIVED write with it (D-39).
282	
283	        Shared by the backup-failure short-circuit and the post-rollback failure path so
284	        `self._outcome` always ends up fully populated (D-27) — a partially-populated map
285	        makes a later `converge()` call for an un-recorded item raise `KeyError` instead of
286	        `ConvergeItemFailed`.
287	        """
288	        assert self._outcome is not None
289	        for diff in group_diffs:
290	            self._outcome[diff.item_id] = (False, message)
291	        self._derived.fail_all(message)
292	        if marker_present:
293	            self._outcome[METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID] = (False, message)
294	
295	    async def _write_files(self, group_diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], staging_dir: str) -> None:
296	        """Every file operation the unit owes, in apt's own order (§3.3 steps 2-5): pins
297	        and apt config first, so a pin is in place the moment its origin becomes fetchable
298	        and an apt-config setting governs the refresh that follows; then the distribution's
299	        sources; then the derived vendor repositories; then the approved deletions.
300	        """
301	        for dest in self._derived.pin_writes:
302	            await self._write_derived(dest, staging_dir)
303	        for diff in group_diffs:
304	            if diff.action != DiffAction.REMOVE:
305	                await self._converge_write(diff, staging_dir)
306	        for dest in (*self._derived.distro_writes, *self._derived.repo_writes):
307	            await self._write_derived(dest, staging_dir)
308	        # Repository files before pin files before apt config, which is the reverse of the
309	        # write order and not the order `plan()` sorted the diffs into: a repository still
310	        # present while its pin is already gone is a fetchable origin nothing prefers,
311	        # whereas the reverse is a pin naming an origin apt no longer has.
312	        removals = sorted(
313	            (diff for diff in group_diffs if diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE),
314	            key=lambda diff: REMOVAL_CLASS_ORDER.get(diff.item_class, 0),
315	        )
316	        for diff in removals:
317	            await self._converge_write(diff, staging_dir)
318	
319	    async def _converge_write(self, diff: ItemDiff, staging_dir: str) -> None:
320	        """Run one REVIEWED item's file operation and record its per-item outcome
321	        (D-27), so a single failing file never stops the rest of the unit."""
322	        assert self._outcome is not None
323	        try:
324	            await self._write_or_remove(diff, staging_dir)
325	        except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
326	            self._outcome[diff.item_id] = (False, str(exc))
327	        else:
328	            self._outcome[diff.item_id] = (True, "converged")
329	
330	    async def _write_derived(self, dest: str, staging_dir: str) -> None:
331	        """Copy one DERIVED `/etc/apt` file from the source, logging what travelled and
332	        recording a failure against the destination rather than against an item (D-39).
333	
334	        There is no item to fail: the user decided about a package, and
335	        `DerivedWrites.install_refusal` is what turns this destination's failure into that
336	        package's refusal. The FULL line is how a derived write stays visible at all — it has
337	        no review entry to appear on (ADR-014).
338	        """
339	        gap = self._keyrings.gap(dest)
340	        if gap is not None:
341	            self._derived.record_failure(dest, gap)
342	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.ERROR, f"not writing {dest}: {gap}", stderr=gap)
343	            return
344	        try:
345	            await self._files.stage_and_promote(dest, dest, staging_dir, staged_name_for(dest))
346	        except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
347	            self._derived.record_failure(dest, str(exc))
348	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.ERROR, f"failed to write {dest}: {exc}", stderr=str(exc))
349	            return
350	        self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"wrote {dest} from the source")
351	
352	    async def _write_or_remove(self, diff: ItemDiff, staging_dir: str) -> None:
353	        """Converge one REVIEWED repository-group diff: `sudo rm --force` for a REMOVE, or
354	        `stage_and_promote` for an apt-config INSTALL/CHANGE (T-02-35).
355	        """
356	        dest = repo_item_destination(diff)
357	
358	        if diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE:
359	            result = await self._files.delete(dest, mutates=f"delete repository file {dest}")
360	            if not result.success:
361	                raise ConvergeItemFailed(f"failed to remove {dest}: {result.stderr.strip()}")
362	            return
363	
364	        staged_name = diff.item_id.replace(":", "_").replace("/", "_")
365	        await self._files.stage_and_promote(dest, dest, staging_dir, staged_name)

2	where under `/etc/apt` each one's file lives.
3	
4	Identity and location are one fact, which is why they share a module: `apt:pin:99-foo`
5	means "the file `/etc/apt/preferences.d/99-foo`", and a split between the two halves would
6	let an id exist that resolves to no path. Everything here is pure — no command, no I/O, no
7	decision. `packages/items.py` keeps the taxonomy every manager is keyed on
8	(`ItemClass`/`DiffClass`/`DiffAction`); these are apt's own shapes, which only this job
9	constructs (D-15).
10	"""

28	# batched `sha256sum` listing (never one command per file).

31	# `.save` and `.curtin.orig` copies Ubuntu's own tooling leaves behind (four of them on the
32	# development machine) — is invisible to apt, so offering one as a syncable item would ask
33	# the user about a file that changes nothing.

261	# -- Convergence order ------------------------------------------------------------------
262	
263	# The three repository-adjacent item classes that converge in a single ordered,
264	# transactional group ahead of packages — kept as one constant so the trigger check in
265	# `accept_review` and the group membership check in `converge` never drift. Signing keys
266	# are deliberately absent: they are not items at all, they are file operations this group
267	# brackets (package docstring).

269	
270	# Convergence order is an apt FACT (a repo's metadata must be fetched before anything
271	# installs from it), not a general ordering concept — which is why it lives here, in the
272	# job, rather than as a sort the shared core imposes on every manager. Packages sort last
273	# (module-level default 3); pins and apt config share a rank since nothing depends on
274	# their relative order. Keys need no rank: keyring provisioning and collection are steps
275	# inside the group's own convergence, not diffs competing for a position in this sort.
276	ITEM_CLASS_ORDER: dict[ItemClass, int] = {
277	    ItemClass.APT_PIN: 1,
278	    ItemClass.APT_CONFIG: 1,
279	    ItemClass.APT_SOURCE: 2,
280	    # Holds converge AFTER package installs (#208, D8: install-before-hold) — rank 4,
281	    # behind the module-level package default (3). A hold is dpkg selection state only:
282	    # holding a package that this same run is installing must happen once it is present.
283	    ItemClass.APT_HOLD: 4,

288	# that prefers it, so the target never sits with a pin naming an origin apt no longer has.

291	    ItemClass.APT_PIN: 2,
292	    ItemClass.APT_CONFIG: 3,

296	class RemovalVocabulary(NamedTuple):
297	    """How one deletable `/etc/apt` item class reads: `action_label` names the action for one
298	    entry, `plural` names the objects for the group title.
299	
300	    Two words rather than one because the two positions are different parts of speech. A
301	    title composed by pluralising the action label produces "Delete repositorys" — English
302	    plurals do not follow from a verb phrase, and the noun is what is being counted.
303	    """

305	    action_label: str
306	    plural: str

310	# the words each reads with (ADR-020 D-37, rulings 5 and 12). Both take two answers — delete
311	# or leave it for now — so both carry `REPO_REMOVAL_REVIEW_ACTION`; keeping them as two
312	# entries is what gives the user two separate screens rather than one mixed list.
313	# `remove`, not "delete repository"/"delete pin file": the action label is also the word in
314	# the decision column, where the group title above it already says what is being deleted, so
315	# the longer phrase said the noun once per row and pushed the column halfway across the
316	# screen. The title keeps the noun; the answer keeps the verb.
317	REPO_REMOVAL_VERBS: dict[ItemClass, RemovalVocabulary] = {
318	    ItemClass.APT_SOURCE: RemovalVocabulary("remove", "repositories"),
319	    ItemClass.APT_PIN: RemovalVocabulary("remove", "pin files"),

1	"""Signing keys: the two file operations that bracket the repository unit (D-12).
2	
3	A key is NOT an item. It has no `ItemClass`, no `item_id`, no diff, no review entry and no
4	decision-file identity: the user thinks in repositories and packages, and a key is only how a
5	repository is made to work. So everything here is driven by the decisions the user made about
6	SOURCES, and nothing here ever asks a question, builds an `ItemDiff`, or writes a decision
7	file.
8	
9	Provisioning runs before any source file is written and collection after every source write
10	and deletion — the order is apt's, and `Keyrings.gap` is what stops a repository being written
11	ahead of its key. Both are ownership-aware in one direction only: a key the target LACKS is
12	copied whatever owns it, because a vendor `.deb` that ships both a repository entry and the
13	keyring trusting it cannot be installed until that keyring is present.
14	"""
15

36	def dangling_ref(keyring_refs: Sequence[str], source_key_filenames: frozenset[str]) -> str | None:
37	    """The first `keyring_refs` entry whose basename is absent from
38	    `source_key_filenames`, or `None` if every reference resolves to a real file on the
39	    source. A source file with no `Signed-By:`/`signed-by=` at all (`keyring_refs` is
40	    empty) has nothing to validate — it is not itself a dangling reference.
41	
42	    `source_key_filenames` spans all three key directories (`KEY_DIRS`), so a reference is
43	    dangling only when the source machine really has no such key — not merely when it keeps
44	    it somewhere this job did not think to look.
45	    """
46	    for ref in keyring_refs:
47	        if Path(ref).name not in source_key_filenames:
48	            return ref
49	    return None

52	class Keyrings:
53	    """Every key decision and both key operations, over the two machines' captured key
54	    digests.
55	
56	    The digest maps ARE the whole key model (package docstring): provisioning compares them
57	    to decide what to copy, the readiness check consults them instead of re-probing the
58	    target, and collection uses the per-directory pair to tell a key the source machine still
59	    has from one it dropped.
60	    """
61	
62	    def __init__(
63	        self,
64	        *,
65	        source_keys: KeyDigests,
66	        target_keys: KeyDigests,
67	        source_refs: SourceFileRefs,
68	        target_refs: SourceFileRefs,
69	        package_owned: frozenset[str],
70	        probe: AptProbe,
71	        files: TargetFiles,
72	        log: Log,
73	    ) -> None:
74	        self._source_keys = source_keys
75	        self._target_keys = target_keys
76	        self._source_refs = source_refs
77	        self._target_refs = target_refs
78	        # Absolute paths of every key file on the TARGET that the target's own dpkg owns,
79	        # from one batched `dpkg --search` at plan time. Consulted in one direction only: it
80	        # never blocks copying a key the target LACKS, it only stops a differing key the
81	        # target's package manages from being overwritten.
82	        self._package_owned = package_owned
83	        self._probe = probe
84	        self._files = files
85	        self._log = log
86	        # Absolute target paths provisioning successfully wrote this run. A source file may
87	        # only be written once every keyring it references is either already byte-identical
88	        # on the target or in here.
89	        self._provisioned: set[str] = set()
90	
91	    def manages(self, ref: str) -> bool:
92	        """Whether the target already has the key `ref` names AND its own dpkg owns that
93	        path — the one case where a differing keyring is deliberately left alone.
94	
95	        Not a general ownership gate (package docstring): a key the target LACKS is copied
96	        whatever owns it on the source, because a vendor `.deb` that ships both a repository
97	        entry and the keyring trusting it cannot be installed until that keyring is present.
98	        """
99	        return self._target_keys.digest_of(ref) is not None and ref in self._package_owned
100	
101	    def writes(self, refs: frozenset[str]) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
102	        """`(local path, target destination)` for every keyring this run must copy, given
103	        the set of references that will be live on the target.
104	
105	        Content-based, not presence-based: a key already on the target whose bytes differ
106	        from the source machine's is copied too. That is what keeps a ROTATED key correct —
107	        the vendor's new key changes no source FILE, so nothing else in the run would ever
108	        notice, and the target's apt would fail that repository's signature check.
109	
110	        Two populations, one rule ("the target's copy matches the source machine's"):
111	
112	        - Every `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d` key the source has. Nothing references these —
113	          they are ambient trust — so a reference count cannot select among them and their
114	          own content is the only signal there is.
115	        - The `/etc/apt/keyrings` and `/usr/share/keyrings` files that `refs` actually
116	          names. Neither directory is mirrored wholesale: a keyring no source on the target
117	          points at is litter, and `/usr/share/keyrings` is mostly the distro's own.
118	
119	        Overwriting is ownership-aware, copying is not (package docstring): a key the target
120	        already has with different bytes is skipped when the target's dpkg owns that path,
121	        while a key the target LACKS is always copied — including a package-owned one,
122	        which is the only way a repository whose keyring ships inside a package it hosts can
123	        ever be bootstrapped.
124	
125	        A destination is emitted at most once, so one rotated key serving three
126	        repositories is still exactly one write.
127	        """
128	        writes: dict[str, str] = {}
129	        for name, digest in self._source_keys.in_dir(APT_TRUSTED_GPG_DIR).items():
130	            dest = f"{APT_TRUSTED_GPG_DIR}/{name}"
131	            if self._target_keys.in_dir(APT_TRUSTED_GPG_DIR).get(name) == digest or self.manages(dest):
132	                continue
133	            writes[dest] = dest
134	        writes.update(self.referenced_writes(refs))
135	        return [(writes[dest], dest) for dest in sorted(writes)]
136	
137	    def referenced_writes(self, refs: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
138	        """`{destination: local path}` for the subset of `refs` whose key this run must
139	        copy — the reference-driven half of `writes`, without the ambient
140	        `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d` population.
141	
142	        Split out because it is also what a single source file's review detail may name: the
143	        keys that travel BECAUSE of that file. The global keys travel regardless of any
144	        source file, so attributing them to one would name the same key on every repository
145	        in the review.
146	        """
147	        writes: dict[str, str] = {}
148	        for ref in refs:
149	            local = self._source_keys.path_of(ref)
150	            if local is None:
151	                # The source machine has no such key. That is D-12's dangling reference,
152	                # already reported on the REPOSITORY item; inventing a key here is exactly
153	                # what "never re-fetched from a vendor" forbids.
154	                continue
155	            if self._source_keys.digest_of(ref) == self._target_keys.digest_of(ref) or self.manages(ref):
156	                continue
157	            writes[ref] = local
158	        return writes
159	
160	    def surviving_refs(
161	        self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], decisions: Mapping[str, Decision], written: frozenset[str]
162	    ) -> frozenset[str]:
163	        """Every keyring reference that will be live on the target once this run's derived
164	        writes and approved removals have been applied. `written` is the basenames of the
165	        source files this run writes.
166	
167	        Three populations, and getting any of them wrong provisions or deletes the wrong
168	        key: source files this run WRITES — the derived set, since ADR-020 D-37 leaves no
169	        other way for one to travel — contribute the SOURCE machine's references (a
170	        repository this run overwrites may point somewhere new); source files this run
171	        REMOVES contribute nothing (their keyring is about to be collected, not refreshed);
172	        every other source file on the target — untouched, recorded machine-specific, or
173	        never synced at all — contributes the references it currently carries.
174	        """
175	        removed = {
176	            diff.item_id.removeprefix(APT_SOURCE_ID_PREFIX)
177	            for diff in diffs
178	            if diff.item_class == ItemClass.APT_SOURCE
179	            and diff.item_id != METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID
180	            and diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE
181	            and decisions.get(diff.item_id) == Decision.APPLY
182	        }
183	
184	        refs: set[str] = set()
185	        for filename, (target_refs, _uris) in self._target_refs.by_filename.items():
186	            if filename not in removed and filename not in written:
187	                refs.update(target_refs)
188	        for filename in written:
189	            refs.update(self._source_refs.refs_of(filename))
190	        return frozenset(refs)
191	
192	    def pending_work(self) -> bool:
193	        """Whether ANY keyring could need writing this run, judged before the derived write
194	        set is consulted — the trigger that lets the repository unit run for a rotated key
195	        whose source file is byte-identical and therefore derives no write at all.
196	
197	        Deliberately a superset: it counts the references of every source file on BOTH
198	        machines, because which of them survive is decided later. A false positive costs
199	        nothing — the unit recomputes the exact set from `surviving_refs` and returns early
200	        when it turns out to be empty.
201	        """
202	        return bool(self.writes(self._target_refs.all_refs() | self._source_refs.all_refs()))
203	
204	    def gap(self, dest: str) -> str | None:
205	        """Why writing this derived source file would leave apt with a repository it cannot
206	        verify, or `None` when every keyring it names is in place (D-12).
207	
208	        A repository written without its key is a repository apt refuses on every
209	        subsequent operation, so writing it anyway is strictly worse than leaving the target
210	        alone. The refusal lands on the destination and, through the derived-write
211	        attribution, on the packages that needed it — the things the user actually decided
212	        about (D-39).
213	
214	        A key the target has and its own dpkg owns counts as ready even though this run
215	        deliberately did not overwrite it: the target's package manages that file, so the
216	        repository is trusted there. Pin and apt-config destinations name no keys and always
217	        return `None`.
218	        """
219	        for ref in self._source_refs.refs_of(Path(dest).name):
220	            if ref in self._provisioned:
221	                continue
222	            source_digest = self._source_keys.digest_of(ref)
223	            if source_digest is not None and source_digest == self._target_keys.digest_of(ref):
224	                continue
225	            if self.manages(ref):
226	                continue
227	            return (
228	                f"it references keyring {ref!r}, which is neither already present on the target with "
229	                "the source's own bytes nor among the keys this run provisioned (D-12/T-02-16)"
230	            )
231	        return None

233	    async def provision(self, writes: Sequence[tuple[str, str]], staging_dir: str) -> None:
234	        """Copy each planned keyring onto the target, recording the destinations that
235	        landed so `gap` can let their repositories be written.
236	
237	        A failure here fails no ITEM — there is no key item to fail. It is logged and the
238	        destination is simply left out of the provisioned set, which makes every source
239	        file referencing that keyring refuse its own write with a message naming the key.
240	        That is the D-12 outcome either way, reported against the thing the user reviewed.
241	        """
242	        for local, dest in writes:
243	            try:
244	                await self._files.stage_and_promote(local, dest, staging_dir, staged_name_for(dest))
245	            except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
246	                self._log(
247	                    Host.TARGET, LogLevel.ERROR, f"failed to provision signing key {dest}: {exc}", stderr=str(exc)
248	                )
249	                continue
250	            self._provisioned.add(dest)

252	    async def remove_unused(self, backup_dir: str, existed_before: dict[str, bool]) -> None:
253	        """Delete every `/etc/apt/keyrings` file on the target that no surviving source
254	        references — the garbage-collection half of transparent key handling.
255	
256	        Called only after every source write and deletion in the unit, and only when this
257	        run removed at least one source file. The reference count comes from a FRESH scan of
258	        the target's real source files, which is what makes the two cases the user cares
259	        about come out right without a guard of their own: a repository this run deleted has
260	        stopped referencing its key, and one whose deletion the user declined — or that
261	        failed to be deleted — still references it and keeps it alive.
262	
263	        Scoped to `/etc/apt/keyrings`, the one directory that exists purely for this. Legacy
264	        `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d` keys are ambient trust that nothing references by
265	        construction, so "unused" is not computable for them; `/usr/share/keyrings` is
266	        package territory and holds keys the distro's own tooling put there. Both are left
267	        to accumulate rather than deleted on a guess.
268	
269	        Each deletion is backed up into the unit's own backup directory first and recorded
270	        in `existed_before`, so a failing `apt-get update` rolls a collected key back with
271	        everything else. A key that cannot be backed up is not deleted: without the backup a
272	        rollback could not restore it, and an unused keyring costs nothing to keep.
273	        """
274	        candidates = frozenset(self._target_keys.in_dir(APT_KEYRINGS_DIR)) - frozenset(
275	            self._source_keys.in_dir(APT_KEYRINGS_DIR)
276	        )
277	        if not candidates:
278	            return
279	        references = await scan_source_file_references(self._probe.target_run, Host.TARGET)
280	        referenced = {Path(ref).name for ref in references.all_refs()}
281	
282	        for filename in sorted(candidates - referenced):
283	            dest = f"{APT_KEYRINGS_DIR}/{filename}"
284	            try:
285	                existed = await self._files.backup(dest, backup_dir)
286	            except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
287	                self._log(
288	                    Host.TARGET,
289	                    LogLevel.WARNING,
290	                    f"keeping unused signing key {dest}: it could not be backed up first ({exc})",
291	                )
292	                continue
293	            if not existed:
294	                continue
295	            existed_before[dest] = True
296	            result = await self._files.delete(
297	                dest, mutates=f"delete signing key {dest}, which no repository references any more"
298	            )
299	            if not result.success:
300	                self._log(
301	                    Host.TARGET,
302	                    LogLevel.WARNING,
303	                    f"could not delete unused signing key {dest}: {result.stderr.strip()}",
304	                    stderr=result.stderr,
305	                )

4	detail string built where it is needed drifts from the one beside it, and
5	`tests/manual/review_harness.py` rehearses these builders directly so what a tester reads
6	is what a real run shows rather than a paraphrase of it.
7	
8	Every builder takes `Machines` and names both machines by hostname — never "source" and
9	"target", which are the tool's words for the two ends of a run and not the names of
10	anybody's computers.

20	# A URI's scheme, stripped for DISPLAY only (ruling 9). Matches `cdrom:`-style schemes too,
21	# whose `//` is optional, so an origin apt can never replicate still reads as itself.
22	_URI_SCHEME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9+.\-]*:(//)?", re.IGNORECASE)

25	def display_origin(uri: str) -> str:
26	    """A repository URI in the form the review shows it (ruling 9): the FULL path with its
27	    scheme stripped — `ppa.launchpadcontent.net/git-core/ppa/ubuntu`.
28	
29	    The path, never the bare host: one Launchpad host serves thousands of unrelated PPAs and
30	    one vendor host often serves several channels, so a hostname does not identify the
31	    repository the package actually came from. Only the display strips; the comparison form
32	    stays exactly what `normalise_repo_uri` produces, scheme included, because that is what
33	    apt prints and what the two machines' URIs are matched on.
34	    """
35	    return _URI_SCHEME_RE.sub("", uri).rstrip("/")

38	def build_origin_detail(origins: Sequence[str]) -> str | None:
39	    """Detail naming where an approved install would come from, or `None` when there is
40	    nothing worth naming (ruling 9).
41	
42	    `origins` is the package's NON-distribution origins, already filtered by the caller
43	    against the origins that machine's own distribution files declare — so an empty sequence
44	    means the distribution's archive serves it, which is the unremarkable case and earns no
45	    text. Several are named comma-separated and sorted, because a package genuinely served
46	    by two vendors is a fact the user should see whole.

53	def build_repo_unavailable_detail(name: str, origins: Sequence[str], cause: str, machines: Machines) -> str:
54	    """Detail for a `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` diff: where the source has this package from, and why
55	    the target cannot be given the same place (ADR-020 D-34).
56	
57	    Both halves are load-bearing. Naming the origin is what stops this reading as "apt has
58	    never heard of it"; naming the cause is what tells the user whether the remedy is theirs
59	    (a repository file that no longer exists, a missing signing key) or nobody's.
60	    """
61	    where = f" from {', '.join(display_origin(uri) for uri in origins)}" if origins else ""

66	    source_origins: Sequence[str], target_origins: Sequence[str], machines: Machines

71	    mean a cross-vendor reinstall, which is not a float (D-04) and not something the user
72	    asked for. The user is the only one who can say which machine is the odd one out.
73	    """
74	    source = ", ".join(display_origin(uri) for uri in source_origins)
75	    target = ", ".join(display_origin(uri) for uri in target_origins)

80	    name: str, source_origins: Sequence[str], target_origins: Sequence[str], machines: Machines

82	    """Why an approved install was refused at the last moment (ADR-020 D-35): the origin the
83	    source uses, and the origin the target's apt would have installed from instead.

85	    Both are named because either half alone is unactionable. "The wrong vendor" does not

88	    on the item the user actually decided about.

93	    else:

190	def build_trigger_phrase(triggers: frozenset[str], candidates: Sequence[str]) -> str:

192	    back to the earlier screens when the answer really is all of them and listing them would

1	"""Converging one package, one removal, one hold — and the guard chain that decides whether
2	each may run at all.
3	
4	The chain's ORDER is the load-bearing part, so it is written once, here, in the order it must
5	run: a derived file that never landed refuses the install before any command at all (D-39,
6	cheapest and most specific); then the run's single `apt-get update`; then the origin read-back
7	(D-35, one cached lookup); then the transaction simulation and the collateral guard (D-30, one
8	command). Each step is stated as its own early return so the sequence is readable as a
9	sequence rather than inferred from nesting.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import shlex
15	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
16	
17	from pcswitcher.executor import RemoteExecutor
18	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.collateral import Collateral
19	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.commands import (
20	    compare_deb_versions,
21	    install_args,
22	    remove_args,
23	    simulate_apt_transaction,
24	)
25	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.derived import DerivedWrites
26	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.items import hold_name, package_name
27	from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync.origins import OriginClassifier
28	from pcswitcher.jobs.packages.items import DiffAction, ItemDiff

30	from pcswitcher.jobs.packages.sync_core import ConvergeItemFailed

34	class MetadataRefresh:
35	    """The run's single `apt-get update`, whoever issues it.
36	
37	    At most ONE runs per run across both paths: the repository unit's own refresh and the
38	    pre-install refresh set the same flag, so the second path becomes a no-op. A failure on the
39	    install path is cached so every remaining install aborts on the same error WITHOUT issuing
40	    a second `apt-get update` — the "at most one" guarantee holds even on the failure path.
41	    """
42	
43	    def __init__(self) -> None:
44	        self._refreshed = False
45	        self._error: str | None = None
46	
47	    @property
48	    def done(self) -> bool:
49	        return self._refreshed
50	
51	    def mark_done(self) -> None:
52	        """Record that a refresh has already happened this run — called by the repository
53	        unit, whose own `apt-get update` IS the run's single refresh."""
54	        self._refreshed = True
55	
56	    async def ensure(self, target: RemoteExecutor, manager_id: str) -> None:
57	        """Run exactly one `apt-get update` before the first package install of a run that
58	        approves an INSTALL but changes no repository-group item — resolving installs against
59	        a stale package list can pick candidates the target can no longer fetch. A no-op once
60	        metadata has already been refreshed this run, INCLUDING by the repository unit's own
61	        `apt-get update`, so the two refresh paths never both fire.
62	
63	        Aborts the install by raising `ConvergeItemFailed` if the refresh fails: unlike the
64	        repository-unit path — which has `/etc/apt` writes to roll back and owns that
65	        behaviour — this path made no changes, so failing the item (installing nothing) is
66	        its whole safe response. Never reached under dry-run: the base `apply()` loop does not
67	        call `converge()` when `self.context.dry_run` is set.
68	        """
69	        if self._refreshed:
70	            return
71	        if self._error is not None:
72	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(self._error)
73	
74	        result = await target.run_command(
75	            "sudo apt-get update",
76	            login_shell=False,
77	            mutates="refresh apt package lists before the first install of this run",
78	        )
79	        if not result.success:
80	            self._error = (
81	                f"apt-get update failed before installing {manager_id} packages; refusing to install "
82	                f"against a stale package list (decision 1): {result.stderr.strip()}"
83	            )
84	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(self._error)
85	        self._refreshed = True
86

88	class PackageConverger:
89	    """One package per invocation (D-27) so a single bad package cannot fail the whole batch,
90	    and so each package's simulation corresponds exactly to the command that follows it. The
91	    target resolves dependencies and downloads from its own repos (D-28) — no source cache is
92	    consulted.
93	    """
94	
95	    def __init__(
96	        self,
97	        *,
98	        target: RemoteExecutor,
99	        manager_id: str,
100	        collateral: Collateral,
101	        derived: DerivedWrites,
102	        origins: OriginClassifier,
103	        refresh: MetadataRefresh,
104	    ) -> None:
105	        self._target = target
106	        self._manager_id = manager_id
107	        self._collateral = collateral
108	        self._derived = derived
109	        self._origins = origins
110	        self._refresh = refresh
111	
112	    async def install(
113	        self, diff: ItemDiff, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]
114	    ) -> CommandResult:
115	        """Simulate, then apply, one apt install — the last line of defence behind the
116	        plan-time collateral classification (D-30). Auto-installed collateral (a package
117	        apt pulls in that is outside the target's `apt-mark showmanual` set) proceeds
118	        silently — apt resolving its own dependencies. A manually-installed collateral
119	        removal or downgrade (manual on the TARGET, ADR-020 D-40) is refused unless the user
120	        let it go ahead in the review; the decision was made at plan time, and this guard only
121	        verifies the real transaction has not drifted to touch a manual package nobody saw.
122	        """
123	        name = package_name(diff.item_id)
124	
125	        # A derived `/etc/apt` write this package needed and that failed refuses it first
126	        # (D-39), before any command at all: the file is named, which the origin check could
127	        # only say the consequence of.
128	        blocked = self._derived.install_refusal(diff.item_id, name)
129	        if blocked is not None:
130	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(blocked)
131	
132	        await self._refresh.ensure(self._target, self._manager_id)
133	
134	        # The origin check runs immediately after the refresh and before the collateral
135	        # simulation: refusing an install whose origin is wrong costs one cached lookup,
136	        # while simulating it costs a command.
137	        refusal = await self._origins.refusal(name, diffs=diffs, decisions=decisions, target=self._target)
138	        if refusal is not None:
139	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(refusal)
140	
141	        args = install_args([name])
142	        preview = await simulate_apt_transaction(self._target, args, login_shell=False)
143	
144	        protected = self._collateral.protected()
145	        approved_collateral = self._collateral.approved
146	        refused = [pkg for pkg in preview.removals if pkg in protected and pkg not in approved_collateral]
147	        if refused:
148	            removed = ", ".join(refused)
149	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(
150	                f"install of {name} refused: apt-get --dry-run would remove manually-installed {removed}, "
151	                "which was not approved as collateral in this run (D-30)"
152	            )
153	
154	        for pkg, (old_version, new_version) in preview.install_versions.items():
155	            if old_version is None or pkg not in protected or pkg in approved_collateral:
156	                continue
157	            if await compare_deb_versions(self._target, new_version, old_version) < 0:
158	                raise ConvergeItemFailed(
159	                    f"install of {name} refused: apt-get --dry-run would downgrade manually-installed {pkg} "
160	                    f"from {old_version} to {new_version}, which was not approved as collateral (D-30, D-04)"
161	                )
162	
163	        real_cmd = f"sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get {args}"
164	        return await self._target.run_command(real_cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"install apt package {name}")
165	
166	    async def remove(
167	        self, diff: ItemDiff, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff], decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]
168	    ) -> CommandResult:
169	        """Simulate, then apply, one apt remove — the same last line of defence the
170	        install guard is (D-30). A collateral removal of an auto-installed package (outside
171	        the target's `apt-mark showmanual` set) proceeds — removing a package legitimately
172	        removes the now-orphaned dependencies apt pulled in for it. A collateral removal of a
173	        manually-installed package (manual on the TARGET, ADR-020 D-40) is refused unless it
174	        was itself an approved removal this run or approved let go ahead as collateral; that
175	        decision was made at plan time, and this guard only catches a real transaction that
176	        drifted to touch a manual package nobody reviewed.
177	        """
178	        name = package_name(diff.item_id)
179	        args = remove_args([name])
180	
181	        preview = await simulate_apt_transaction(self._target, args, login_shell=False)
182	        approved = self._collateral.approved_removals(diffs, decisions)
183	        protected = self._collateral.protected()
184	        approved_collateral = self._collateral.approved
185	        refused = [
186	            pkg
187	            for pkg in preview.removals
188	            if pkg != name and pkg not in approved and pkg not in approved_collateral and pkg in protected
189	        ]
190	        if refused:
191	            removed = ", ".join(refused)
192	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(
193	                f"removal of {name} refused: apt-get --dry-run would also remove manually-installed {removed}, "
194	                "which was neither an approved removal nor approved as collateral in this run (D-30)"
195	            )
196	
197	        real_cmd = f"sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get {args}"
198	        return await self._target.run_command(real_cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"remove apt package {name}")
199	
200	    async def hold(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
201	        """Converge one `apt:hold:<name>` membership item (#208, D4/D5): `apt-mark hold`
202	        for the add direction (INSTALL), `apt-mark unhold` for the remove direction
203	        (REMOVE). Selection state only — no `apt-get --dry-run` simulation and no transaction
204	        guard (a hold changes nothing about the installed package set, D4). The command's
205	        exit code alone decides pass/fail (D-27); a hold on an absent or unknown package
206	        that `apt-mark` rejects is a normal per-item failure (D6), not a gated abort.
207	        """
208	        name = hold_name(diff.item_id)
209	        verb = "hold" if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL else "unhold"
210	        return await self._target.run_command(
211	            f"sudo apt-mark {verb} {shlex.quote(name)}", login_shell=False, mutates=f"{verb} apt package {name}"
212	        )

1	"""Every file this job puts on, or takes off, the target — and the only module that knows
2	how a root-owned `/etc/apt` file is written at all.

5	(`executor.py:508`) and cannot write into `/etc/apt` directly, so every write is the same
6	two-step: bytes land under the target user's own `~/.cache` staging directory, then `sudo
7	install` promotes them with the right ownership and mode. Keeping that in one place is what
8	lets the repository unit and the keyring provisioning share it without either owning it, and
9	what keeps shell strings out of both.
10	"""

12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import shlex
15	from pathlib import Path

17	from pcswitcher.executor import RemoteExecutor
18	from pcswitcher.jobs.packages.sync_core import ConvergeItemFailed
19	from pcswitcher.models import CommandResult

22	def backup_path_for(backup_dir: str, dest: str) -> str:
23	    """A stable, unique backup filename for an absolute `dest` path, flattened into
24	    `backup_dir` (`/etc/apt/sources.list.d/foo.list` -> `etc_apt_sources.list.d_foo.list`)
25	    so every backed-up file lives directly under one run-scoped directory.
26	    """
27	    return f"{backup_dir}/{dest.lstrip('/').replace('/', '_')}"

31	    """The staging filename an absolute destination gets, flattened the same way a backup
32	    is so two destinations can never collide in the one staging directory."""
33	    return dest.lstrip("/").replace("/", "_")

36	class TargetFiles:
37	    """The target's filesystem, for the paths this job owns."""
38	
39	    def __init__(self, target: RemoteExecutor) -> None:
40	        self._target = target
41	        self._home: str | None = None
42	
43	    async def home(self) -> str:
44	        """The target user's home directory, resolved once per run via `echo $HOME`
45	        (`config_sync._copy_config_to_target`'s established pattern) and cached — every
46	        repository-group file write needs the same absolute staging path.
47	        """
48	        if self._home is None:

53	    async def staging_dir(self) -> str:

65	        returns whether it existed (so rollback knows restore-vs-delete per file).

68	        exists = await self._target.run_command(f"test -f {quoted_dest}", login_shell=False)
69	        if not exists.success:
70	            return False
71	
72	        await self._target.run_command(
73	            f"mkdir --parents {shlex.quote(backup_dir)}",
74	            login_shell=False,
75	            mutates="create the repository-group backup directory",
76	        )
77	        backup_path = backup_path_for(backup_dir, dest)
78	        result = await self._target.run_command(
79	            f"sudo cp --archive {quoted_dest} {shlex.quote(backup_path)}",
80	            login_shell=False,
81	            mutates=f"back up {dest} before the repository group is written",
82	        )
83	        if not result.success:
84	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(
85	                f"failed to back up {dest} before converging the repository group: {result.stderr.strip()}"
86	            )
87	        return True

89	    async def restore(self, dest: str, backup_dir: str) -> CommandResult:
90	        """Put `dest` back from its backup copy."""
91	        return await self._target.run_command(
92	            f"sudo install --owner=root --group=root --mode=0644 "
93	            f"{shlex.quote(backup_path_for(backup_dir, dest))} {shlex.quote(dest)}",
94	            login_shell=False,

99	        return await self._target.run_command(
100	            f"sudo rm --force {shlex.quote(dest)}", login_shell=False, mutates=mutates
101	        )

103	    async def discard_backup(self, backup_dir: str, *, mutates: str) -> CommandResult:
104	        return await self._target.run_command(
105	            f"rm --recursive --force {shlex.quote(backup_dir)}", login_shell=False, mutates=mutates
106	        )
107	
108	    async def stage_and_promote(self, local: str, dest: str, staging_dir: str, staged_name: str) -> None:
109	        """Copy the SOURCE machine's `local` onto the target at `dest`, byte-for-byte
110	        (T-02-35). The two paths are the same for every `/etc/apt` file this job writes
111	        except a keyring the two machines keep in different directories, where the
112	        destination has to be the path the repository's `Signed-By:` actually names.
113	
114	        Bytes land under the target user's own `~/.cache` staging directory first, then `sudo
115	        install` promotes them with the right ownership/mode in one atomic step (no window
116	        where the file exists under `/etc/apt` owned by the wrong user, unlike a `mv` plus
117	        separate `chown`/`chmod`). The staging copy is removed in a `finally` so a failed
118	        promotion never leaves transferred key material sitting in the cache.
119	        """
120	        # `sources.list.d`, `preferences.d`, `apt.conf.d` and `trusted.gpg.d` ship with
121	        # the `apt` package, but `/etc/apt/keyrings` is a third-party convention that a
122	        # fresh Ubuntu 24.04 target does not have — `install` (unlike `install -D`)
123	        # never creates DEST's missing parent directories, so a per-repo key promotion
124	        # to a fresh machine would otherwise fail every time. `mkdir --parents --mode` only chmods
125	        # directories it actually creates (unlike `install --directory`, which would also chmod
126	        # the four directories that already exist), so this is a no-op everywhere except
127	        # the one directory this project actually needs to create.
128	        dest_dir = str(Path(dest).parent)
129	        mkdir_result = await self._target.run_command(
130	            f"sudo mkdir --parents --mode=0755 {shlex.quote(dest_dir)}",
131	            login_shell=False,
132	            mutates=f"create directory {dest_dir} for {dest}",
133	        )
134	        if not mkdir_result.success:
135	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(
136	                f"failed to prepare directory {dest_dir} for {dest}: {mkdir_result.stderr.strip()}"
137	            )
138	
139	        staged_dest = f"{staging_dir}/{staged_name}"
140	        try:
141	            await self._target.send_file(
142	                Path(local), staged_dest, mutates=f"stage {dest} into the target's cache before promotion"
143	            )
144	            promote = await self._target.run_command(
145	                f"sudo install --owner=root --group=root --mode=0644 {shlex.quote(staged_dest)} {shlex.quote(dest)}",
146	                login_shell=False,
147	                mutates=f"promote the staged file into {dest} as root:root 0644",
148	            )
149	            if not promote.success:
150	                raise ConvergeItemFailed(f"failed to install {dest}: {promote.stderr.strip()}")
151	        finally:
152	            await self._target.run_command(
153	                f"rm --force {shlex.quote(staged_dest)}",
154	                login_shell=False,
155	                mutates=f"remove the staging copy of {dest}",
156	            )

2	
3	One module for every read so "is anything asked per-package?" is answerable by looking in one
4	place. It is not: every command here is batched — one `apt-cache policy` over a whole name
5	set, one `sha256sum` listing per directory, one `awk` over every source file, one
6	`dpkg --search` over every key file.
7	
8	The facts are frozen and answer their own questions (`SourceFileRefs.files_serving`,
9	`KeyDigests.digest_of`) rather than being dicts the rest of the job re-derives things from.
10	That is what lets the deciding half — origins, diffing, derivation, keyrings — be pure
11	functions over two snapshots instead of methods reaching into a job's mutable state.
12	
13	Unlike apt packages, the five `/etc/apt` directories are diffed by whole-FILE digest: one
14	batched `sha256sum` listing per directory tells us which filenames differ without
15	transferring a single byte, and the full content of a file is only fetched for the files a
16	diff actually implicates (missing-on-target, extra-on-target, or digest-mismatched) — never
17	for a file that is already identical on both machines.

70	def parse_sha256sum(output: str) -> dict[str, str]:
71	    """`<digest>  <path>` lines (one per `sha256sum` invocation) -> `{basename: digest}`.
72	
73	    Basename, not the full path: every caller already knows which directory it asked
74	    about, and item identity is the filename, not the path.
75	    """
76	    digests: dict[str, str] = {}
77	    for line in lines(output):
78	        parts = line.split(None, 1)
79	        if len(parts) != 2:
80	            continue
81	        digest, path = parts
82	        digests[Path(path).name] = digest
83	    return digests

86	def keyring_reference(value: str) -> str | None:
87	    """`value` as a keyring PATH reference, or `None` when it is not one.
88	
89	    A `Signed-By:` field carries either a path or an INLINE armored key. Only an absolute
90	    path is a reference to a file that has to exist; anything else is the armored block
91	    itself and needs no provisioning, because it travels inside the source file. The
92	    distinction is not cosmetic: `add-apt-repository` writes the armor's first line on the
93	    field line (`Signed-By: -----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----`), so a bare `\\S+` capture
94	    turns every PPA added the normal way into a reference to a file named `-----BEGIN`,
95	    which resolves nowhere and downgrades the repository to `REPORT_ONLY`.
96	    """
97	    return value if value.startswith("/") else None
98

100	def parse_source_file(
101	    filename: str, content: str
102	) -> tuple[Literal["deb822", "list"], tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]]:
103	    """A source file's format (by extension), every keyring path it names, and every
104	    repository URI it points at (normalised by `normalise_repo_uri`).
105	
106	    deb822 `.sources` files name a key via a `Signed-By:` field and their repositories via
107	    `URIs:`; legacy `.list` files put both on the `deb` line, the key inside the options
108	    bracket as `[... signed-by=<path> ...]` and the URI immediately after it (RESEARCH
109	    Standard Stack). Parsed just far enough to extract these — never rewritten,
110	    normalised, or migrated between formats (RESEARCH Pitfall 3, deferred ideas).
111	
112	    One parser, three consumers: the keyring refs drive D-12's dangling-reference check
113	    and keyring garbage collection, the URIs drive the source-removal impact (C26) by
114	    matching against the origin `apt-cache policy` reports for an installed package.
115	
116	    A `Signed-By:` field may carry an INLINE armored key instead of a path, either with an
117	    empty field value and the block on continuation lines or with the block's first line on
118	    the field line itself. Neither yields a ref (`keyring_reference`), which is correct in
119	    both directions: the file depends on no key FILE, so nothing is invented for it, and no
120	    part of the armored block is mistaken for a path.
121	    """
122	    fmt: Literal["deb822", "list"] = "deb822" if filename.endswith(".sources") else "list"
123	    refs: list[str] = []
124	    uris: list[str] = []
125	    for raw_line in content.splitlines():
126	        line = raw_line.strip()
127	        if fmt == "deb822":
128	            signed_by = _SIGNED_BY_RE.match(line)
129	            uri_field = _URIS_RE.match(line)
130	            if uri_field:
131	                uris.extend(normalise_repo_uri(uri) for uri in uri_field.group("uris").split())
132	        else:
133	            signed_by = _LEGACY_SIGNED_BY_RE.search(raw_line)
134	            deb_line = _LEGACY_DEB_LINE_RE.match(line)
135	            if deb_line:
136	                uris.append(normalise_repo_uri(deb_line.group("uri")))
137	        if signed_by:
138	            ref = keyring_reference(signed_by.group("path"))
139	            if ref is not None:
140	                refs.append(ref)
141	    return fmt, tuple(refs), tuple(uris)

148	class SourceFileRefs:

159	    def empty(cls) -> SourceFileRefs:
160	        return cls(by_filename={})

163	        return self.by_filename.get(filename, ((), ()))[0]

172	        """Every file whose repository URIs intersect `origins` — the files that would have

177	        origins (a vendor repository and a security pocket both carrying it), and every one of
178	        them served it, so narrowing to one would drop a file the package really depends on.
179	        """

189	        """

192	            for filename, (_refs, uris) in self.by_filename.items()

213	    def empty(cls) -> KeyDigests:
214	        return cls(by_dir={})

217	        return self.by_dir.get(directory, {})

330	async def capture_dir_digests(
331	    run: Run, directory: str, host: Host, *, extensions: Sequence[str] = ()
332	) -> dict[str, str]:
333	    """One `if sudo test -d <dir>; then sudo find <dir> -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec sha256sum
334	    {} +; fi` per directory — a single batched command, never one `sha256sum` per file.
335	    `-exec ... {} +` never runs at all when the directory has no matching files, so an empty
336	    directory degrades to an empty digest map rather than a shell error.
337	
338	    `extensions` narrows the capture to the files apt itself reads, and is only correct
339	    where apt HAS such a rule: `sources.list.d` is read for `*.list`/`*.sources` alone, so
340	    the `.save`/`.curtin.orig` copies apt ignores must not become syncable items.
341	    `preferences.d` and `apt.conf.d` pass no extensions, because apt reads extensionless
342	    files in both.
343	
344	    An ABSENT directory is a separate case and is what the `sudo test -d` wrapper is for
345	    (ADR-022). Measured: `find` on a path that does not exist exits 1, exactly as it does
346	    when it cannot read one that does — so without the wrapper the two would be one signal,
347	    and the only ways to resolve it are both wrong. Failing every run on a machine with no
348	    `/etc/apt/preferences.d` turns a legitimate "no pins here" into an error; accepting the
349	    exit code turns a directory this run could not read into "that machine has no
350	    repositories", which offers every file on the other machine for removal. With the
351	    wrapper an absent directory answers "nothing" at exit 0 and a non-zero exit is only
352	    ever a real failure, which `require_answer` then fails the job on.
353	
354	    The test runs under `sudo` for the same WR-04 reason the `find` does, and the two must
355	    stay at the same privilege: measured, an unprivileged `test -d` on a directory inside an
356	    unsearchable parent exits 1, which collapses the whole `if` to exit 0 with no output —
357	    the reshape's one failure mode, answering "this machine has no pins or keys" for a
358	    directory root would have listed.
359	    """
360	    quoted = shlex.quote(directory)
361	    predicate = ""
362	    if extensions:
363	        names = " -o ".join(f"-name {shlex.quote(f'*{ext}')}" for ext in extensions)
364	        predicate = f"\\( {names} \\) "
365	    command = (
366	        f"if sudo test -d {quoted}; then sudo find {quoted} -maxdepth 1 -type f {predicate}-exec sha256sum {{}} +; fi"
367	    )
368	    result = await run(command)
369	    require_answer(command, result, host)
370	    return parse_sha256sum(result.stdout)

373	async def capture_file_digest(run: Run, path: str) -> str | None:
374	    """One `sudo sha256sum <path>`, or `None` when the file is absent.
375	
376	    The single-file counterpart to `capture_dir_digests`, for `/etc/apt/sources.list`,
377	    which is a file rather than a directory and so has no `find` listing to appear in.
378	    Verified: `sha256sum` on a missing path exits 1 and writes nothing to stdout, so the
379	    absent case falls out of the parse rather than needing a probe of its own.
380	    """
381	    result = await run(f"sudo sha256sum {shlex.quote(path)}")
382	    return parse_sha256sum(result.stdout).get(Path(path).name)

385	async def read_file_content(run: Run, path: str, host: Host) -> str:
386	    """One `sudo cat <path>` — used only for a file a diff actually implicates.
387	
388	    `sudo`-qualified to match `capture_dir_digests`'s `sudo find ... sha256sum`

411	async def scan_source_file_references(run: Run, host: Host) -> SourceFileRefs:
412	    """`{filename: (keyring_refs, repository URIs)}` for EVERY source file on a machine,
413	    from ONE batched command — `sources.list.d` AND `/etc/apt/sources.list`.
414	
415	    Machine-agnostic by construction (it takes the `run` callable and names no host), and
416	    run against BOTH machines: the target's answer drives the two consumers below, the
417	    source's answer is what maps a package's origin URIs back to the repository file that
418	    would have to travel for it (ADR-020 D-34).
419	
420	    Two target-side consumers, both of which need a fact no diff carries. The source-removal
421	    impact (C26) needs the repository URIs of a file whose deletion is offered. Keyring
422	    garbage collection needs the reference count of a key across every source file that
423	    exists, which is emphatically not the set of files any diff implicates: a keyring is
424	    commonly named only by files that are byte-identical on both machines, or that the user
425	    marked machine-specific, or — `/etc/apt/sources.list` — that pc-switcher never syncs at
426	    all. Missing any of those would delete a key that is still in use.
427	
428	    Deliberately unfiltered by extension, unlike `capture_dir_digests`' `sources.list.d`
429	    capture: a keyring named only by a file apt ignores is still a key nothing else
430	    references, and keeping it is cheaper than deleting one that turns out to be in use.
431	
432	    `find ... -exec awk {} +` passes every file to one awk process, never one command per
433	    file, and awk emits only the `URIs:`/`Signed-By:`/`deb` lines rather than whole
434	    files — so this stays compatible with the rule that full content is fetched only for a
435	    file a diff implicates. `sudo`-qualified to match `capture_dir_digests`'s privilege
436	    (WR-04): an unprivileged read of a locked-down source file returns empty output rather
437	    than failing, which would silently report no dependency where one exists.
438	    """
439	    awk = (
440	        r"tolower($0) ~ /^uris:/ || tolower($0) ~ /signed-by/ || tolower($0) ~ /^[ \t]*deb(-src)?[ \t]/ "
441	        r'{print FILENAME "\t" $0}'
442	    )
443	    # ONE start point that is always there, with `-path` selecting the two locations, rather
444	    # than naming `/etc/apt/sources.list.d` and `/etc/apt/sources.list` as two start points.
445	    # Measured: naming a `/etc/apt/sources.list` that is absent makes find complain on stderr
446	    # about that path and exit 1 while still walking the directory — so the two-start-point
447	    # form reports a legitimately-absent file with the same exit code as a scan that could
448	    # not run at all. That ambiguity is not affordable here: the scan's silence reads as "no
449	    # source file references any keyring", which deletes keys still in use. Selecting by
450	    # `-path` makes an absent file match nothing at exit 0, leaving a non-zero exit to mean
451	    # only a real failure, which `require_answer` fails the job on (ADR-022).

454	        f"sudo find {shlex.quote(APT_ROOT_DIR)} -maxdepth 2 -type f {selector} -exec awk {shlex.quote(awk)} {{}} +"
455	    )
456	    result = await run(command)
457	    require_answer(command, result, host)

459	    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
460	        path, tab, rest = line.partition("\t")
461	        if tab:
462	            lines_by_file.setdefault(Path(path).name, []).append(rest)

464	    for filename, file_lines in lines_by_file.items():
465	        _fmt, refs, uris = parse_source_file(filename, "\n".join(file_lines))
466	        parsed[filename] = (refs, uris)

572	        becomes the empty string, which reads as a version difference against the other
573	        machine and turns the whole manifest into upgrade proposals. Measured: `dpkg-query`

1	"""Shared package-sync pipeline: `PackageSyncJob`'s plan()/review/apply() split (D-15, D-16, D-24).
2	
3	Every package job (`apt_sync`, `snap_sync`, `flatpak_sync`, `manual_installs_sync`) is
4	independent (D-15): its own config, enable flag, failure isolation and progress. What is
5	here is what all four genuinely share — the plan/review/apply ORDER, the decision-file
6	rules, the review grouping and the converge loop. A manager's own item shapes, its own
7	diff and the facts only it can collect live in that manager's module, not here: a base
8	class holding one manager's logic makes the other three inherit a surface they never use
9	and cannot change. D-24 requires each job to present its
10	own batched review before that job's own first mutating command — the batching is per
11	manager, never across managers. The split of `plan()` from `apply()` exists to make that
12	review-before-any-change ordering checkable and testable per job:
13	
14	- `plan()` is ABSTRACT: each manager captures, queries and diffs its own way, and no diff
15	  shape is common to all four. What is common lives here as pieces an implementation
16	  calls — `filter_inert` (`packages/state.py`) on the way in, `_drop_inert_diffs` on the
17	  way out for identities no input item carries (`apt:hold:`, `snap:hold:`), and
18	  `_build_review_groups` at the end. Every implementation issues READ commands only.
19	- `accept_review()` stores this job's plan plus the outcome its own review returned, so
20	  `apply()` and the apt guards read a consistent pair.

22	  collecting per-item failures (D-27) so one bad item never stops the rest. It also
23	  persists a permanent decision (D-08a) for every `SKIP_ALWAYS`-decided item, on
24	  whichever machine holds it.
25	- `execute()` — the `SyncJob` entry point the orchestrator's sequential loop calls — is
26	  self-contained: it plans, reviews through the injected `JobContext.reviewer`, accepts the
27	  outcome, then applies. A `plan()` failure propagates naturally out of `execute()` and
28	  lands in this job's own `JobResult` through the orchestrator's per-job exception handling.
29	  A non-interactive run with a NON-EMPTY plan raises `JobSkipped` there instead of applying
30	  nothing and reporting SUCCESS; an empty plan on the same path stays SUCCESS.
31	"""

176	class PackageSyncJob(SyncJob):
177	    """Shared plan()/apply() pipeline every package-manager job subclasses.
178	
179	    Deliberately carries NO `name` ClassVar: `Orchestrator._resolve_sync_job_class` scans
180	    a job module's attributes for a `SyncJob` subclass whose `name` matches the module
181	    name (`getattr(attr, "name", None) == job_name`), so an abstract base without `name`
182	    is invisible to job discovery even when a concrete subclass imports it into scope.
183	    """

185	    manager_id: ClassVar[str]
186	
187	    def __init__(self, context: JobContext) -> None:
188	        super().__init__(context)
189	        self._accepted_plan: PackagePlan | None = None
190	        self._accepted_outcome: ReviewOutcome | None = None
191	        # Both machines' decision files as the last `plan()` call read them, so a subclass
192	        # that EXTENDS the base plan (only `apt_sync`, with its collateral and repo diffs)
193	        # can run `_drop_inert_diffs` over its own extra diffs without a second pair of
194	        # remote reads. Re-assigned on every `plan()`, never cached across calls.
195	        self._plan_decisions: tuple[Mapping[str, DecisionEntry], Mapping[str, DecisionEntry]] = ({}, {})
196	
197	    # -- Abstract hooks subclasses implement -------------------------------------------
