199	    @abstractmethod
200	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
201	        """Capture, diff and build this job's review groups. Read-only.
202	
203	        Every manager owns its own: what a diff even IS differs per ecosystem (apt has
204	        pins, holds and transaction collateral; snap converges a revision and a channel;
205	        flatpak carries scope and remote trust; a manual install has a snippet or has
206	        nothing). There is no diff shape all four share, so there is no base
207	        implementation to inherit — only the pieces below, which every implementation
208	        does use: `filter_inert` on the way in, `_drop_inert_diffs` on the way out, and
209	        `_build_review_groups` at the end.
210	
211	        Nothing here may mutate either machine: a job plans and reviews before it
212	        converges, so `plan()` runs before the user has approved anything. An
213	        implementation MUST load both machines' decision files and filter each side's
214	        items through its OWN file (D-08), then run the resulting diffs through
215	        `_drop_inert_diffs` to catch the recorded items no input-side filter can see —
216	        the block-state membership items (`apt:hold:`, `snap:hold:`) and anything else
217	        whose identity is derived rather than carried on an input item.
218	        """
219	        ...
220	
221	    @abstractmethod
222	    async def converge(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
223	        """Apply one approved diff on the target.
224	
225	        May raise `ConvergeItemFailed` to refuse the item without even attempting the
226	        mutating command (e.g. a transaction-safety guard); otherwise returns the
227	        `CommandResult` of the converge command, whose `.success` decides pass/fail.
228	        Called for every APPLY-decided diff whose action is `INSTALL`, `REMOVE` or
229	        `CHANGE` — `REPORT_ONLY` diffs never reach this hook (see `apply()`).
230	        """
231	        ...
232	
233	    @property
234	    def machines(self) -> Machines:
235	        """The two machines' own names, for every string this job puts in front of the user."""
236	        return Machines(source=self.context.source_hostname, target=self.context.target_hostname)
237	
238	    @staticmethod
239	    def _decision_holder_is_source(action: DiffAction) -> bool:
240	        """D-08a's holder rule: an `INSTALL`/`CHANGE` diff is source-held (the source has
241	        the item, or the version it should converge to), a `REMOVE` diff target-held.
242	
243	        One definition shared by the WRITE path (`_record_permanent_skips` picks the
244	        executor whose file gets the entry) and the READ path (`_drop_inert_diffs` picks
245	        the file to look the item up in), so the machine a skip-always lands on is by
246	        construction the machine it is read back from.
247	        """
248	        return action in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE)
249	
250	    def _drop_inert_diffs(
251	        self,
252	        diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff],
253	        source_decisions: Mapping[str, DecisionEntry],
254	        target_decisions: Mapping[str, DecisionEntry],
255	    ) -> tuple[ItemDiff, ...]:
256	        """Drop every diff whose `item_id` is recorded "skip always" on the machine that
257	        holds it (D-08/D-08a) — the post-diff counterpart to `filter_inert`.
258	
259	        Required for any diff whose identity does not exist on an input item and so cannot
260	        be filtered at the diff-input boundary: the block-state membership items
261	        (`apt:hold:<name>`, `snap:hold:<name>`) are derived from hold-set membership, and
262	        apt's repo/collateral diffs are derived from directory digests. Without this pass
263	        a permanently-declined hold is re-emitted every run — and in the add direction it
264	        comes back default-checked, so a bulk accept applies the very hold the user
265	        declined.
266	
267	        `REPORT_ONLY` diffs pass through untouched: they carry no converge verb, so
268	        `_record_permanent_skips` never records one and there is no holder to match.
269	        """
270	        kept: list[ItemDiff] = []
271	        for diff in diffs:
272	            if diff.action not in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE, DiffAction.REMOVE):
273	                kept.append(diff)
274	                continue
275	            holder = source_decisions if self._decision_holder_is_source(diff.action) else target_decisions
276	            if diff.item_id not in holder:
277	                kept.append(diff)
278	        return tuple(kept)
279	
280	    def _build_review_groups(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff]) -> tuple[ReviewGroup, ...]:
281	        """One `ReviewGroup` per `(action, item_class)` present in `diffs`, keyed on
282	        `(manager, action)` for the reviewer's removal-direction test (D-24) so removals
283	        never share a group with installs. The title's verb and every entry's
284	        `action_label` come from `_ACTION_VOCABULARY`, keyed by the group's own item
285	        class — so a block-state membership item (`apt:hold:`, `snap:hold:`,
286	        `flatpak:mask:`) whose add direction shares the `INSTALL` action with a package
287	        still reads "Hold/Mask ..." rather than displaying under "Install packages"
288	        (#208). `_ITEM_CLASS_NOUN` does the same for the title's OBJECT, so the one
289	        reviewed class that is not a package — `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d` — is not announced as
290	        one. Grouping by item class as well as action is what keeps that verb correct
291	        when one action mixes item classes (e.g. apt package INSTALL alongside apt hold
292	        INSTALL); the group's `action` value stays the raw `DiffAction` so add-direction
293	        stays default-checked and remove-direction lands in its own unticked group.
294	
295	        Emission order: `_ACTION_ORDER` (install, change, remove, report) outer, and
296	        within one action the item classes in first-seen order — which, because
297	        `_diff_apt_packages` emits package diffs before hold diffs, keeps a package group
298	        ahead of its hold group.
299	        """
300	        # A reported condition is keyed by its CAUSE as well (ruled by the user): version
301	        # drift, an origin the target cannot reproduce and a package installed from two
302	        # different repositories were one group called "Report apt packages", which named
303	        # none of them. `DiffClass` is that cause, and report-only is the one action whose
304	        # members carry different ones.
305	        by_key: dict[tuple[DiffAction, ItemClass, DiffClass | None], list[ItemDiff]] = {}
306	        class_order: dict[DiffAction, list[tuple[ItemClass, DiffClass | None]]] = {}
307	        for diff in diffs:
308	            cause = diff.diff_class if diff.action is DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY else None
309	            key = (diff.action, diff.item_class, cause)
310	            if key not in by_key:
311	                by_key[key] = []
312	                class_order.setdefault(diff.action, []).append((diff.item_class, cause))
313	            by_key[key].append(diff)
314	
315	        groups: list[ReviewGroup] = []
316	        for action in _ACTION_ORDER:
317	            for item_class, cause in class_order.get(action, []):
318	                entries = by_key[(action, item_class, cause)]
319	                # REPORT_ONLY has no more-specific per-item-class meaning for any current
320	                # manager (IN-01): fall back to "report" rather than the raw enum value
321	                # ("report_only"), which read awkwardly in review text like "Report_only
322	                # flatpak packages". Every other action still falls back to its own
323	                # `action.value`, unchanged.
324	                default_verb = "report" if action == DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY else action.value
325	                verb = _ACTION_VOCABULARY.get((item_class, action), default_verb)
326	                noun = _ITEM_CLASS_NOUN.get(item_class, f"{self.manager_id} packages")
327	                title = f"{verb.capitalize()} {noun}"
328	                note = None
329	                if cause is not None:
330	                    title = f"{_REPORT_TITLES.get(cause, 'Reported').format(target=self.machines.target)} ({noun})"
331	                    # A manager with no upgrade command of its own gets no note rather than
332	                    # a sentence with a hole in it.
333	                    upgrade = _UPGRADE_COMMANDS.get(self.manager_id)
334	                    template = _REPORT_NOTES.get(cause)
335	                    if template and upgrade:
336	                        note = template.format(target=self.machines.target, upgrade=upgrade)
337	                groups.append(
338	                    ReviewGroup(
339	                        manager=self.manager_id,
340	                        action=action.value,
341	                        title=title,
342	                        note=note or None,
343	                        entries=tuple(
344	                            ReviewEntry(item_id=diff.item_id, label=diff.label, action_label=verb, detail=diff.detail)
345	                            for diff in entries
346	                        ),
347	                    )
348	                )
349	        return tuple(groups)

351	    # -- plan() / accept_review() / apply() / execute() -------------------------------
352	
353	    def accept_review(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> None:
354	        """Store this job's plan plus the outcome its own review returned."""
355	        self._accepted_plan = plan
356	        self._accepted_outcome = outcome
357	
358	    async def after_review(self) -> None:
359	        """Hook: work that must run AFTER this job's review returns but BEFORE any
360	        mutation on the target (`apply()`).
361	
362	        No-op on the base — the three managers that produce no unreproducible items (apt,
363	        snap, flatpak) need nothing between review and converge. Only `manual_installs_sync`
364	        overrides it (D-23): it pushes the freshly reconciled install-snippet registry to
365	        the target here, so a snippet the user authored during THIS run's review is on the
366	        target before `apply()` replays it. Keeping the hook on the base leaves `execute()`
367	        the single source of the plan/review/apply order rather than each manager
368	        re-deriving it.
369	        """
370	        return
371	
372	    async def apply(self) -> None:
373	        """Converge every APPLY-decided diff from the accepted plan, one item at a time.
374	
375	        Per-item detail at `LogLevel.FULL`, one `LogLevel.INFO` summary line per job
376	        (ADR-010). A per-item failure (`ConvergeItemFailed`, or a converge command that
377	        exits non-zero) is caught, logged with its stderr as structured context, and
378	        collected — the loop always completes (D-27) — then `PackageItemFailures` is
379	        raised once, after the loop, if anything failed OR anything is left unresolved
380	        (D-21) — even when `total` is zero, since an interactive run whose ONLY diffs
381	        were unreproducible items never has any INSTALL/CHANGE/REMOVE work to do, and
382	        must still fail if one of them ended up unresolved.
383	
384	        Dry-run (ADR-014): each intended action is logged at FULL with a `[dry-run] `
385	        prefix, carrying the diff's own detail, and no converge command is ever issued.
386	
387	        `REPORT_ONLY` diffs are excluded here regardless of decision: they imply no
388	        converge verb (D-25's version-mismatch, repo-unavailable, origin-mismatch and
389	        unreproducible classes are informational), so `converge()` is never called
390	        for one even if something recorded `APPLY` against it.
391	
392	        Before converging anything, `_record_permanent_skips` persists a `DecisionEntry`
393	        for every `SKIP_ALWAYS`-decided item (D-08). The `_finalize_unreproducible` hook
394	        then persists this run's authored snippets and unreproducible-item skip-always
395	        decisions (D-20/D-21/D-23); it is a no-op on the base and only
396	        `manual_installs_sync` implements it (D-18), but the call site stays here so both
397	        run before any converge, independent of whether this run applies anything else
398	        (a run with zero installs but one newly-authored snippet still records it). The
399	        `_unresolved_as_failures` hook (also no-op on the base, overridden only by
400	        `manual_installs_sync`) supplies the genuinely-undecided items that fail an
401	        interactive run — which is why `total == 0` can still raise `PackageItemFailures`.
402	        """
403	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
404	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
405	        plan = self._accepted_plan
406	        outcome = self._accepted_outcome
407	        decisions = outcome.decisions
408	
409	        await self._record_permanent_skips(plan, decisions)
410	        await self._finalize_unreproducible(plan, outcome)
411	
412	        apply_diffs = [
413	            diff
414	            for diff in plan.diffs
415	            if decisions.get(diff.item_id) == Decision.APPLY and diff.action != DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY
416	        ]
417	        prefix = "[dry-run] " if self.context.dry_run else ""
418	        total = len(apply_diffs)
419	
420	        failures: list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]] = []
421	        if total == 0:
422	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.INFO, f"{prefix}No {self.manager_id} changes to apply")
423	            self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=100))
424	        else:
425	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.INFO, f"{prefix}Applying {total} {self.manager_id} change(s)")
426	
427	            for index, diff in enumerate(apply_diffs):
428	                if self.context.dry_run:
429	                    # The detail belongs on the line, not only in the review panel: a
430	                    # dry run never renders that panel, and ADR-014 makes the preview
431	                    # the whole report. Without it the preview says strictly less about
432	                    # an item than the interactive review does.
433	                    detail = f" — {diff.detail}" if diff.detail else ""
434	                    self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"{prefix}Would {diff.action.value} {diff.label}{detail}")
435	                else:
436	                    await self._converge_one(diff, failures)
437	                self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=int((index + 1) / total * 100)))
438	
439	            succeeded = total - len(failures)
440	            self._log(
441	                Host.TARGET,
442	                LogLevel.INFO,
443	                f"{prefix}{succeeded}/{total} {self.manager_id} change(s) applied",
444	            )
445	
446	        all_failures = [*failures, *self._unresolved_as_failures(plan, outcome)]
447	        if all_failures:
448	            summary = "; ".join(f"{diff.label}: {stderr.strip()}" for diff, stderr in all_failures)
449	            self._log(
450	                Host.TARGET,
451	                LogLevel.INFO,
452	                f"{len(all_failures)} {self.manager_id} item(s) failed: {summary}",
453	            )
454	            raise PackageItemFailures(self.manager_id, all_failures)

456	    def _unresolved_as_failures(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]]:
457	        """Hook: this job's genuinely-undecided items that fail an interactive run (D-27).
458	
459	        No-op on the base — it returns an empty list, so the three managers that produce
460	        no unreproducible items (apt, snap, flatpak) never fail on this basis. Only
461	        `manual_installs_sync` overrides it (D-18/D-21): an unreproducible item left with
462	        neither a snippet nor a recorded decision after an interactive review fails the
463	        job. The D-27 converge-failure contract in `apply()` is unchanged — converge
464	        failures fail the job regardless of what this hook returns.
465	        """
466	        return []

469	        """Hook: persist this job's unreproducible-item snippet authoring and skip-always

472	        No-op on the base — only `manual_installs_sync` produces unreproducible items

478	    async def _record_permanent_skips(self, plan: PackagePlan, decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]) -> None:
479	        """Persist a `DecisionEntry` for every `SKIP_ALWAYS`-decided, actionable diff.
480	
481	        D-08a decides WHICH machine's file gets the entry by which machine HOLDS the
482	        item: `INSTALL`/`CHANGE` diffs are source-held (the source has the item, or the
483	        version it should converge to), so they record on `self.source`; `REMOVE` diffs
484	        are target-held (only the target has the item), so they record on `self.target`
485	        — through the remote executor, never a local write (ADR-002).
486	
487	        `REPORT_ONLY` diffs are skipped: they carry no converge verb (version-mismatch,
488	        repo-unavailable, origin-mismatch and unreproducible are informational only), so
489	        there is no "holder" for D-08a to record against.
490	
491	        Two guards, both required before anything is ever written: never for a
492	        non-interactive outcome (D-26 — nothing is recorded permanently when nothing
493	        was actually decided by a human), and never during a dry run (ADR-014 — a
494	        rehearsal must leave no trace).
495	        """
496	        if self.context.dry_run or not self._accepted_outcome_was_interactive():
497	            return
498	
499	        recorded_at = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
500	        for diff in plan.diffs:
501	            if decisions.get(diff.item_id) != Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS:
502	                continue
503	            if diff.action not in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE, DiffAction.REMOVE):
504	                continue
505	
506	            executor = self.source if self._decision_holder_is_source(diff.action) else self.target
507	            await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, executor).record(
508	                DecisionEntry(
509	                    item_id=diff.item_id,
510	                    item_class=diff.item_class,
511	                    label=diff.label,
512	                    reason=None,
513	                    recorded_at=recorded_at,
514	                )
515	            )
516	
517	    def _accepted_outcome_was_interactive(self) -> bool:
518	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
519	        return self._accepted_outcome.was_interactive
520	
521	    async def _converge_one(self, diff: ItemDiff, failures: list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]]) -> None:
522	        try:
523	            result = await self.converge(diff)
524	        except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
525	            failures.append((diff, str(exc)))
526	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.ERROR, f"{diff.label} failed: {exc}", stderr=str(exc))
527	            return
528	
529	        if result.success:
530	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"{diff.action.value} {diff.label}")
531	        else:
532	            failures.append((diff, result.stderr))
533	            self._log(
534	                Host.TARGET,
535	                LogLevel.ERROR,
536	                f"{diff.label} failed: {result.stderr.strip()}",
537	                stderr=result.stderr,
538	            )
539	
540	    async def execute(self) -> None:
541	        """The `SyncJob` entry point the orchestrator's sequential job loop calls.
542	
543	        Self-contained (D-24): plan this job's diffs, review its own groups through the
544	        injected `JobContext.reviewer`, accept the outcome, run the `after_review()` hook
545	        (the seam where `manual_installs_sync` pushes its snippet registry, D-23), then
546	        apply. No component outside the job owns its review, and no fallback applies diffs
547	        that never came back from one — a missing reviewer fails loudly here rather than
548	        silently skipping the review and converging unreviewed diffs (T-02-38).
549	
550	        A `plan()` failure propagates unchanged, so the orchestrator's per-job exception
551	        handling attributes it to this job's own `JobResult`.
552	
553	        A non-interactive run with a non-empty plan raises `JobSkipped`: D-26 forces every
554	        item to SKIP_ONCE with nobody present to decide, so continuing would converge
555	        nothing and report SUCCESS. It is raised before `after_review()`, so
556	        `manual_installs_sync` does not push its registry either, and before any mutating
557	        command, as `JobSkipped` requires. An EMPTY plan on the same path stays SUCCESS —
558	        the target already matches the source, which is the goal met.
559	        """
560	        assert self.context.reviewer is not None, (
561	            f"{self.manager_id} sync has no reviewer; the orchestrator must inject one "
562	            "through JobContext.reviewer before execute()."
563	        )
564	        plan = await self.plan()
565	        outcome = await self.context.reviewer.review(plan.groups)
566	        if plan.groups and not outcome.was_interactive:
567	            raise JobSkipped(
568	                self.name,
569	                f"non-interactive run left every {self.manager_id} review item undecided",
570	            )
571	        self.accept_review(plan, outcome)
572	        await self.after_review()
573	        await self.apply()

1	"""Batched review — the single interaction surface for every package diff (D-24).
2	
3	Each package job computes its own set of differences against the source's manifest and hands
4	them to `review_items` as `ReviewGroup`s before applying anything. The user answers one
5	screen per group in one sitting rather than a sequence of yes/no prompts.
6	
7	An actionable group is one `decision_list` screen (`packages.decision_list`): every item on
8	its own row, the decision it currently carries in a column to the right, one key per answer.
9	Nothing is echoed afterwards — the answered list stays in the scrollback, and the decision
10	column is the record. That also removes the Rich panel that used to precede each screen:
11	the control lists the items itself, so a panel above it said everything twice. The panel
12	survives only where there is nothing to answer, on the non-interactive path (D-26), where it
13	IS the report.
14	
15	This composes with the single persistent Live display (Phase 1 plans 01-17/01-18) exactly
16	as `TerminalUIConfirmer.confirm` (`pcswitcher.confirmer`) does: pause the live region before
17	the prompt, run the blocking prompt off the event loop via `asyncio.to_thread` (ADR-005 —
18	no blocking calls on the event loop), and resume it in a `finally` so the terminal is always
19	handed back even if the prompt raises.
20	
21	Removals get their own group, never sharing a screen with installs (D-07/D-24): a bulk
22	confirm that also deleted software would be exactly the silent-destruction failure D-07
23	exists to prevent, which is also why a removal-direction row starts at skip-once while an
24	install-direction row starts applied. Which of a caller's `ReviewGroup`s are
25	"removal-direction" is decided by `ReviewGroup.action`; grouping itself (turning an
26	`ItemDiff` into `ReviewGroup`s keyed by manager+action) belongs to
27	`PackageSyncJob._build_review_groups`, and this module only consumes already-grouped input.
28	
29	`ask_gate` is the one question here that is NOT a review item: a two-answer yes/no about the
30	target's environment, asked before any group is built, whose "no" answer means there is no
31	review to hold (`apt_sync`'s Ubuntu Pro gate, ADR-020 D-38). It lives here because this
32	module already owns pause-the-live-UI-ask-resume, interactivity detection and the
33	Ctrl-C-aborts-the-sync rule; it returns `None` when nobody could be asked, and the caller
34	owns what that means.
35	
36	D-07's three answers are all on the one screen for an actionable group (install / change /
37	remove direction, which includes the block-state items): apply, skip now, or skip for good —
38	treat the item as specific to one machine, which makes it inert here in both roles (D-08a).
39	Those are the decisions; what each screen CALLS them is `_options_for` and the hints beside
40	them, which say the act, the machine it happens to, and how long the answer lasts.
41	`REPORT_ONLY` groups offer the first two only: an informational item has no machine that
42	holds it, so a permanent mark would silently stop the underlying package syncing rather than
43	stop reporting the condition.
44	
45	`PACKAGE_REVIEW_AUTOMATION_ENV`: undocumented escape hatch for integration tests, which run
46	without a TTY and cannot drive a real terminal prompt. When set, its value is trusted JSON
47	(no schema validation) mapping item_id -> decision, applied instead of prompting. It never
48	widens what the review offers (D-25 items are still exactly what the caller passed in) and
49	is deliberately absent from `--help`, the config schema and user docs (D-26).
50	
51	A `ReviewGroup` whose `action` is `UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION` gets a different
52	interaction shape from every other group (D-21): instead of a row on a decision screen, each
53	entry is resolved one at a time with a three-way choice — write the commands that install
54	it, mark it as belonging to the source machine alone, or skip for now — because "should this
55	apply" is not the question for an item no package manager can reproduce; "how does the other
56	machine get this" is.
57	`ReviewOutcome.snippets` carries that group's authored snippets back to the caller
58	(`PackageSyncJob.apply()`), which persists them. An interactive review always resolves
59	every entry (decision 10): an empty snippet capture re-prompts rather than falling through
60	to an "unresolved" state, and Ctrl-C anywhere in the review aborts the whole sync
61	(`SyncAbortedByUser`) rather than skipping items. `ReviewOutcome.unresolved` is therefore
62	populated only on the non-interactive path, where it reports (never fails) the items no
63	one was present to resolve (D-26).
64	
65	A `ReviewGroup` whose `action` is `REPO_REMOVAL_REVIEW_ACTION` uses the same screen with one
66	fewer answer (ADR-020 D-07): delete, or leave it for now. It starts at skip-once like every
67	other removal direction and is never offered permanence, so `Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS` is
68	unreachable for it and nothing about it is ever recorded. That is why `_REMOVAL_ACTIONS` and
69	`_PROMOTABLE_ACTIONS` are two independent sets rather than one derived from the other. An
70	entry carrying `ReviewEntry.content` prints that whole file first: a pin file's name says
71	nothing about what it does, and its name is all a decision row can show.
72	
73	A `ReviewGroup` whose `action` is `REPO_CONFLICT_REVIEW_ACTION` is the same two-answer screen
74	(ADR-020 D-37) preceded by its own content: something that differs on the two machines and
75	feeds an item the target recorded machine-specific — a repository file for `apt_sync`, a
76	remote for `flatpak_sync` — is printed as both versions, never a unified diff, before the one
77	screen that answers overwrite or skip-once for all of them. Nothing is recorded either way,
78	and it starts at skip-once: an overwrite moves software the target explicitly marked
79	machine-specific, so it is chosen, never defaulted.
80	
81	A `ReviewGroup` whose `action` is `COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION` likewise gets its own
82	interaction shape (D-30): each entry is a package the TARGET's own apt has marked manually
83	installed and the pending transaction would remove or downgrade, resolved one at a time
84	with a three-way choice — go ahead, keep the package, or stop the whole sync. The decision
85	is recorded against the entry's `item_id` (the triggering change, set by the caller), so
86	"go ahead" proceeds with it, "keep" leaves it unapproved, and "stop" raises
87	`SyncAbortedByUser` naming the collateral package. A non-interactive run leaves every
88	collateral entry `SKIP_ONCE` like every other item, so the change it gates is simply not
89	approved (D-26).
90	
91	Every screen here names the two machines by hostname. `review_items` takes both and they
92	are required: what an answer costs is "nomad loses this package", never "the target loses
93	this package", and no wording in this module may fall back to the tool's own vocabulary for
94	the user's computers. Source and target survive as the names of the ROLES in code,
95	docstrings and logs, which is where they belong.
96	"""

330	    return action in _PROMOTABLE_ACTIONS

333	# The keys that set a decision. `y` for the act, `s` for the answer that lasts one sync, and
334	# `x` — a cross, read as "exclude" — for the one that is recorded. NOT `n`: `y` and `n` read
335	# as a yes/no pair, so `n` invited "no, not now" from the answer that actually means never
336	# again. `a` is unavailable: it is conventionally Abort in a terminal prompt, and
337	# `decision_list` rejects it.
338	_APPLY_KEY = "y"
339	_SKIP_NOW_KEY = "s"
340	_SKIP_ALWAYS_KEY = "x"
341	
342	# The words the decision column shows for the answers that are not the act. They are short
343	# because they share a column with the act verb, past the longest item on the screen; what
344	# each one commits the user to is said in the legend hint beside it, which has room for a
345	# sentence.
346	SKIP_NOW_WORD = "skip now"
347	KEEP_FOR_GOOD_WORD = "keep for good"
348	
349	# A reported condition is not converged in either direction, so neither of its answers is an
350	# act: one says the user has read it, the other that it should come back.
351	ACKNOWLEDGED_WORD = "acknowledged"
352	REPORT_AGAIN_WORD = "report again"
353	
354	# Verbs whose sentences take a preposition other than "on". "remove from nomad" and "never
355	# install it to nomad" are the two the English wants; "hold on nomad", "change on nomad" and
356	# "never hold it on nomad" take the default. A verb missing from both sets reads correctly
357	# with "on", which is why they are enumerated rather than derived.
358	_VERBS_TAKING_FROM = frozenset({"remove", "delete"})
359	_VERBS_TAKING_TO = frozenset({"install", "add"})
360	
361	
362	# Filled / hollow / crossed. The glyph is what carries the row's state, so the screen stays
363	# readable in a terminal whose background colours the user cannot distinguish.
364	_APPLY_GLYPH = "●"
365	_SKIP_ONCE_GLYPH = "○"
366	_SKIP_ALWAYS_GLYPH = "⊘"

369	def _group_act_word(group: ReviewGroup) -> str:
370	    """The verb the group's rows share, used for the act option's legend and column word.
371	
372	    The commonest `action_label` rather than the first: it is the one the group title
373	    already names, so it is the one a row does NOT need to repeat.
374	    """
375	    counts = Counter(entry.action_label for entry in group.entries)
376	    return counts.most_common(1)[0][0] if counts else "apply"

379	def _default_decision(action: str) -> Decision:
380	    """Where a group's rows start before the user touches anything.
381	
382	    Install-direction rows start applied; anything that removes, deletes or disables starts
383	    at skip-once — and so does the repository/remote overwrite, which moves software the
384	    target explicitly marked machine-specific. Confirming a screen unread must never destroy
385	    or displace something the user did not choose.
386	    """
387	    if _is_removal_direction(action) or _is_repo_conflict_group(action):
388	        return Decision.SKIP_ONCE
389	    return Decision.APPLY

392	def _act_word(group: ReviewGroup) -> str:
393	    """The word for the answer that acts — the group's own verb, except where nothing acts."""
394	    if group.action == _REPORT_ACTION:
395	        return ACKNOWLEDGED_WORD
396	    return _group_act_word(group)

399	def _skip_now_word(group: ReviewGroup) -> str:
400	    """The word for the answer that lasts one sync.
401	
402	    "skip now" on every screen, whatever the direction, so the key means one thing across a
403	    review — including the conflict screen, whose version-keeping is stated in its hint
404	    rather than in the word. The report screen is the exception in substance, not in
405	    phrasing: its second answer asks for the condition to be raised again, which is not a
406	    skip of anything.
407	    """
408	    return REPORT_AGAIN_WORD if group.action == _REPORT_ACTION else SKIP_NOW_WORD

411	def _skip_always_word(group: ReviewGroup) -> str:
412	    """The word for the answer that is recorded and never asked about again.
413	
414	    Said as this screen's own act, not as a generic "always skip": on a removal screen the
415	    item is on the target and the answer keeps it, while everywhere else the item is not
416	    there at all and the answer is that it never arrives. One word cannot be both.
417	    """
418	    if _is_removal_direction(group.action):
419	        return KEEP_FOR_GOOD_WORD
420	    return f"never {_group_act_word(group)}"

423	def _hints(group: ReviewGroup, source_hostname: str, target_hostname: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
424	    """The act / skip-now / skip-always sentences for this screen's legend.
425	
426	    Each says what the answer DOES — the act named as itself on the machine it happens to,
427	    and each skip as the state it leaves behind plus how long that lasts. Not "go ahead" or
428	    "leave nomad alone": a neutral word for the act is the same non-answer as "apply", and
429	    the user is reading these to find out what the key does, not to be reassured.
430	
431	    Four shapes, because the answers genuinely differ by direction. A reported condition
432	    converges nothing either way; a conflict is a choice between two versions of one file;
433	    an item already on the target is kept rather than refused; everything else arrives or
434	    does not.
435	    """
436	    verb = _group_act_word(group)
437	    if group.action == _REPORT_ACTION:
438	        # Third element unused: a report group is never promotable, so no screen shows it.
439	        return (
440	            f"nothing on {target_hostname} changes; you have read it",
441	            f"nothing on {target_hostname} changes; raise it again next sync",
442	            "",
443	        )
444	    if _is_repo_conflict_group(group.action):
445	        return (
446	            f"{target_hostname} changes this sync",
447	            f"keep {target_hostname}'s version; will be asked again next sync",
448	            "",
449	        )
450	
451	    takes_from = verb in _VERBS_TAKING_FROM
452	    act = f"{verb} {'from' if takes_from else 'on'} {target_hostname}"
453	    now = (
454	        f"keep on {target_hostname} for now; will be asked again next sync"
455	        if takes_from
456	        else f"do not {verb} on {target_hostname} for now; will be asked again next sync"
457	    )
458	    if _is_removal_direction(group.action) or group.action == _CHANGE_ACTION:
459	        # The item is already on the target, so the recorded answer protects what is there
460	        # rather than refusing an arrival — and it protects it in both directions, which is
461	        # what "never touch it" says and "never remove it" would not.
462	        return act, now, f"this is specific to {target_hostname}; pc-switcher will never touch it"
463	    preposition = "to" if verb in _VERBS_TAKING_TO else "on"
464	    return (
465	        act,
466	        now,
467	        f"this is specific to {source_hostname}; pc-switcher will never {verb} it {preposition} "
468	        f"{target_hostname} or other machines",
469	    )

472	def _options_for(group: ReviewGroup, *, source_hostname: str, target_hostname: str) -> tuple[DecisionOption, ...]:
473	    """The answers one group's screen offers — three, or two where D-07 records nothing.
474	
475	    The same widget either way: the user sees a missing option in the legend rather than a
476	    differently-shaped prompt.
477	    """
478	    act_hint, now_hint, always_hint = _hints(group, source_hostname, target_hostname)
479	    options = [
480	        DecisionOption(
481	            value=Decision.APPLY,
482	            key=_APPLY_KEY,
483	            word=_act_word(group),
484	            glyph=_APPLY_GLYPH,
485	            is_act=True,
486	            hint=act_hint,
487	        ),
488	        DecisionOption(
489	            value=Decision.SKIP_ONCE,
490	            key=_SKIP_NOW_KEY,
491	            word=_skip_now_word(group),
492	            glyph=_SKIP_ONCE_GLYPH,
493	            hint=now_hint,
494	        ),
495	    ]
496	    if _is_promotable_group(group.action):
497	        options.append(
498	            DecisionOption(
499	                value=Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS,
500	                key=_SKIP_ALWAYS_KEY,
501	                word=_skip_always_word(group),
502	                glyph=_SKIP_ALWAYS_GLYPH,
503	                is_permanent=True,
504	                hint=always_hint,
505	            )
506	        )
507	    return tuple(options)

510	def _rows_for(group: ReviewGroup) -> tuple[DecisionRow, ...]:
511	    """One row per entry, with the group's own verb stripped off the label.
512	
513	    Every row of an `AptSyncJob`/`PackageSyncJob` group carries the same `action_label` as
514	    its title's verb, so prefixing each row with it said the same word once per line. A row
515	    whose action genuinely differs keeps it, in both places it matters: as a prefix on the
516	    item, and as its own word in the decision column.
517	    """
518	    act_word = _group_act_word(group)
519	    default = _default_decision(group.action)
520	    return tuple(
521	        DecisionRow(
522	            row_id=entry.item_id,
523	            label=entry.label,
524	            default=default,
525	            prefix=None if entry.action_label == act_word else entry.action_label,
526	            act_word=None if entry.action_label == act_word else entry.action_label,
527	            detail=entry.detail,
528	        )
529	        for entry in group.entries
530	    )

533	def _snippet_authoring_note(target_hostname: str) -> str:
534	    """Printed once before the multi-line capture, so a user does not author a snippet that
535	    hangs the sync (T-02-18): the executor supplies no stdin, and a worked shape showing the
536	    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive + dependency-fix pattern is cheaper to read here than to
537	    discover as a stuck sync. Said as what happens on the machine that will run it, rather
538	    than as a fact about the executor.
539	    """
540	    return (
541	        f"These commands run on {target_hostname} with nobody watching — there is no keyboard\n"
542	        "attached to them, so a command that asks a question (e.g. a debconf prompt) hangs the\n"
543	        "sync instead of failing. A typical shape:\n\n"
544	        "  sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive dpkg --install /path/to/package.deb || \\\n"
545	        "  sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install --assume-yes --fix-broken\n"
546	    )

549	# Shown in place of questionary's own multiline instruction, which offers "Alt+Enter or Esc
550	# then Enter" — two chords for one gesture, neither of which a user guesses.

554	def _snippet_submit_bindings() -> KeyBindings:
555	    """Ctrl-D finishes the snippet: prompt_toolkit's own end-of-input gesture, and the one a
556	    user reaches for in a multi-line capture.
557	
558	    Scoped to this editor only. Ctrl-D as an ABORT anywhere else stays unhandled — that is a
559	    separate question this does not reopen.
560	    """
561	    bindings = KeyBindings()
562	
563	    def submit(event: KeyPressEvent) -> None:
564	        event.current_buffer.validate_and_handle()
565	
566	    bindings.add(Keys.ControlD, eager=True)(submit)
567	    return bindings

573	# highlight and for a multi-line editor is the whole thing the user is typing. A shell
574	# snippet is not an answer to be echoed back; it is text being written, and it reads as

579	def _render_group_panel(group: ReviewGroup) -> Panel:
580	    """Build the REPORT panel for one group — the non-interactive path only, where there is
581	    nothing to answer and this is all the user gets (D-26).
582	
583	    An interactive run never prints it: the decision screen lists the same items, and a
584	    panel above it made every group appear twice.
585	
586	    Package names, versions and stderr fragments come from package-manager output and
587	    must never reach a `Panel` as a bare `str` — Rich would parse `[...]`-shaped
588	    substrings as console markup and raise `MarkupError` (T-02-02).
589	    """
590	    body = Text()
591	    for index, entry in enumerate(group.entries):
592	        if index:
593	            # Separator, not terminator: a newline after the last entry renders as an empty
594	            # final line inside the panel border.
595	            body.append("\n")
596	        body.append(entry.action_label, style="bold")
597	        body.append(" ")
598	        body.append(entry.label)
599	        if entry.detail:
600	            body.append(" (")
601	            body.append(entry.detail, style="dim")
602	            body.append(")")
603	    return Panel(body, title=Text(group.title), border_style="cyan")

656	async def _ask_about_one_item(
657	    entry: ReviewEntry,
658	    *,
659	    title: str,
660	    options: Sequence[DecisionOption],
661	    default: str,
662	    detail: str | None = None,
663	) -> str:
664	    """Put ONE item on a decision screen and return the answer's value.
665	
666	    Some questions cannot be batched: a collateral package's answers name the change that
667	    causes it, and an unreproducible item's "install" answer opens an editor. Both were
668	    plain pickers of sentence-long choices, which made them the two screens in the review
669	    that looked nothing like the rest of it. The shape is what is shared here, not the
670	    batching — one row, the same glyphs, colours, keys and hint column.
671	
672	    Ctrl-C (`ask` returns `None`) is the caller's to interpret: what stopping means differs
673	    between an item that can be left undecided and one that cannot.
674	    """
675	    prompt = decision_list(
676	        title,
677	        rows=[DecisionRow(row_id=entry.item_id, label=entry.label, default=default, detail=detail or entry.detail)],
678	        options=options,
679	    )
680	    answered: Mapping[str, str] | None = await asyncio.to_thread(prompt.ask)
681	    if answered is None:
682	        raise SyncAbortedByUser(f"package review aborted at {entry.label!r} (Ctrl-C)")
683	    return answered[entry.item_id]

686	async def _review_unreproducible_group(
687	    group: ReviewGroup,
688	    *,
689	    console: Console,
690	    source_hostname: str,
691	    target_hostname: str,
692	    decisions: dict[str, Decision],
693	    snippets: dict[str, str],
694	) -> None:
695	    """Resolve one `UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION` group's entries, one at a time, with
696	    the three-way choice D-21 requires: write an install snippet, skip for now, or never
697	    install it here. One item per screen, because answering "install" opens an editor for
698	    that item — but a decision screen like every other, so the review has one shape.
699	
700	    All three choices are VALID resolutions (D-21): a snippet, a skip-always, and an
701	    explicit skip-once. There is no fourth "genuinely undecided" outcome (decision 10 —
702	    unresolved must be unrepresentable in an interactive flow):
703	
704	    - Ctrl-C at the resolution screen means the user wants to stop, so `_ask_about_one_item`
705	      aborts the ENTIRE sync with `SyncAbortedByUser` — never a per-item
706	      skip-and-mark-unresolved.
707	    - Choosing "add an install snippet" and then submitting an empty body (or abandoning
708	      the editor) is NOT accepted and does NOT fall through: the three-way choice is
709	      re-prompted so the user must supply a real snippet or pick an explicit skip.
710	
711	    The body is STORED verbatim, never stripped — D-20 forbids reasoning about it, and
712	    leading whitespace/newlines are the user's own formatting choice. Emptiness is decided
713	    on the stripped body, though: a body of only spaces and newlines replays as nothing at
714	    all, so accepting it would record a snippet that resolves the item without installing
715	    anything.
716	    """
717	    options = _unreproducible_options(source_hostname, target_hostname)
718	    for entry in group.entries:
719	        # Re-prompt until the entry is resolved by a real snippet or an explicit skip. An
720	        # empty snippet capture loops back here rather than manufacturing an unresolved
721	        # item (decision 10); a cancelled screen breaks out by aborting the whole sync.
722	        while True:
723	            selected = await _ask_about_one_item(
724	                entry,
725	                title=f"How should {target_hostname} get {entry.label}?",
726	                options=options,
727	                default=_ADD_SNIPPET_VALUE,
728	            )
729	
730	            if selected == Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS:
731	                decisions[entry.item_id] = Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS
732	                break
733	
734	            if selected == Decision.SKIP_ONCE:
735	                # An explicit "skip now" is a real decision (D-21): the item is resolved
736	                # for this run.
737	                decisions[entry.item_id] = Decision.SKIP_ONCE
738	                break
739	
740	            # selected == _ADD_SNIPPET_VALUE
741	            console.print(Text(_snippet_authoring_note(target_hostname), style="dim"))
742	            body_prompt = questionary.text(
743	                f"Install snippet for {entry.label}:",
744	                multiline=True,
745	                instruction=_SNIPPET_INSTRUCTION,
746	                key_bindings=_SNIPPET_SUBMIT_BINDINGS,
747	                style=_SNIPPET_STYLE,
748	            )
749	            body = await asyncio.to_thread(body_prompt.ask)
750	            if body and body.strip():
751	                snippets[entry.item_id] = body
752	                break
753	
754	            # Empty, whitespace-only, or an abandoned editor (`None`): not a resolution and
755	            # not an unresolved fall-through — re-prompt the three-way choice (decision 10).
756	            console.print(
757	                Text("An install snippet cannot be empty — enter a real snippet or choose a skip.", style="yellow")
758	            )

166	class DecisionFile:
167	    """Read/write access to ONE manager's machine-local decision file, through
168	    whichever `Executor` is local to the machine that should hold it (D-08a).
169	
170	    Construct with `executor=self.source` to read/write the SOURCE machine's file,
171	    or `executor=self.target` to read/write the TARGET machine's file — the caller
172	    (`PackageSyncJob`, plan 02-04 task 2) decides which per D-08a, this class only
173	    ever talks to the executor it was given.
174	    """
175	
176	    def __init__(self, manager: str, executor: Executor) -> None:
177	        self._manager = manager
178	        self._executor = executor
179	        # shlex.quote() is a no-op for this fixed, already-shell-safe relpath (only
180	        # word chars, '.', '/'), but is applied anyway per T-02-01 (ASVS V5) rather
181	        # than assuming a future manager name stays that safe. Left OUTSIDE the `~/`
182	        # prefix: quoting the whole `~/...` expression would disable tilde expansion,
183	        # while `~/` immediately followed by a (possibly-)quoted word is still one
184	        # shell word — bash expands the leading `~/` and appends the rest literally.
185	        relpath = DECISION_FILE_RELPATH_TEMPLATE.format(manager=manager)
186	        self._path_expr = f"~/{shlex.quote(relpath)}"
187	        self._display_path = f"~/{relpath}"

189	    async def load(self) -> dict[str, DecisionEntry]:
190	        """Read this manager's decisions, or an empty mapping (D-08's degrade rule).
191	
192	        Absent, empty and malformed all degrade to "no permanent decisions" rather
193	        than aborting the sync; only the malformed case logs a WARNING (naming the
194	        path) since that one indicates the file was tampered with or hand-edited
195	        incorrectly, not simply "nothing recorded yet".
196	        """
197	        result = await self._executor.run_command(f"cat {self._path_expr} 2>/dev/null")
198	        if not result.success or not result.stdout.strip():
199	            return {}
200	
201	        try:
202	            return _deserialize(result.stdout)
203	        except (yaml.YAMLError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
204	            _logger.warning(
205	                "Malformed decision file %s (%s); treating as no permanent decisions",
206	                self._display_path,
207	                exc,
208	            )

211	    async def record(self, entry: DecisionEntry) -> None:
212	        """Merge `entry` into this file by `item_id` (last write wins) and write
213	        atomically: `mkdir --parents` the directory, write the new content to a sibling
214	        `.pcswitcher-tmp` path, then `mv --force` it into place — the same
215	        atomic-replace-within-the-same-directory shape `vscode_state_sync._sync_editor`
216	        uses, so an interrupted write can never leave a truncated file.
217	
218	        The serialised bytes travel as one shlex-quoted `printf` argument through
219	        `self._executor` — never a local filesystem write — so this identical method
220	        is correct whether `self._executor` is the source's `LocalExecutor` or the
221	        target's `RemoteExecutor`.
222	        """
223	        entries = await self.load()
224	        entries[entry.item_id] = entry
225	        content = _serialize(entries)
226	
227	        dir_relpath = shlex.quote(_DECISION_DIR_RELPATH)
228	        tmp_expr = f"{self._path_expr}.pcswitcher-tmp"
229	        cmd = (
230	            f"mkdir --parents ~/{dir_relpath} && "
231	            f"printf '%s' {shlex.quote(content)} > {tmp_expr} && "
232	            f"mv --force {tmp_expr} {self._path_expr}"
233	        )
234	        result = await self._executor.run_command(
235	            cmd, mutates=f"record permanent skip for {entry.label} in {self._display_path}"
236	        )

239	                f"failed to record decision for {entry.item_id!r} in {self._display_path}: {result.stderr.strip()}"

409	    async def replay(self, item_id: str, executor: RemoteExecutor) -> CommandResult:
410	        """Replay the snippet registered for `item_id` against `executor` (always the

412	        templated or inspected, only quoted.
413	
414	        Runs as `bash -c <shlex.quote(body)>` — the same build-a-command,

417	        not something that needs the user's `~/.profile` sourced. No stdin is ever

419	        snippet expecting a prompt fails rather than hanging the sync. The returned
420	        `CommandResult`'s exit code alone decides success — never raises for "no

430	        if snippet is None:
431	            return CommandResult(exit_code=1, stdout="", stderr=f"no snippet registered for {item_id!r}")

433	        cmd = f"bash -c {shlex.quote(snippet.body)}"
434	        return await executor.run_command(
435	            cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"replay install snippet for {snippet.label}"

2	D-29, ADR-020).
3	
4	Scope (user vs. system) is part of a flatpak item's identity, not just a field on it:
5	this project's own reference machine has several runtimes installed in BOTH scopes
6	under the same application id, and `FlatpakItem.item_id`/`FlatpakRemoteItem.item_id`
7	already fold scope into the identity string (`FlatpakItem` below). That is what makes
8	"same application, different scope" fall out of the generic source-vs-target diff as
9	two independent items with no special-casing in this module — a ref present as
10	`user` on the source and `system` on the target produces one install diff and one
11	removal diff, never a single in-place change, because they are simply two different
12	`item_id`s. Normalising that scope split across a machine's own two installations is
13	explicitly out of scope (deferred, CONTEXT.md): it is a change to the machines, not a
14	sync feature, and this job reports the split exactly as found.
15	
16	BRANCH is identity for the same reason (`FlatpakItem`): a ref is identified by its full
17	`<application>/<arch>/<branch>` ref, which is also the only string `flatpak install` and
18	`flatpak uninstall` can resolve on a remote or a machine holding two branches of one
19	application id. Origin is deliberately NOT identity — see `FlatpakItem` for why the two
20	go opposite ways.
21	
22	A remote is DERIVED from the refs approved from it, never ticked (ADR-020 D-41, which is
23	D-37's rule for apt repositories in a second ecosystem). `flatpak install` refuses outright when
24	the remote it names is not configured in the scope being installed into (D-14), so
25	"ref ticked, its remote unticked" was an unrepresentable pairing offered as two independent
26	review lines — and worse, "ref ticked, its remote's URL change declined" silently installed
27	another vendor's build. `accept_review()` therefore turns the approved ref installs into
28	the set of remotes this run must provision (`_derive_remotes`), and `apply()` writes them
29	before the base converge loop reaches the first ref. A remote the source has that feeds no
30	ref approved this run does not travel; there is no flatpak counterpart to apt's
31	never-removed distribution sources, because a fresh flatpak install configures ZERO remotes
32	and a machine with none is a perfectly ordinary machine (measured), so even Flathub travels
33	only as a consequence of something needing it. A derived write has no item of its own, so a
34	failure is recorded against the remote and charged to every approved ref that depended on
35	it (D-39). Only the REMOVAL direction stays a review line, and it takes two answers rather
36	than three (`REPO_REMOVAL_REVIEW_ACTION`): a permanent machine-local mark on a remote whose
37	whole purpose is to feed refs would silently and permanently change where those refs come
38	from, and the remedy is consolidating the two configurations, not recording a preference.
39	
40	Repointing a remote is silent too, with ADR-020 D-41's single exception, which this job
41	applies to remotes exactly as `apt_sync` applies D-37's to repository files: a remote whose URL
42	or verification setting differs is overwritten without a word UNLESS a ref the TARGET
43	recorded skip-always takes it as its origin, in which case both configurations are shown and
44	the answer is overwrite or skip-once (`_capture_remote_conflicts`,
45	`REPO_CONFLICT_REVIEW_ACTION`). Machine-specific is the trigger, not target-only: a
46	skip-always ref is structurally invisible — `filter_inert` keeps it out of the manifest, so
47	it produces no diff in any run — and repointing the remote it updates from moves software
48	the user explicitly told this tool to leave alone. Two answers, nothing recorded. A skipped
49	conflict keeps the remote out of the write set but NOT out of the D-39 attribution map, so
50	every approved ref that needed the source's URL fails naming the decision rather than
51	installing from the URL the target still has.
52	
53	Before converging a ref, its origin remote is re-read off the TARGET and required to carry
54	the source
55	remote's URL and verification setting — not merely to exist under the same name
56	(`_origin_refusal`), because a same-named remote pointing elsewhere serves a different
57	vendor's build of the same ref at exit 0 with no warning; and after the install the ref's
58	own reported origin is read back and resolved to a URL again (`_installed_origin_refusal`),
59	so the guarantee is checked rather than inferred. Either refusal is a per-item failure
60	naming both URLs, never an install issued in hope (T-02-24). That same read is what checks
61	the derived writes actually landed: `flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists <name> <other url>`
62	exits 0 and changes nothing (measured), so the write's exit code proves nothing and only
63	the target's own answer does.
64	
65	The removal direction is disclosure rather than refusal (#214): a remote offered for
66	deletion carries, in its review `detail`, the target refs that still name it as their
67	origin in that same scope — deleting a remote whose refs are being removed too is
68	legitimate cleanup, so the decision stays in the review where D-30 puts apt's collateral:
69	the dependent refs are known from the plan's own reads, so the consequence can be stated
70	while the user is deciding about the deletion that causes it.
71	
72	A remote carries its TRUST as part of the item, not as a property of the machine that
73	happens to hold it (#215): `FlatpakRemoteItem` records the remote's GPG-verification
74	setting and the digest of its own ostree keyring, and convergence replicates both —
75	`flatpak remote-add --gpg-import=<staged key>` for a signed remote, `--no-gpg-verify`
76	only when the SOURCE remote is itself unverified. Without this a replicated remote is
77	configured but unusable: flatpak refuses every install from it with `Can't check
78	signature: public key not found`. The key bytes travel byte-for-byte from the source
79	machine and are never re-fetched from a vendor (ADR-020 D-12's rule for apt signing
80	keys), staged under the target's `~/.cache/pc-switcher/` exactly as `apt_sync` stages
81	`/etc/apt` content, because SFTP reaches only the SSH user's own home.
82	
83	The flatpak OSTree store stays authoritative for its own state (D-01): this job never
84	WRITES into `/var/lib/flatpak` or `~/.local/share/flatpak`, only shells out to `flatpak`
85	itself. It does READ one file there, `<installation>/repo/<remote>.trustedkeys.gpg`,
86	because no flatpak command prints or exports a remote's key and libostree's own CLI is
87	not installed alongside flatpak on Ubuntu. `flatpak_sync_exclude_paths()` exports
88	`~/.local/share/flatpak` so `folder_sync` stops mirroring the store this job owns
89	(D-29, ADR-018) — but NOT `~/.var/app`, which is per-application USER DATA that stays
90	folder_sync's territory;
91	D-17's job-before-folder_sync ordering exists precisely so `flatpak install` creates
92	the store first and folder_sync's data lands on top of it, never the reverse.
93	
94	`FlatpakSyncJob` subclasses `PackageSyncJob` and implements the abstract `plan()`, for the
95	same reason `SnapSyncJob` does: what a diff even IS differs per manager, so the base class
96	holds no diff to inherit. apt's own diff is apt-package-shaped — one item class,
97	`MISSING_ON_TARGET`/`EXTRA_ON_TARGET`/`VERSION_MISMATCH` only, no notion of derived work
98	that must land ahead of an item. `plan()` here reuses every manager-agnostic building
99	block the shared core provides — `DecisionFile`/`filter_inert` (D-08's machine-local
100	skip-always filtering) and `PackageSyncJob._build_review_groups` (D-24's action-grouped
101	review) — so only capture, diff and converge are genuinely flatpak-specific.
102	`accept_review()` is overridden to turn the approved refs into the derived remote set,
103	and `apply()` to write those remotes before the base converge loop reaches its first ref.
104	`execute()` is inherited unchanged and is where this job's own single review happens,
105	before its own first mutating command: there is no coordinator and no review spanning two
106	managers (D-15, D-24).
107	
108	Flatpak ref VERSIONS are captured for reporting only (D-04, like apt package
109	versions): a version difference on a ref present in the same scope on both machines
110	is a `REPORT_ONLY` diff, never something this job installs or removes to force.
111	
112	A ref's ORIGIN is reported the same way and outranks it (`_diff_flatpak_refs`, D-41). The
113	two install-time refusals above guard an install, and a ref already present on BOTH machines
114	issues none — so the already-diverged case they cannot see is `ORIGIN_MISMATCH`: same scope,
115	same `<application>/<arch>/<branch>`, two vendors. It is compared by the remotes' URLs rather
116	than their names for the reason `5fc3ac01` records, so a target `flathub` pointing at the beta
117	repo is caught and a remote the two machines merely named differently is not. It is
118	`REPORT_ONLY` because flatpak leaves no verb: `flatpak install <other remote> <installed ref>`
119	refuses with `already installed from remote <name>` (measured), so converging it would mean
120	uninstalling the app the user has and reinstalling it from the other vendor.
121	"""

287	class FlatpakItem:
288	    """One installed flatpak application ref (D-06), scoped user or system.
289	
290	    `scope` lives inside the identity string, not just as a field: this project's own
291	    machine has several runtimes installed in both scopes with the same application
292	    id, and folding scope into `item_id` is what makes "same name, different scope"
293	    fall out of the generic diff engine as two distinct items with no special-casing
294	    in `flatpak_sync`.
295	
296	    So does `ref` (`<application>/<arch>/<branch>`), and NOT the bare application id, for
297	    two reasons that the application id alone cannot serve:
298	
299	    - Two branches of one application id can be installed side by side in ONE scope —
300	      that is what branches are for — so `(scope, application)` is not a unique key for a
301	      machine's own listing, and keying on it silently drops one of the two rows when the
302	      captured items are folded into a `{item_id: item}` map.
303	    - The install and the removal both need the full ref anyway (`_FLATPAK_LIST_CMD`), so
304	      the identity and the command argument are the same string rather than two facts that
305	      can drift.
306	
307	    ORIGIN deliberately stays out (a field, not identity), because the install-plus-removal
308	    pair it would produce cannot converge: `flatpak install <other remote> <ref>` on an
309	    already-installed ref exits with `<ref> is already installed from remote <name>`, so
310	    the install half could never run while the removal half proposed deleting the app the
311	    user has. A BRANCH difference has the opposite property — branches coexist, so the
312	    install half succeeds and the removal half then leaves exactly the source's set — which
313	    is why a branch change replicates as two items and an origin change does not.
314	    """

316	    application: str
317	    version: str
318	    origin: str
319	    scope: Literal["user", "system"]
320	    ref: str

324	    @property
325	    def item_id(self) -> str:
326	        """Stable identity string: `flatpak:ref:<scope>:<application>/<arch>/<branch>`."""
327	        return f"flatpak:ref:{self.scope}:{self.ref}"
328	
329	    def label(self) -> str:
330	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
331	        return f"{self.ref} ({self.version}, {self.origin}, {self.scope})"

481	    """The scope's ostree repo directory, as a SHELL EXPRESSION for `run_command`.
482	
483	    `$HOME` is left for the remote shell to expand rather than resolved here: the user

490	    the same user's remotes live and manufacture a phantom key diff.
491	    """

515	def _parse_keyring_digests(output: str) -> dict[str, str]:
516	    """`{remote name: sha256}` from one scope's batched `sha256sum` output.
517	
518	    `<digest>  <path>` lines, mapped by stripping the `.trustedkeys.gpg` suffix off the
519	    basename — a remote name may contain dots (`my.remote.name.trustedkeys.gpg`,
520	    verified live), so only the fixed suffix is removed, never everything after the
521	    first dot.
522	    """
523	    digests: dict[str, str] = {}
524	    for line in _lines(output):
525	        parts = line.split(maxsplit=1)
526	        if len(parts) != 2:
527	            continue
528	        digest, path = parts
529	        name = Path(path.strip()).name
530	        if not name.endswith(_TRUSTEDKEYS_SUFFIX):
531	            continue
532	        digests[name[: -len(_TRUSTEDKEYS_SUFFIX)]] = digest
533	    return digests

536	def _split_flatpak_item_id(item_id: str, expected_kind: Literal["ref", "remote", "mask"]) -> tuple[str, str]:
537	    """`(scope, name)` from a `flatpak:<kind>:<scope>:<name>` item id (`FlatpakItem` above).
538	
539	    `name` is the full `<application>/<arch>/<branch>` ref for a ref, the remote name for
540	    a remote, the pattern for a mask — none carries a `:` of its own: application ids and
541	    remote names are dotted/alnum tokens, and refs and mask patterns are partial refs with
542	    `/` and `*` but never `:` (RESEARCH Standard Stack, verified live), so a fixed 3-colon
543	    split is exact rather than a heuristic (the `split(":", 3)` cap keeps every `/` intact).
544	    This is a legitimate use of a
545	    stable identity string (the same pattern `apt_sync._package_name` and
546	    `snap_sync._snap_name` already establish): the plan only ever carries `ItemDiff`s,
547	    not the richer item dataclasses, so converge() recovers scope/name from the id.
548	    """
549	    parts = item_id.split(":", 3)
550	    if len(parts) != 4 or parts[0] != "flatpak" or parts[1] != expected_kind:
551	        raise ValueError(f"not a flatpak {expected_kind} item id: {item_id!r}")
552	    _, _, scope, name = parts
553	    return scope, name

556	def _parse_flatpak_list(output: str) -> list[FlatpakItem]:
557	    """Parse `_FLATPAK_LIST_CMD`'s tab-separated output into `FlatpakItem`s.
558	
559	    A line whose `installation` field is neither `user` nor `system` (flatpak permits
560	    additional named installations beyond the two this item model represents) is
561	    skipped rather than guessed at — this project's own machines only ever use the
562	    two standard scopes (CONTEXT.md's live inventory), and a third would need its own
563	    modelling decision, not a silent default.
564	    """
565	    items: list[FlatpakItem] = []
566	    for line in _lines(output):
567	        fields = line.split("\t")
568	        if len(fields) != 5:
569	            continue
570	        application, version, origin, installation, ref = fields
571	        scope: Literal["user", "system"]
572	        if installation == "user":
573	            scope = "user"
574	        elif installation == "system":
575	            scope = "system"
576	        else:
577	            continue
578	        items.append(FlatpakItem(application=application, version=version, origin=origin, scope=scope, ref=ref))
579	    return items

582	def _parse_flatpak_remotes(
583	    output: str, scope: Literal["user", "system"], key_digests: Mapping[str, str]
584	) -> list[FlatpakRemoteItem]:
585	    """Parse one scope's `flatpak remotes --columns=name,url,options` output.
586	
587	    `scope` is a parameter, not a parsed column: unlike `flatpak list`, this command
588	    has no scope column of its own — the caller already knows which scope it asked
589	    about, because it chose the `--user`/`--system` flag (module docstring).
590	    `key_digests` is the same scope's `_parse_keyring_digests` map, joined here by
591	    remote name so a remote's trust arrives as part of the item rather than as a
592	    second lookup at converge time (#215).
593	
594	    `options` is a comma-separated token list carrying two facts this job reads: whether
595	    verification is off (`no-gpg-verify`) and whether the remote carries a ref filter
596	    (`filtered`, `_FILTERED_OPTION`). They are independent tokens, so a filtered remote's
597	    verification state parses exactly as an unfiltered one's.
598	
599	    A remote with no options at all prints only two fields (no trailing tab), so both
600	    widths are accepted; a remote absent from `key_digests` keeps `key_digest=None`,
601	    which is the honest reading of "verification is on but this remote carries no key of
602	    its own" — trust then comes from a machine-level anchor this job neither reads nor
603	    replicates.
604	    """
605	    items: list[FlatpakRemoteItem] = []
606	    for line in _lines(output):
607	        fields = line.split("\t")
608	        if len(fields) not in (2, 3):
609	            continue
610	        name, url = fields[0], fields[1]
611	        options = fields[2].split(",") if len(fields) == 3 else []
612	        gpg_verify = _NO_GPG_VERIFY_OPTION not in options
613	        items.append(
614	            FlatpakRemoteItem(
615	                name=name,
616	                url=url,
617	                scope=scope,
618	                gpg_verify=gpg_verify,
619	                key_digest=key_digests.get(name) if gpg_verify else None,
620	                is_filtered=_FILTERED_OPTION in options,
621	            )
622	        )
623	    return items

626	def _parse_flatpak_masks(output: str, scope: Literal["user", "system"]) -> list[FlatpakMaskItem]:
627	    """Parse one scope's `flatpak {--user|--system} mask` output into `FlatpakMaskItem`s.
628	
629	    Unlike the tab-separated list commands, `flatpak mask` prints each pattern on its
630	    own line prefixed with two leading spaces and no header (RESEARCH: verified live,
631	    Flatpak 1.14.6), so this strips leading/trailing whitespace per non-blank line
632	    rather than splitting on tabs. `scope` is a parameter, not a parsed column: the
633	    command has no scope column: the caller already chose the `--user`/`--system` flag
634	    (same reasoning as `_parse_flatpak_remotes`).
635	    """
636	    items: list[FlatpakMaskItem] = []
637	    for line in output.splitlines():
638	        pattern = line.strip()
639	        if not pattern:
640	            continue
641	        items.append(FlatpakMaskItem(pattern=pattern, scope=scope))
642	    return items

723	def _same_vendor(
724	    source_item: FlatpakItem,
725	    target_item: FlatpakItem,
726	    source_remote_urls: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
727	    target_remote_urls: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
728	) -> bool:
729	    """Whether the two machines' copies of one ref provably come from the same vendor.
730	
731	    ADR-020 D-41: origin is compared by the remote's URL, never by its name. Both directions
732	    of that rule matter here and pull opposite ways, which is why neither comparison alone is
733	    the answer:
734	
735	    - Same NAME, different URL is the dangerous case — a target remote called `flathub`
736	      pointing at the beta repo serves a different vendor's build and `flatpak list
737	      --columns=origin` prints `flathub` on both machines (measured, `5fc3ac01`). Comparing
738	      names would report nothing at all.
739	    - Different NAME, same URL is a pure rename. The provenance is identical, so reporting it
740	      would be noise about a label.
741	
742	    When either side's origin resolves to no configured remote — the machine holds a ref whose
743	    remote has since been deleted — there is no URL to compare and the fallback is the name.
744	    That is the conservative reading: it keeps an ordinary machine quiet on the equal-name case
745	    rather than manufacturing a mismatch out of a lookup miss, and still reports two different
746	    names, which is all the evidence there is.
747	    """
748	    source_url = source_remote_urls.get((source_item.scope, source_item.origin))
749	    target_url = target_remote_urls.get((target_item.scope, target_item.origin))
750	    if source_url is not None and target_url is not None:
751	        return source_url == target_url
752	    return source_item.origin == target_item.origin

755	def _diff_flatpak_refs(
756	    source_items: Sequence[FlatpakItem],
757	    target_items: Sequence[FlatpakItem],
758	    source_remote_urls: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
759	    target_remote_urls: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
760	    machines: Machines,
761	) -> list[ItemDiff]:
762	    """One diff per ref `item_id` present on either side, source-then-target order —
763	    same shape as `PackageSyncJob._diff_apt_packages`/`snap_sync._diff_snap_items`.
764	    Scope already lives inside `item_id`, so an application installed in a different
765	    scope on each machine naturally produces one install-side entry and one
766	    remove-side entry here, never a single combined diff.
767	
768	    Present on both, the origin comparison runs BEFORE the version comparison, exactly as
769	    `_diff_apt_packages` orders its own two provenance-and-version branches: two vendors'
770	    builds of one ref share no version scale — Flathub's and Flathub-beta's `org.mozilla.
771	    firefox` are numbered independently — so reporting "source has X, target has Y" would
772	    state a difference of degree where the real difference is of provenance, and would hide
773	    the wrong-vendor finding behind a version line the user reads as ordinary drift.
774	    """
775	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
776	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
777	
778	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
779	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
780	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
781	
782	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
783	    for item_id in seen:
784	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
785	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
786	
787	        if source_item is not None and target_item is None:
788	            diffs.append(_install_ref_diff(source_item))
789	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
790	            diffs.append(_remove_ref_diff(target_item))
791	        elif source_item is not None and target_item is not None:
792	            if not _same_vendor(source_item, target_item, source_remote_urls, target_remote_urls):
793	                diffs.append(
794	                    _origin_mismatch_ref_diff(
795	                        item_id,
796	                        source_item,
797	                        target_item,
798	                        source_remote_urls.get((source_item.scope, source_item.origin)),
799	                        target_remote_urls.get((target_item.scope, target_item.origin)),
800	                        machines,
801	                    )
802	                )
803	            elif source_item.version != target_item.version:
804	                diffs.append(_version_mismatch_ref_diff(item_id, source_item, target_item, machines))
805	            # else: present on both, one vendor, equal version -> no diff.
806	
807	    return diffs

852	def _derive_remotes(
853	    approved_ref_ids: frozenset[str],
854	    source_refs_by_id: Mapping[str, FlatpakItem],
855	    source_ref_origins: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
856	    source_runtime_by_ref_id: Mapping[str, str],
857	) -> tuple[tuple[_DerivedRemote, ...], dict[str, frozenset[str]]]:
858	    """`(remotes to provision, {approved ref item_id: the remote_ids it depends on})`.
859	
860	    Two sources feed the set, both computed from facts `plan()` already read off the source
861	    and neither costing a command here:
862	
863	    - the approved ref's own origin, and
864	    - the origin of the runtime that ref is built against, because `flatpak install` pulls
865	      the runtime too and resolves it from whatever remotes are configured — an app on
866	      remote X built against a runtime the source holds from remote Y would otherwise be
867	      approved with only X provisioned.
868	
869	    The runtime is looked up in EITHER scope on the source (a user app against a
870	    system-installed runtime is the ordinary case) but its remote is always derived in the
871	    APP's scope, because that is the installation the target may have to pull the runtime
872	    into. Deriving one remote too many in the rare cross-scope case costs a
873	    `flatpak remote-add`; deriving one too few costs the install.
874	
875	    The attribution map is D-39's: a derived write has no item to fail, so it fails every
876	    approved ref that named it.
877	    """
878	    derived: dict[str, _DerivedRemote] = {}
879	    depends_on: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
880	
881	    def need(item_id: str, scope: Literal["user", "system"], name: str, reason: str) -> None:
882	        remote_id = f"flatpak:remote:{scope}:{name}"
883	        derived.setdefault(
884	            remote_id,
885	            _DerivedRemote(
886	                remote_id=remote_id,
887	                scope=scope,
888	                name=name,
889	                reason="ref_origin" if reason == "ref_origin" else "runtime_origin",
890	            ),
891	        )
892	        depends_on.setdefault(item_id, set()).add(remote_id)
893	
894	    for item_id in sorted(approved_ref_ids):
895	        item = source_refs_by_id.get(item_id)
896	        if item is None:
897	            continue
898	        need(item_id, item.scope, item.origin, "ref_origin")
899	        runtime = source_runtime_by_ref_id.get(item_id)
900	        if runtime is None:
901	            continue
902	        other_scope = "system" if item.scope == "user" else "user"
903	        runtime_origin = source_ref_origins.get((item.scope, runtime)) or source_ref_origins.get(
904	            (other_scope, runtime)
905	        )
906	        if runtime_origin is not None:
907	            need(item_id, item.scope, runtime_origin, "runtime_origin")
908	
909	    return (
910	        tuple(derived[remote_id] for remote_id in sorted(derived)),
911	        {item_id: frozenset(remote_ids) for item_id, remote_ids in depends_on.items()},
912	    )

936	def _remote_facets(source_item: FlatpakRemoteItem, target_item: FlatpakRemoteItem) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...]:
937	    """`(facet, the source's value, the target's value)` for every facet in which the two
938	    sides' same-identity remotes differ.
939	
940	    One definition serving both readers of that question — the log line a silent repoint
941	    leaves (`_remote_change_detail`) and the two configurations a conflict screen shows
942	    (`_remote_conflict_versions`) — so the two can never disagree about what "differs" means.
943	    Only differing facets are returned, so a plain URL edit still reads exactly as it did
944	    before trust joined the item (#215) and a trust-only divergence never mentions a URL both
945	    machines agree on.
946	    """
947	    facets: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
948	    if source_item.url != target_item.url:
949	        facets.append((_URL_FACET, source_item.url, target_item.url))
950	    if source_item.gpg_verify != target_item.gpg_verify:
