1107	def _diff_flatpak_masks(
1108	    source_items: Sequence[FlatpakMaskItem], target_items: Sequence[FlatpakMaskItem]
1109	) -> list[ItemDiff]:
1110	    """One diff per mask `item_id` (scope + pattern) present on either side (#208, D-10).
1111	
1112	    Pure membership, no `CHANGE`: a mask has no value to change, only presence — so
1113	    source-has & target-lacks -> `INSTALL` (add the mask on target); target-has &
1114	    source-lacks -> `REMOVE` (unmask on target); present on both -> no diff. A pattern
1115	    edit therefore reads as remove-old + add-new and a user/system scope split as
1116	    add + remove (scope is identity, same as refs/remotes), reported as found rather
1117	    than normalised.
1118	    """
1119	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
1120	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
1121	
1122	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
1123	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
1124	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
1125	
1126	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
1127	    for item_id in seen:
1128	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
1129	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
1130	
1131	        if source_item is not None and target_item is None:
1132	            diffs.append(_install_mask_diff(source_item))
1133	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
1134	            diffs.append(_remove_mask_diff(target_item))
1135	        # else: present on both -> no diff (pure membership, no value to change).
1136	
1137	    return diffs

1342	        `uninstall`/`remote-add`/`remote-delete`/`mask` mutation before this returns.
1343	        Caches the source/target refs and remotes by id for `converge()` (see `__init__`);
1344	        masks need no cache (pattern is fully in the item_id).
1345	
1346	        The two derivation inputs are read here for the same reason apt reads its origin
1347	        state before the package diff: derivation runs in the synchronous
1348	        `accept_review()`, which cannot issue a command, so every fact it consumes has to
1349	        be in hand by then. That costs one extra source listing plus one
1350	        `flatpak info --show-runtime` per source app (10 ms each, no network — measured).
1351	
1352	        Diffs are ordered refs -> masks in the returned `diffs` tuple: a mask applied before
1353	        its refs could suppress an auto-pulled dependency of a ref being installed the same
1354	        run (D-08). Remotes are no longer in this ordering at all in the add direction —
1355	        they are derived and written by `apply()` ahead of the whole loop — and a remote
1356	        REMOVAL is order-independent, since the refs it could orphan are named in its own
1357	        review detail rather than converged around it.
1358	
1359	        Ruling 6's conflicts are computed here too and cost no command at all: every fact
1360	        they need — both machines' remote records, the target's own ref listing and its
1361	        decision file — was already read for the diff.
1362	        """
1363	        source_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.source).load()
1364	        target_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.target).load()
1365	
1366	        source_refs = await filter_inert(await self.capture_source_items(), source_decisions)
1367	        installed_target_refs = await self.query_target_items()
1368	        target_refs = await filter_inert(installed_target_refs, target_decisions)
1369	        source_remotes = await self._capture_all_source_remotes()
1370	        installed_target_remotes = await self._query_all_target_remotes()

1419	    def _capture_remote_conflicts(
1420	        self,
1421	        diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff],
1422	        installed_target_refs: Sequence[FlatpakItem],
1423	        target_decisions: Mapping[str, DecisionEntry],
1424	    ) -> None:

1426	        write: a remote this run may repoint, whose URL or verification setting differs, and
1427	        which a MACHINE-SPECIFIC target ref takes as its origin in that same scope.
1428	
1429	        Machine-specific means recorded skip-always in the TARGET's decision file, exactly as
1430	        `AptSyncJob._machine_specific_packages_by_source_file` reads it — not "a ref the
1431	        target has and the source does not". The narrower set is the point: a skip-always ref
1432	        is structurally invisible (`filter_inert` drops it before the diff, so it can never
1433	        produce an `ItemDiff` of its own in any run) and the user's explicit "this machine
1434	        keeps this, syncs never touch it" is exactly the promise a silent repoint breaks. An
1435	        ordinary target ref is at least eligible for its own diff, and keying off every ref
1436	        from the remote would make the question a property of the machine — one Flathub
1437	        repoint would name every app on it and inform nobody.

1440	        every proposed install — a superset of what `accept_review()` actually derives, since
1441	        the review has not happened yet. Gating on it is what keeps this job's rule intact:
1442	        a remote travels because a ref needs it, so a remote nothing will touch this run is
1443	        not a question, and answering "overwrite" cannot by itself make one travel. That is
1444	        the one place this deliberately diverges from apt, whose conflict screen covers every
1445	        differing file and whose approval does force the write.

1448	        is being replaced, so there is nothing to ask about.
1449	        """

1456	        candidates, _attribution = _derive_remotes(
1457	            frozenset(

1461	            ),
1462	            self._source_refs_by_id,

1489	        `REPO_REMOVAL_REVIEW_ACTION`), mirroring `AptSyncJob`'s, and append D-41's conflict
1490	        screen when `_capture_remote_conflicts` found one.

1493	        difference is that "always skip" is absent from it, because a permanent machine-local
1494	        mark on a remote whose purpose is to feed refs would silently and permanently change
1495	        where those refs come from. The conflict screen is the same two-answer screen
1496	        (`REPO_CONFLICT_REVIEW_ACTION`), preceded by both versions of every remote it lists,
1497	        and records nothing either way. Both trail the base groups so the user sees the diff
1498	        first, conflicts before removals: one decides what the target's remotes become, the
1499	        other what it loses.

1504	        removal_ids = {diff.item_id for diff in removals}

1507	            groups.append(
1508	                ReviewGroup(
1509	                    manager=self.manager_id,
1510	                    action=REPO_CONFLICT_REVIEW_ACTION,
1511	                    title=f"Resolve {self.manager_id} remote conflicts",
1512	                    entries=tuple(
1513	                        ReviewEntry(

1515	                            label=f"{conflict.name} remote ({conflict.scope})",
1516	                            action_label="overwrite",
1517	                            detail=build_remote_conflict_detail(

1519	                            ),
1520	                            versions=(conflict.target_version, conflict.source_version),
1521	                        )

1529	            ReviewGroup(
1530	                manager=self.manager_id,

1768	            # the configuration could be restored piecemeal afterwards.
1769	            cmd = f"{sudo}flatpak remote-delete {scope_flag} {shlex.quote(name)}"

1775	            f"FlatpakSyncJob.converge: unsupported action {diff.action.value!r} for a flatpak remote ({diff.label})"

12	target on the source's exact revision without touching the standing auto-refresh
13	policy at all — the mechanism D-06 requires: both machines converge on the same
14	revision, neither stops updating.
15	
16	The snapd store stays authoritative for its own state (D-01): this job never touches

18	`apt_sync` uses for `apt`/`dpkg`.
19	
20	Snap has no repository or key decision to replicate, and gets no screen for one (D-42).
21	One store serves the device, and name -> publisher is pinned store-side by a
22	canonical-signed `snap-declaration` snapd validates itself, so one name resolves to one
23	snap-id resolves to one publisher and there is no second `firefox` for the target to
24	install by accident. Keys are snapd's own, not the user's. A brand store or a store
25	proxy could in principle make two machines draw from different stores, but both are
26	device-provisioning facts rather than per-snap facts and neither is replicable, so snap
27	is treated as having one store and no store-identity check exists. The provenance
28	variable that remains is which revision of that one snap is installed and which channel
29	it tracks, and D-06 converges both.

133	    `snap_sync` can pass `--classic`/`--devmode` to `snap install`/`snap refresh`, which
134	    snapd requires as explicit per-revision confirmation before it will install a
135	    classic-confinement or devmode revision at all.
136	    """
137	
138	    name: str
139	    channel: str
140	    revision: str
141	    held: bool = False
142	    classic: bool = False
143	    devmode: bool = False

150	        return f"snap:{self.name}"

163	def _parse_snap_list(output: str) -> list[SnapItem]:
164	    """Parse `snap list --all` by HEADER column names, never fixed offsets or assumed
165	    order (RESEARCH Open Question 2): a future snapd column reorder must yield correct
166	    values, never a silently wrong revision driving a wrong `--revision` install.
167	
168	    Skips a disabled older-revision line (`Notes` names `disabled`) for a snap that
169	    also has an active line — only the active revision becomes the item. Output shaped
170	    like "No snaps are installed yet." (no recognizable header) degrades to an empty
171	    list rather than raising: a snap-free machine is a valid, if rare, state.
172	    """
173	    lines = [line for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]
174	    if not lines:
175	        return []
176	
177	    header = lines[0].split()
178	    try:
179	        name_idx = header.index("Name")
180	        rev_idx = header.index("Rev")
181	        tracking_idx = header.index("Tracking")
182	        notes_idx = header.index("Notes")
183	    except ValueError:
184	        return []
185	
186	    max_idx = max(name_idx, rev_idx, tracking_idx, notes_idx)
187	    items: list[SnapItem] = []
188	    for line in lines[1:]:
189	        fields = line.split()
190	        if len(fields) <= max_idx:
191	            continue
192	        notes = fields[notes_idx].split(",")
193	        if "disabled" in notes:
194	            continue
195	        # `held` in the Notes column is a PER-SNAP refresh hold (#208, D9) — snapstate
196	        # attached to this one snap. It is SEPARATE state from the system-wide
197	        # `refresh.hold` the orchestrator sets across the sync window via `snap set
198	        # system refresh.hold` (different snapd namespaces), so capturing here, inside
199	        # the sync window, does not mask a per-snap hold: the system hold never writes
200	        # `held` into an individual snap's Notes. If a VM integration test ever shows a
201	        # system hold flipping this token, capture would have to move BEFORE the
202	        # sync-window hold is applied. Fail-safe even then: a system hold flips both
203	        # hosts symmetrically -> both-held -> no spurious diff.
204	        held = "held" in notes
205	        # Confinement, from the same Notes list: snapd refuses to install a classic or a
206	        # devmode revision without the matching flag as explicit confirmation, so the
207	        # capture has to carry it or `_converge_install` cannot build a working command.
208	        items.append(
209	            SnapItem(
210	                name=fields[name_idx],
211	                channel=fields[tracking_idx],
212	                revision=fields[rev_idx],
213	                held=held,
214	                classic="classic" in notes,
215	                devmode="devmode" in notes,
216	            )
217	        )
218	    return items

221	def _confinement_flags(item: SnapItem) -> str:
222	    """The `--classic`/`--devmode` confirmation flag `snap install`/`snap refresh` need
223	    for this item's confinement, as a leading-space command fragment ("" for a strictly
224	    confined snap).
225	
226	    At most ONE flag is ever emitted, classic winning. The two mean different, mutually
227	    incompatible things — `--classic` confirms a revision the store published with classic
228	    confinement, `--devmode` (per `snap install --help`) "relax[es] confinement for strict
229	    snaps" — so a snap is one or the other, never both. The `snap` CLI only rejects one
230	    mode-flag pair outright (`cannot use devmode and jailmode flags together`, verified in
231	    the 2.76.1 binary); a nonsensical `--classic --devmode` pair would be accepted
232	    silently, which is exactly why this never emits it.
233	
234	    Passing `--classic` where it is not needed is safe: `snap` warns `flag --classic
235	    ignored for strictly confined snap %s` rather than failing.
236	    """
237	    if item.classic:
238	        return " --classic"
239	    if item.devmode:
240	        return " --devmode"
241	    return ""

244	def _is_sideloaded(item: SnapItem) -> bool:
245	    """Whether this snap's bytes came from a local `.snap` file rather than the store.
246	
247	    snapd assigns a store-less revision to a snap installed from a file (`snap install
248	    --dangerous ./foo.snap`, `snap try`) and `snap list` renders it with an `x` prefix —
249	    `x1`, `x2`, … — where a store revision is a plain integer. No store can serve an
250	    `x<N>` revision, so `snap install --revision=x1 <name>` can never succeed; and such a
251	    snap usually tracks no channel either, which makes the channel switch that follows
252	    meaningless too.
253	    """
254	    return item.revision.startswith("x")

257	def _partition_sideloaded(items: Sequence[SnapItem]) -> tuple[list[SnapItem], list[SnapItem]]:
258	    """Split a captured listing into (store-installed, sideloaded), preserving order."""
259	    store_items = [item for item in items if not _is_sideloaded(item)]
260	    sideloaded = [item for item in items if _is_sideloaded(item)]
261	    return store_items, sideloaded

287	    """Present on both with a different revision and/or channel (D-06: unlike apt
288	    package versions, D-04, both actively converge — never `REPORT_ONLY`). `detail`
289	    names revisions when the revision differs (the more consequential fact); otherwise
290	    it is a same-revision retrack and names channels instead.
291	    """

293	        detail = build_version_mismatch_detail(source_item.revision, target_item.revision, machines)
294	    else:
295	        detail = build_version_mismatch_detail(source_item.channel, target_item.channel, machines)

297	        item_class=ItemClass.SNAP,
298	        diff_class=DiffClass.VERSION_MISMATCH,

306	def _hold_diff(name: str, *, in_source: bool) -> ItemDiff:
307	    """One `snap:hold:<name>` membership diff (#208, D2, the snap analog of
308	    `AptHoldItem`): `in_source` (source-held, target-not) -> INSTALL (hold on target);
309	    otherwise (target-held, source-not) -> REMOVE (unhold on target). The identity
310	    (`snap:hold:<name>`) is DISTINCT from the snap item's (`snap:<name>`) so a snap and
311	    its hold are two separate review items.
312	    """
313	    return ItemDiff(
314	        item_class=ItemClass.SNAP_HOLD,
315	        diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET if in_source else DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
316	        action=DiffAction.INSTALL if in_source else DiffAction.REMOVE,
317	        item_id=f"{_SNAP_HOLD_ID_PREFIX}{name}",
318	        label=f"{name} (hold)",
319	        detail=None,
320	    )

323	def _diff_snap_holds(source_items: Sequence[SnapItem], target_items: Sequence[SnapItem]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
324	    """Per-snap hold membership diffs (#208, D2), emitted AFTER the presence diffs so
325	    install-before-hold ordering holds (`apply()` preserves diff order): source-held &
326	    not target-held -> INSTALL (hold); target-held & not source-held -> REMOVE (unhold);
327	    both-held or neither -> no diff.
328	
329	    Only snaps present on the SOURCE are considered — source is authoritative for hold
330	    intent (a hold on a snap the source no longer has is not the user's current intent).
331	    `sorted` for a stable, deterministic review order.
332	    """
333	    source_by_name = {item.name: item for item in source_items}
334	    target_held = {item.name for item in target_items if item.held}
335	
336	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
337	    for name in sorted(source_by_name):
338	        in_source = source_by_name[name].held
339	        in_target = name in target_held
340	        if in_source == in_target:
341	            continue
342	        diffs.append(_hold_diff(name, in_source=in_source))
343	    return diffs

346	def _diff_snap_items(
347	    source_items: Sequence[SnapItem], target_items: Sequence[SnapItem], machines: Machines
348	) -> list[ItemDiff]:
349	    """One diff per snap name present on either side, source-then-target order — same
350	    shape as `PackageSyncJob._diff_apt_packages`, but with D-06's own convergence rule.
351	    Per-snap hold membership diffs follow the presence diffs (D8: install-before-hold).
352	    """
353	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
354	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
355	
356	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
357	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
358	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
359	
360	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
361	    for item_id in seen:
362	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
363	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
364	
365	        if source_item is not None and target_item is None:
366	            diffs.append(_install_diff(source_item))
367	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
368	            diffs.append(_remove_diff(target_item))
369	        elif (
370	            source_item is not None
371	            and target_item is not None
372	            and (source_item.revision != target_item.revision or source_item.channel != target_item.channel)
373	        ):
374	            diffs.append(_change_diff(item_id, source_item, target_item, machines))
375	        # else: present on both, identical revision and channel -> no diff.
376	
377	    # Hold diffs AFTER presence diffs (D8) so a hold on a same-run install lands once the
378	    # snap is present.
379	    diffs.extend(_diff_snap_holds(source_items, target_items))
380	
381	    return diffs

384	def _current_revision_name(app_dir: Path) -> str | None:
385	    """The revision directory name `~/<app>/current` resolves to, or None when the
386	    symlink is missing or dangling.
387	
388	    snapd maintains `current` as a symlink to the active revision's directory. Resolving
389	    it (readlink, followed to the real dir) yields that revision's directory name so the
390	    caller can keep the matching data dir in the mirror (decision 3). A missing or dangling
391	    `current` — the active revision is then indeterminate — returns None, and the caller
392	    falls back to excluding every revision dir for that app (the safe default).
393	    """
394	    current = app_dir / "current"
395	    try:
396	        resolved = current.resolve(strict=True)
397	    except OSError:
398	        return None
399	    if not resolved.is_dir():
400	        return None
401	    return resolved.name

404	def snap_sync_exclude_paths() -> list[Path]:
405	    """Absolute `~/snap/<app>/<revision>` data directories folder_sync must NOT mirror,
406	    resolved against `Path.home()` at call time exactly like `vscode_state_exclude_paths()`
407	    — unlike VS Code's fixed relpath list, the revision set is dynamic, so it is enumerated
408	    from the filesystem rather than hardcoded.
409	
410	    Per app this excludes every revision dir EXCEPT the one the app's `current` symlink
411	    resolves to (decision 3, issue #118): snap_sync converges the target onto the source's
412	    revision before folder_sync runs (D-17 order), so by folder_sync time both machines'
413	    `current` points at the same revision, and mirroring THAT revision's data dir carries
414	    the active revision's per-user app data across. The retained older revision dirs stay
415	    excluded so folder_sync never plants data dirs for revisions the target's snapd never
416	    installed.
417	
418	    `~/snap/<app>/common` (revision-independent user data folder_sync must keep mirroring)
419	    and `~/snap/<app>/current` (the symlink itself) are always kept — the whole reason this
420	    export is not simply `~/snap`. When `current` is missing or dangling the active revision
421	    cannot be determined, so ALL of that app's revision dirs are excluded (safe default).
422	    """
423	    snap_root = Path.home() / "snap"
424	    if not snap_root.is_dir():
425	        return []
426	
427	    paths: list[Path] = []
428	    for app_dir in sorted(snap_root.iterdir()):
429	        if not app_dir.is_dir():
430	            continue
431	        current_revision = _current_revision_name(app_dir)
432	        for entry in sorted(app_dir.iterdir()):
433	            if entry.name in _NON_REVISION_DIR_NAMES or not entry.is_dir():
434	                continue
435	            if current_revision is not None and entry.name == current_revision:
436	                continue  # active-revision data dir travels with folder_sync (decision 3)
437	            paths.append(entry)
438	    return paths

441	class SnapSyncJob(PackageSyncJob):
442	    """Converge snap name/channel/revision after the coordinator's batched review.
443	
444	    Overrides `plan()` with a snap-specific capture -> diff -> review-group pipeline
445	    (module docstring explains why the inherited apt-package-shaped one cannot be
446	    reused); `accept_review()`, `apply()` and `execute()` are inherited unchanged.
447	    """
448	
449	    name: ClassVar[str] = "snap_sync"
450	    manager_id: ClassVar[str] = "snap"
451	
452	    # No configurable properties: mirrors AptSyncJob's empty schema — only the enable
453	    # flag in sync_jobs is needed for this slice.
454	    CONFIG_SCHEMA: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {
455	        "type": "object",
456	        "properties": {},
457	        "additionalProperties": False,
458	    }
459	
460	    def __init__(self, context: JobContext) -> None:
461	        super().__init__(context)
462	        # Populated by plan()'s own capture/query step (post filter_inert) and
463	        # consulted by converge(): the base pipeline only ever hands converge() an
464	        # ItemDiff, whose item_id ("snap:<name>") carries no revision/channel data of
465	        # its own — unlike an apt package name, `snap install --revision=N` needs the
466	        # literal N, which has to come from somewhere other than the diff itself.
467	        self._source_items_by_id: dict[str, SnapItem] = {}
468	        self._target_items_by_id: dict[str, SnapItem] = {}
469	
470	    async def capture_source_items(self) -> Sequence[SnapItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
471	        """`snap list --all` on the source (D-06).
472	
473	        This job overrides `plan()` and never routes through `PackageSyncJob.
474	        diff_items`'s apt-package-shaped dispatch (module docstring), so widening this
475	        hook's item type here is safe: no code holding a `PackageSyncJob`-typed
476	        reference ever calls it expecting an `AptPackageItem` back.
477	
478	        Guarded on the exit code (ADR-022). This is the read whose silence is worst: an
479	        empty source manifest offers every snap on the target for removal, and the only
480	        thing standing between that and a wiped target is that removal groups arrive
481	        unticked. Measured against the real `snap` binary — with snapd unreachable it exits
482	        1, and with snapd answering that zero snaps are installed it exits 0, writes "No
483	        snaps are installed yet." to STDERR and leaves stdout empty. So the exit code
484	        separates the two cleanly, and an empty stdout at exit 0 is a machine with no snaps,
485	        which is an ordinary machine.
486	        """
487	        command = "snap list --all"
488	        result = await self.source.run_command(command)
489	        require_answer(command, result, Host.SOURCE)
490	        return _parse_snap_list(result.stdout)
491	
492	    async def query_target_items(self) -> Sequence[SnapItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
493	        """The target's own `snap list --all` (same reasoning as `capture_source_items`)."""
494	        command = "snap list --all"
495	        result = await self.target.run_command(command, login_shell=False)
496	        require_answer(command, result, Host.TARGET)
497	        return _parse_snap_list(result.stdout)
498	
499	    @override
500	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
501	        """Load decision files -> capture -> query -> diff -> build review groups.
502	
503	        Read-only: only `snap list --all` (both machines) and a decision-file `cat`
504	        run here — no `snap install`/`refresh`/`switch`/`remove` before this returns.
505	        Caches the filtered source/target items by id for `converge()` (see
506	        `__init__`), since `ItemDiff.item_id` alone carries no revision/channel data.
507	
508	        Sideloaded source snaps are reported once and dropped from the diff input:
509	        reproducing them is not implemented (there is no mechanism to carry the `.snap`
510	        bytes to the target), so every diff they could produce — install, revision/channel
511	        change, and the `snap:hold:` diff `_diff_snap_holds` derives from a source snap —
512	        would be an item that can only fail at converge, every run. A warning states that
513	        once; no review item is emitted, since the user has no action to take on it.
514	        """
515	        source_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.source).load()
516	        target_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.target).load()
517	
518	        source_items = await filter_inert(await self.capture_source_items(), source_decisions)
519	        target_items = await filter_inert(await self.query_target_items(), target_decisions)
520	
521	        source_items, sideloaded = _partition_sideloaded(source_items)
522	        if sideloaded:
523	            self._log(
524	                Host.SOURCE,
525	                LogLevel.WARNING,
526	                "Skipping snap(s) installed from a local file: their revision exists in no store, so they "
527	                "cannot be reproduced on the target — "
528	                + ", ".join(f"{item.name} (revision {item.revision})" for item in sideloaded),
529	            )
530	            # The target's own entry for those names goes with them. Dropping only the
531	            # source side would leave the target's copy unmatched, and an unmatched target
532	            # snap is an EXTRA_ON_TARGET removal — turning "cannot reproduce this" into
533	            # "propose deleting it there". A sideloaded snap the source does NOT have stays
534	            # an ordinary removal candidate: its name is not in this set.
535	            withheld = {item.name for item in sideloaded}
536	            target_items = [item for item in target_items if item.name not in withheld]
537	
538	        self._source_items_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
539	        self._target_items_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
540	
541	        # `_drop_inert_diffs` after the diff, not `filter_inert` before it: a hold's
542	        # identity is `snap:hold:<name>`, which no `SnapItem` carries (its own id is
543	        # `snap:<name>`), so a recorded hold decision can only be matched on the ItemDiff.
544	        diffs = self._drop_inert_diffs(
545	            _diff_snap_items(source_items, target_items, self.machines), source_decisions, target_decisions
546	        )
547	        groups = self._build_review_groups(diffs)
548	        return PackagePlan(manager=self.manager_id, diffs=diffs, groups=groups)
549	
550	    @override
551	    async def converge(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
552	        """Install/refresh at the source's explicit revision, switch channel only when
553	        it differs, or remove (never purge) — the only D-06-safe verbs (module
554	        docstring). One snap per invocation (D-27) so a single bad snap cannot fail the
555	        whole batch.
556	
557	        Hold membership items (`snap:hold:<name>`) are routed FIRST, by item_id prefix
558	        (#208, D4), so a `snap:hold:` INSTALL runs `snap refresh --hold=forever` rather
559	        than a snap install, and a `snap:hold:` REMOVE (unhold) is never misread as a
560	        snap removal. This test MUST precede the action-based dispatch below, because
561	        `snap:hold:` also matches the plain `snap:` prefix.
562	        """
563	        if diff.item_id.startswith(_SNAP_HOLD_ID_PREFIX):
564	            return await self._converge_hold(diff)
565	
566	        if diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE:
567	            return await self._converge_remove(diff)
568	
569	        source_item = self._source_items_by_id.get(diff.item_id)
570	        if source_item is None:
571	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(
572	                f"no captured source snap for {diff.label} (item_id={diff.item_id!r}); "
573	                "was plan() run before converge()?"
574	            )
575	
576	        if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL:
577	            return await self._converge_install(source_item)
578	        if diff.action == DiffAction.CHANGE:
579	            target_item = self._target_items_by_id.get(diff.item_id)
580	            return await self._converge_change(source_item, target_item)
581	
582	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(f"SnapSyncJob.converge: unsupported action {diff.action.value!r} for {diff.label}")
583	
584	    async def _converge_install(self, source_item: SnapItem) -> CommandResult:
585	        """`snap install --revision=<N>` lands the exact revision without ever
586	        touching a hold (D-06); the channel switch always follows so the target
587	        tracks the same channel as the source. There is no cheap way to learn
588	        "snapd's default channel for a not-yet-installed snap" from `snap list --all`
589	        alone (only installed snaps appear in it), and re-running `switch` to a
590	        channel the install already landed on is a harmless no-op, so always
591	        switching is simpler and no less correct than conditioning on that unknown.
592	
593	        The SOURCE item's confinement flag is interpolated because snapd requires it as
594	        explicit per-revision confirmation: without `--classic`, installing a
595	        classic-confinement snap fails with "repeat the command including --classic" on
596	        every run, forever. `--revision=N` does NOT bypass that check — snapd's own
597	        wording is "This revision of snap %q was published using classic confinement".
598	        """
599	        name = shlex.quote(source_item.name)
600	        revision = shlex.quote(source_item.revision)
601	        install_result = await self.target.run_command(
602	            f"sudo snap install{_confinement_flags(source_item)} --revision={revision} {name}",
603	            login_shell=False,
604	            mutates=f"install snap {source_item.name} at revision {source_item.revision}",
605	        )
606	        if not install_result.success:
607	            return install_result
608	        return await self._switch_channel(source_item)
609	
610	    async def _converge_change(self, source_item: SnapItem, target_item: SnapItem | None) -> CommandResult:
611	        """`snap refresh --revision=<N>` when the revision differs, plus the channel
612	        switch when the channel also differs (or is the only thing that differs) —
613	        `converge()` only reaches here for a diff `_diff_snap_items` built because at
614	        least one of the two was true.
615	
616	        The refresh carries the SOURCE item's confinement flag for the same reason the
617	        install does. `snap refresh --help` says a plain refresh preserves the snap's
618	        existing confinement options, but that describes the TARGET's current confinement,
619	        which is the wrong one whenever the two hosts disagree: source classic + target
620	        strict is a real case (a snap that changed confinement between the two installed

37	class ProbeFailed(RuntimeError):
38	    """A package-manager READ this run's correctness depends on did not answer at all.
39	
40	    Deliberately NOT a `ConvergeItemFailed`. That type means "what we asked for is wrong",
41	    which is under our control, belongs to one item, and lets the run continue (ADR-020
42	    D-27). This one means the tool or the machine is broken — a transient network failure,
43	    a package-manager lock, an interrupted dpkg, a daemon that is not running — which no
44	    item's own state explains. It escapes the per-item loops on purpose, so the run fails
45	    ONCE naming the command that failed rather than N times naming N items.
46	
47	    One type across all four package jobs, because the caller that must react to it is the
48	    orchestrator, which has no reason to care which manager's read went dark.
49	    """

51	
52	def require_answer(
53	    command: str,
54	    result: CommandResult,
55	    host: Host,
56	    *,
57	    answers: int | None = None,
58	    answer_noun: str = "answer",
59	) -> None:
60	    """Refuse to read a probe's silence as an answer about the things it was asked about.
61	
62	    Raises `ProbeFailed` on a NON-ZERO EXIT, and — only when the caller passes `answers` —
63	    on `answers == 0`. `answers` is the number of parsed answers the caller KNOWS was owed;
64	    pass it only where at least one answer is genuinely guaranteed, never as a blanket
65	    "output was empty" check, because for most of these commands an empty answer is a
66	    legitimate state of the machine.
67	
68	    The `answers` half is a JUDGEMENT, recorded as one: a probe that answered "I know none
69	    of these" and a probe that died both print nothing, and the output alone cannot
70	    separate them. It is resolved toward failing fast because the alternative misattributes
71	    an environment failure to every item, and because a set the tool knows nothing about is
72	    a set nothing could be done with anyway. A per-name absence INSIDE an answered probe is
73	    left alone: that is the tool saying it does not know that one name, which is evidence
74	    about that one request.
75	    """
76	    if result.success and answers != 0:
77	        return
78	    condition = (
79	        f"exited {result.exit_code}"
80	        if not result.success
81	        else f"exited 0 but printed no {answer_noun}, so its output is not an answer"
82	    )
83	    detail = f": {result.stderr.strip()}" if result.stderr.strip() else ""
